title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄序
國朝求賢於天下三歲一大比而
賓興之
京師天下之本而直隸州郡皆畿
甸也乃合諸生及太學之士試
之順天府其考校也必
詔詞臣主之其命題也必經
===
進而後頒其取士之數則視諸大
藩加十五重之也成化十三年
秋適維其期挟藝就試者二千
五百人雲集
闕下前此未有也府丞臣英以考
試官請於是洗馬臣環侍講臣
教承
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄序

國朝求賢於天下，三歲一大比而賓興之。京師，天下之本，而直隸州郡皆畿甸也。乃合諸生及太學之士，試之順天府。其考校也，必詔詞臣主之；其命題也，必經進而後頒；其取士之數，則視諸大藩加十五，重之也。成化十三年秋，適維其期，挟藝就試者二千五百人，雲集闕下，前此未有也。府丞臣英以考試官請，於是洗馬臣環、侍講臣教承
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

Our dynasty seeks worthy men throughout the realm, holding a great examination every three years and honoring those selected as guests before advancing them. The capital is the foundation of the realm, and the directly administered subprefectures and prefectures all belong to the metropolitan domain. Accordingly, students of the local government schools and the Imperial University are assembled to sit the examination at Shuntian Prefecture. For the assessment of their work, literary officials are invariably appointed by imperial decree to preside. Examination questions must be submitted for imperial review before being issued. The quota of men selected exceeds that of the major provinces by fifteen, reflecting the importance accorded to this examination.

In the autumn of the thirteenth year of Chenghua [1477], the appointed time came round. Two thousand five hundred men came to demonstrate their literary skills in the examination, gathering like clouds beneath the palace gates—a number without precedent. Your servant Ying, Vice Prefect, requested the appointment of Examiners. Thereupon your servants Huan, Librarian, and Jiao, Expositor-in-waiting, received …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
上命涖其事翌日
陛辭入院時同考官學正臣澄教
諭臣尚彜臣澄臣璧臣富訓導臣
岳臣存臣境監試官御史臣進
臣仁而提調則臣英也洎諸執
事咸集相與戒誓務精白一心
恪共乃事以仰副
===
朝廷委任之盛意闈棘三試之得
士百三十五人錄其名氏及文
之優者以
獻臣謹敘諸首竊惟政化與氣運
相為流通而賢才係焉政化盛
則氣運盛氣運盛則賢才亦從
而盛唐虞之際萬邦黎獻共惟
punctuated:
上命涖其事。翌日，陛辭入院。時同考官學正臣澄，教諭臣尚彜、臣澄、臣璧、臣富，訓導臣岳、臣存、臣境，監試官御史臣進、臣仁，而提調則臣英也。洎諸執事咸集，相與戒誓，務精白一心，恪共乃事，以仰副朝廷委任之盛意。闈棘三試之，得士百三十五人，錄其名氏及文之優者以獻。臣謹敘諸首。
竊惟政化與氣運相為流通，而賢才係焉。政化盛則氣運盛，氣運盛則賢才亦從而盛。唐虞之際，萬邦黎獻共惟
translation_en:
… received His Majesty’s command to oversee the examination. The following day, we took leave of His Majesty and entered the examination compound. The Associate Examiners were your servant Cheng, a school instructor; your servants Shangyi, Cheng, Bi, and Fu, instructors; and your servants Yue, Cun, and Jing, assistant instructors. The Examination Monitors were your servants Jin and Ren, investigating censors, while your servant Ying served as Proctor. Once all the functionaries had assembled, we solemnly admonished one another and pledged to act with purity and single-minded dedication, respectfully discharging our duties so as to fulfill the court’s generous intentions in entrusting us with this responsibility. Within the examination compound, we examined the candidates in three sessions and selected 135 men. We recorded their names and the best of their compositions for presentation to His Majesty. Your servant respectfully places this preface at the beginning.
I humbly consider that government’s transforming influence and the movements of cosmic forces flow into one another, and that worthy talent is bound up with them. When government’s transforming influence flourishes, cosmic forces likewise flourish; when cosmic forces flourish, worthy talent flourishes in their wake. In the age of Tang and Yu, the many worthy men of the myriad states all were …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
帝臣而周之藹藹吉士必於土
宇孔厚之日見之故其生也有
自来其出也有所為又將以資
國家之用隆太平之業而氣化
愈久而愈盛矣我
朝自
太祖高皇帝光啟文明之運
===
列聖相承至于
皇上重熈累洽百有餘年氣化益隆
賢才彙進熈
帝載而賛
皇猷者濟濟其盛矧京畿故燕趙之
地號多豪傑今四方萬國環視
內向衣冠禮樂聲明文物之華
punctuated:
帝臣，而周之藹藹吉士，必於土宇孔厚之日見之。故其生也有自来，其出也有所為，又將以資國家之用，隆太平之業，而氣化愈久而愈盛矣。
我朝自太祖高皇帝光啟文明之運，列聖相承，至于皇上，重熈累洽百有餘年，氣化益隆，賢才彙進，熈帝載而賛皇猷者，濟濟其盛。矧京畿，故燕趙之地，號多豪傑。今四方萬國環視內向，衣冠禮樂、聲明文物之華，
translation_en:
… ministers to the sovereign; and Zhou’s abundant worthy men were surely to be seen in the days when its territory was vast. Thus, their birth had its source, and their emergence into public service had its purpose. They would moreover serve the needs of the state and advance the enterprise of Great Peace, so that the transforming cosmic forces would grow ever more flourishing with time.
In our dynasty, since Emperor Taizu Gao gloriously inaugurated an era of enlightened culture, successive sage sovereigns have followed one another down to His Majesty. Splendor and harmonious rule have accumulated for more than a hundred years; the transforming cosmic forces have become ever more abundant, and worthy talent has advanced in great numbers. Those who bring glory to imperial undertakings and assist imperial plans are plentiful indeed. How much more so in the capital region, the former lands of Yan and Zhao, renowned for their many outstanding men! Now the myriad states of the four quarters look toward the center and turn their allegiance inward; the splendor of ceremonial dress, rites and music, illustrious institutions, and cultural accomplishments …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
於是乎萃而瑰瑋卓絕之才揚
芳振烈相望後先諸士子生長
於斯觀光於斯得於漸摩涵育
之最先者能不顒顒而起乎詩
曰思皇多士生此王國王國克
生惟周之楨際
聖明之時預賢良之薦先天下之士
===
貢之
天子之庭何其幸歟行當捷春闈奉
大對而駸駸嚮用矣必思有以自
振上忠于
君而澤下加于民樹勳業于時佐
盛治於無窮庶幾爲
國之楨而趾美乎前修將天下後
punctuated: 於是乎萃，而瑰瑋卓絕之才，揚芳振烈，相望後先。諸士子生長於斯，觀光於斯，得於漸摩涵育之最先者，能不顒顒而起乎？詩曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，惟周之楨。」際聖明之時，預賢良之薦，先天下之士，貢之天子之庭，何其幸歟！行當捷春闈，奉大對，而駸駸嚮用矣。必思有以自振，上忠于君，而澤下加于民，樹勳業于時，佐盛治於無窮，庶幾爲國之楨，而趾美乎前修。將天下後
translation_en: …gather here, while men of extraordinary and surpassing talent spread their good names and display their illustrious achievements, following one another in succession. You scholars have grown up here and beheld the splendor of the realm here; you have been foremost in receiving its gradual refinement and nurturing influence. How could you fail to rise eagerly to the occasion? The Book of Odes says: “Illustrious are the many worthy men born in this royal kingdom. The royal kingdom can bring them forth: they are the pillars of Zhou.” To live in an age of sagely enlightenment, to be included among those recommended for worth and ability, and to be presented at the Son of Heaven’s court ahead of the scholars of the realm—how fortunate you are! Soon you should succeed in the spring Metropolitan Examination, submit your answers at the Palace Examination, and advance steadily toward employment in office. You must consider how to rouse yourselves: be loyal to your sovereign above and extend benefits to the people below, establish meritorious achievements in your age, and help sustain flourishing government without end. Thus you may become pillars of the state and carry forward the excellence of your worthy predecessors. Then, throughout the realm and in later ages, …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
世稱之曰邦畿之士也顧不偉
歟其毋庸庸無爲碌碌無聞自
負自棄於
明朝俾時之人多前修而不之齒
也
司經局洗馬鄭環謹序
punctuated:
世稱之曰：「邦畿之士也。」顧不偉歟？其毋庸庸無爲，碌碌無聞，自負自棄於明朝，俾時之人多前修而不之齒也。

司經局洗馬鄭環謹序。
translation_en:
… generations will praise them, saying, “These are scholars of the capital region.” Would this not be magnificent? Let them not remain mediocre and inactive, undistinguished and unknown, betraying and abandoning themselves under this enlightened dynasty, so that their contemporaries esteem their worthy predecessors but do not count them among their ranks.

Preface respectfully written by Zheng Huan, Librarian in the Classics Office.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
立則見其參於前也在輿則見其倚於衡
也
夫微之顯誠之不可揜如此夫
堯以不得舜為己憂舜以不得禹皐陶為
己憂夫以百畝之不易為己憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠教人以善謂之忠
為天下得人者謂之仁
===
易
泰小往大来吉亨彖曰泰小往大来吉亨
則是天地交而萬物通也上下交而其
志同也内陽而外陰内健而外順内君
子而外小人君子道長小人道消也
无所往其来復吉有攸往夙吉
富有之謂大業日新之謂盛德生生之謂
易
河出圖洛出書聖人則之
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

立則見其參於前也，在輿則見其倚於衡也。

夫微之顯，誠之不可揜，如此夫！

堯以不得舜為己憂，舜以不得禹、皐陶為己憂。夫以百畝之不易為己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠，為天下得人者謂之仁。

易

泰，小往大来，吉亨。彖曰：「泰，小往大来，吉亨」，則是天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。内陽而外陰，内健而外順，内君子而外小人，君子道長，小人道消也。

无所往，其来復吉；有攸往，夙吉。

富有之謂大業，日新之謂盛德，生生之謂易。

河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

When standing, see it present before you; when riding in a carriage, see it resting against the crossbar.

How the hidden becomes manifest! Such is the impossibility of concealing sincerity!

Yao regarded failing to obtain Shun as his own concern; Shun regarded failing to obtain Yu and Gao Yao as his own concern. A man whose concern is that his hundred mu of land remain uncultivated is a farmer. Sharing one's wealth with others is called beneficence; teaching others goodness is called loyalty; obtaining worthy men for All under Heaven is called benevolence.

Book of Changes

Tai (Peace): the small departs and the great arrives. Auspicious; success. The Commentary on the Judgment says: “Tai: the small departs and the great arrives. Auspicious; success.” This means that Heaven and Earth interact and the myriad things flourish; those above and those below interact and share the same purpose. Yang is within and yin without; strength is within and compliance without; the noble man is within and the petty man without. The way of the noble man advances, while the way of the petty man declines.

If there is nowhere to go, returning is auspicious. If there is somewhere to go, going early is auspicious.

Abundant possession is called a great undertaking; daily renewal is called flourishing virtue; generation upon generation is called change.

The Yellow River brought forth the Chart, and the Luo River brought forth the Writing; the sages took them as models.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
書
夙夜惟寅直哉惟清
任官惟賢才左右惟其人臣為上為德為
下為民其難其慎惟和惟一
伻來毖殷乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣曰明禋
拜手稽首休享
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
===
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼既同上入執宫功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播
百穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌
陰四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭九月肅霜十
月滌場朋酒斯饗曰殺羔羊躋彼公堂
稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
我田既臧農夫之慶
豈弟君子民之父母
猗與那與置我鞉鼓奏鼓簡簡衎我烈祖
punctuated:
書

夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。

任官惟賢才，左右惟其人。臣為上為德，為下為民。其難其慎，惟和惟一。

伻來毖殷，乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣，曰明禋。拜手稽首，休享。

六卿分職，各率其屬，以倡九牧，阜成兆民。

詩

九月築場圃，十月納禾稼。黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫，我稼既同，上入執宫功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。九月肅霜，十月滌場。朋酒斯饗，曰殺羔羊。躋彼公堂，稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆！

我田既臧，農夫之慶。

豈弟君子，民之父母。

猗與那與！置我鞉鼓。奏鼓簡簡，衎我烈祖。
translation_en:
Book of Documents

Be reverent morning and night; be upright and pure.

Appoint only the worthy and talented to office; place only suitable men at your side. A minister serves his ruler above by cultivating virtue, and those below by caring for the people. Treat this as a difficult charge and exercise caution; maintain harmony and singleness of purpose.

A messenger was sent to admonish the people of Yin; orders were then given to reassure me with two vessels of fragrant black-millet wine, saying that these were for a pure sacrifice. Bowing with hands joined and head to the ground, I presented the auspicious offering.

The six ministers have distinct responsibilities. Each leads his subordinates, setting an example for the nine regional governors, to enrich and perfect the lives of the myriad people.

Book of Odes

In the ninth month we prepare the threshing grounds in the gardens; in the tenth month we bring in the crops: millet of both kinds, late- and early-ripening grain, grain and hemp, beans and wheat. Ah, we farmers! Once our crops are gathered, we go up to undertake work on the lord’s buildings. By day you gather thatch; by night you twist ropes. Quickly attend to the roofs, for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains. In the days of the second month, we cut the ice with ringing blows; in the days of the third month, we store it in the icehouse. Early in the fourth month, we offer a lamb and sacrifice with leeks. In the ninth month the frost is severe; in the tenth month we sweep the threshing grounds. Two jars of wine are set out for the feast, and lambs are slaughtered. We ascend the lord’s hall and raise the rhinoceros-horn cup: may he live ten thousand years, without end!

Our fields have yielded well: this is the farmers’ joy.

The gracious and amiable noble man is the father and mother of the people.

Ah, how splendid, how abundant! Set out our hand drums and great drums. The drums sound deep and strong, bringing joy to our illustrious ancestor. …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
湯孫奏假綏我思成鞉鼓淵淵嘒嘒管
聲既和且平依我磬聲於赫湯孫穆穆
厥聲庸鼓有斁萬舞有奕我有嘉客亦
不夷懌自古在昔先民有作温恭朝夕
執事有恪顧予烝嘗湯孫之將
春秋
天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵隱公元年
翬帥師會宋公陳侯蔡人衞人伐鄭四
年王人子突救衞莊公六年季子來歸閔
===
公元年
齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏莊公
十三年
晋侯入曹執曹伯畀宋人　晋侯齊師宋
師秦師及楚人戰于城濮楚師敗績
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衞子莒
子盟于踐土並僖公二十八年
楚公子貞伐鄭襄公八年公會晋侯宋公
衞侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯
punctuated:
湯孫奏假，綏我思成。鞉鼓淵淵，嘒嘒管聲，既和且平，依我磬聲。於赫湯孫，穆穆厥聲！庸鼓有斁，萬舞有奕。我有嘉客，亦不夷懌？自古在昔，先民有作：温恭朝夕，執事有恪。顧予烝嘗，湯孫之將。

《春秋》
天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵。隱公元年。
翬帥師會宋公、陳侯、蔡人、衞人伐鄭。四年。
王人子突救衞。莊公六年。
季子來歸。閔公元年。
齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏。莊公十三年。
晋侯入曹，執曹伯，畀宋人。晋侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績。公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衞子、莒子盟于踐土。並僖公二十八年。
楚公子貞伐鄭。襄公八年。
公會晋侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯
translation_en:
…Tang’s descendant comes forward to present his offerings, seeking peace and the fulfillment of our thoughts. The hand drums and drums resound deeply; the pipes sound clear and high, harmonious and balanced, following the sound of our stone chimes. Ah, glorious is Tang’s descendant; solemn is his music! The great bells and drums ring out abundantly; the wan dance is splendid. We have honored guests: are they not pleased and delighted? From ancient times, our forebears established this practice: gentle and reverent morning and evening, respectful in performing their duties. Look with favor upon our winter and autumn sacrifices, the offerings presented by Tang’s descendant.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Heavenly King sent Steward Xuan to bring funerary gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi. First year of Duke Yin.

Hui led an army to join the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and men of Cai and Wei in attacking Zheng. Fourth year of Duke Yin.

Zitu, an officer of the king, came to the aid of Wei. Sixth year of Duke Zhuang.

Jizi returned. First year of Duke Min.

The Marquis of Qi and men of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu met at Beixing. Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.

The Marquis of Jin entered Cao, seized the Earl of Cao, and handed him over to the men of Song. The Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought the men of Chu at Chengpu; the Chu army suffered a crushing defeat. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju in making a covenant at Jiantu. All three entries are from the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.

Prince Zhen of Chu attacked Zheng. Eighth year of Duke Xiang.

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, and the Earl of Qi…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
小邾齊世子光伐鄭同盟于戲〔九年〕公
會晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世
子光滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭戌鄭
虎牢楚公子貞救鄭〔十年〕公會晋侯宋
公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭同盟于亳城北
公會晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會
于蕭魚〔十一年〕
===
禮記
天子七廟諸侯五大夫三士一天子之豆
二十有六諸公十有六諸侯十有二上
大夫八下大夫六
少事長賤事貴共帥時
是故君子無物而不在禮矣
子民如父母有憯怛之愛有忠利之教親
而尊安而敬威而愛富而有禮惠而能
散
punctuated:
小邾、齊世子光伐鄭，同盟于戲〔九年〕。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，戌鄭虎牢。楚公子貞救鄭〔十年〕。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，同盟于亳城北。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚〔十一年〕。

禮記

天子七廟，諸侯五，大夫三，士一。天子之豆二十有六，諸公十有六，諸侯十有二，上大夫八，下大夫六。

少事長，賤事貴，共帥時。

是故君子無物而不在禮矣。

子民如父母，有憯怛之愛，有忠利之教，親而尊，安而敬，威而愛，富而有禮，惠而能散。
translation_en:
…the ruler of Xiao Zhu and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, attacked Zheng and jointly swore a covenant at Xi. 〔Ninth year.〕 The duke joined the marquis of Jin, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earl of Cao, the viscounts of Ju and Zhu, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the viscount of Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, and the viscount of Xiao Zhu in attacking Zheng. They garrisoned Hulao in Zheng [?]. Prince Zhen of Chu came to Zheng’s aid. 〔Tenth year.〕 The duke joined the marquis of Jin, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, and the viscount of Xiao Zhu in attacking Zheng. They jointly swore a covenant north of Bocheng. The duke joined the marquis of Jin, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, and the viscount of Xiao Zhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu. 〔Eleventh year.〕

Book of Rites (Liji)

The Son of Heaven has seven ancestral temples; the feudal lords have five, great officers three, and gentlemen one. The Son of Heaven has twenty-six ritual food stands; dukes have sixteen, other feudal lords twelve, senior great officers eight, and junior great officers six.

The young serve their elders, and those of low station serve those of high station: all alike follow this rule.

Thus, for the gentleman, nothing falls outside ritual propriety.

Cherish the people as your children, as their father and mother would: love them with tender concern and instruct them with wholehearted devotion to their welfare. Be close to them yet maintain dignity; put them at ease yet command respect; inspire awe yet show love; possess wealth yet observe ritual propriety; be generous and able to distribute your resources.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第貳場
論
聖人太極之全體
詔誥表内科一道
擬漢遣太中大夫巡行天下詔
擬唐以李靖為定襄道揔管誥
擬
詔加崇闕里釋奠禮樂衍聖公謝表
判語五條
===
濫設官吏
從征違期
私鑄銅錢
詐為瑞應
斷罪不當
第三場
策
問蓋甞伏觀我
太祖高皇帝之聖文矣神授心得體裁敻異皆
punctuated:
第貳場
論：聖人太極之全體。

擬漢遣太中大夫巡行天下詔。
擬唐以李靖為定襄道揔管誥。

第三場
策：
問：蓋甞伏觀我太祖高皇帝之聖文矣，神授心得，體裁敻異，皆…
translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse: The sage embodies the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.

One composition in the categories of edict, proclamation, or memorial [?]:
Draft an edict in the voice of a Han emperor dispatching Grand Masters of the Palace to tour the realm.
Draft a proclamation in the voice of a Tang emperor appointing Li Jing Commander-in-Chief of the Dingxiang Route.
Draft a memorial of thanks from the Duke for Perpetuating the Sage for an imperial edict enhancing the rites and music of the sacrificial offering ceremony at Queli.

Five legal judgments:
Indiscriminately establishing official posts and appointing clerks.
Failing to meet the appointed deadline when accompanying a military expedition.
Privately casting copper coins.
Fabricating auspicious portents.
Improper adjudication of offenses.

Third Session

Policy Question:
I have reverently perused the sagely writings of our Emperor Taizu Gao. Divinely inspired and apprehended in his own mind, they are distinguished in form and style, and all…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
對時宜物先幾前用而又妙探本原識
達遠大如
三誥之論治大祀文之論理大哉
王言非秦漢以下帝王名能文學者所能及
也昔有以馬上得天下者而三侯之章
論者亦以為壯麗雄偉近古未有若汾
上之辭橫槊之賦貞觀開元之製作則
皆成於少習與學士大夫爭長者然究
觀規摸考論旨歸盖亦少貶矣是則所
===
謂文者豈無與於學歟昔人有謂帝王
之學與常人不同者豈或以此歟而又
有以為帝王之學與常人同者其說安
在夫仰瞻
聖祖之製而評隲近代諸君猶日月之於衆星
可覩也請敬陳之
問太極西銘相傳為理學之宗然或有謂
太極之傳出於种放無極之論近於老
氏西銘有平施而無稱物流於兼愛其
punctuated:
對時宜物，先幾前用，而又妙探本原，識達遠大。如《三誥》之論治，《大祀文》之論理，大哉王言！非秦漢以下帝王名能文學者所能及也。昔有以馬上得天下者，而《三侯》之章，論者亦以為壯麗雄偉，近古未有。若汾上之辭、橫槊之賦、貞觀開元之製作，則皆成於少習，與學士大夫爭長者。然究觀規摸，考論旨歸，盖亦少貶矣。是則所謂文者，豈無與於學歟？昔人有謂帝王之學與常人不同者，豈或以此歟？而又有以為帝王之學與常人同者，其說安在？夫仰瞻聖祖之製，而評隲近代諸君，猶日月之於衆星，可覩也。請敬陳之。
問：太極、西銘，相傳為理學之宗。然或有謂太極之傳出於种放，無極之論近於老氏；西銘有平施而無稱物，流於兼愛。其
translation_en:
…responding to the times and fitting the circumstances of things, anticipating the first signs of change and providing for needs before they arise, while also penetrating underlying principles with subtle insight and displaying profound and far-reaching understanding. Consider the discussion of governance in the Three Admonitions and of principle in the Text of the Great Sacrifice: how great are these royal words! They are beyond the reach of those emperors from the Qin and Han onward who were renowned for literary accomplishment. There was once a ruler who won the realm on horseback; critics nevertheless judged his composition, the “Three Marquises” [?], magnificent and majestic, without precedent in recent antiquity. As for the verses composed on the Fen River, the rhapsody declaimed with spear held crosswise, and the compositions of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, these all resulted from practice begun in youth, through which their authors competed for preeminence with scholarly officials. Yet, upon closely examining their scope and design and considering their ultimate purport, one must surely rank them somewhat lower. Does this mean that what we call literary composition is hardly unrelated to learning? Some men of former times said that the learning of emperors differs from that of ordinary people: might this have been their reason? Others, however, have held that the learning of emperors is the same as that of ordinary people. On what grounds does their argument rest? When we reverently contemplate the compositions of the Sagely Progenitor and assess the rulers of more recent ages, the difference is as plain to see as that between the sun and moon and the multitude of stars. Please respectfully set forth your views.
Question: The Supreme Ultimate and the Western Inscription have traditionally been regarded as foundational texts of the Learning of Principle. Some, however, say that the transmission of the Supreme Ultimate originated with Chong Fang, and that its discussion of the Ultimateless approaches the teachings of Laozi; and that the Western Inscription advocates dispensing equally without weighing the particular nature of things, thereby lapsing into indiscriminate love. Their…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
說亦有所見歟而又有稱其首尾相因
脉絡貫通理一分殊名虛理實者說者
謂數語足以盡二書之旨諸生苟以為
然幸為我一二言之
問書曰汝則有大疑謀及卿士謀及庶人
古之人舉事興為未有不詢之下者然
甲可乙否言人人殊將以為可用而用
之不可用而舍之矣然固有因而成功
亦有因而僨事者是則吾何適從試舉
===
古人一二事與諸士子論之撓楚之計
則借筯之籌不同於豎儒之說馬邑之
役則老將之見不附於習胡事者之謀
曹魏之下江陵有畫策拒之者矣彼長
江共之之言何見晋武之議平吳有上
表請之者矣彼以秦凉為憂者何謂苻
堅决投鞭斷流之策而太極之議審不
謂其然宋文銳席卷趙魏之志而歩兵
之諫甞不以為可高麗之伐大臣勸之
punctuated:
說亦有所見歟？而又有稱其首尾相因，脉絡貫通，理一分殊，名虛理實者。說者謂數語足以盡二書之旨。諸生苟以為然，幸為我一二言之。

問：書曰：「汝則有大疑，謀及卿士，謀及庶人。」古之人舉事興為，未有不詢之下者。然甲可乙否，言人人殊，將以為可用而用之，不可用而舍之矣。然固有因而成功，亦有因而僨事者，是則吾何適從？試舉古人一二事，與諸士子論之。撓楚之計，則借筯之籌不同於豎儒之說；馬邑之役，則老將之見不附於習胡事者之謀。曹魏之下江陵，有畫策拒之者矣，彼「長江共之」之言何見？晋武之議平吳，有上表請之者矣，彼以秦凉為憂者何謂？苻堅决投鞭斷流之策，而太極之議審不謂其然；宋文銳席卷趙魏之志，而歩兵之諫甞不以為可。高麗之伐，大臣勸之。
translation_en:
…does this argument, too, contain some insight? Yet others praise the way their beginnings and endings support one another and their underlying threads run throughout, saying that “principle is one, but its particular manifestations differ,” and that “the designation is abstract, but the principle is real.” Commentators say that these few phrases suffice to exhaust the purport of the two works. If you students agree, please explain this briefly for me.

Question: The Book of Documents says: “When you have a grave doubt, consult your high ministers and officers, and consult the common people.” In undertaking any enterprise, the ancients invariably consulted those below them. Yet one person approves and another objects; everyone offers a different opinion. Presumably, one adopts advice judged usable and discards advice judged unusable. Nevertheless, following advice has sometimes brought success and sometimes ruined an undertaking. Whom, then, should we follow? Let me raise a few instances from antiquity for discussion with you candidates.

In planning to thwart Chu, the strategy explained with borrowed chopsticks differed from the proposal of the contemptible scholar. In the campaign at Mayi, the veteran general’s opinion did not accord with the plan of the man familiar with affairs among the Hu. When Cao Wei advanced on Jiangling, someone devised a strategy to resist it; what insight lay behind the remark that “the Yangtze is shared by both sides”? When Emperor Wu of Jin deliberated on conquering Wu, someone submitted a memorial requesting the campaign; what did those who expressed concern about Qin and Liang mean? Fu Jian resolved upon the strategy of “throwing whips into the river to stop its flow,” yet the deliberations in the Taiji Hall decidedly did not endorse it. Emperor Wen of the Song was intent on sweeping through Zhao and Wei, yet the remonstrance of the Commandant of Infantry had judged this inadvisable. As for the invasion of Gaoli, the high ministers urged it…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也然不有萬一蹉跌傷威損望之言乎
清水之盟廷臣主之也然不有戎狄豺
狼非盟可結之論乎淮西之討四年不
克宰相有罷兵之請矣而誓不與賊俱
生者何壯歟澶淵之報一夕五至左右
有南幸之謀矣而勸帝親征者何决歟
夫事之成敗未易定也寧無精識遠見
早辨而預言之者在聽而用之何如耳
聽之不審用之不當鮮不以佞為忠以
===
直為謗而欲事之不敗不可得也孟子
曰我知言知之必有道矣其明言之以
觀通博之學
問治莫近於州縣之官教莫先於學校之
職夫人能知之今之君子蓋嘗留意矣
異時為長民者類取之監學其後也病
其迫遲暮而久沉困於是以進士之選
充州縣之正所以重之也而說者謂漸
輕之勢已有見于今異時為師儒者或
punctuated:
也，然不有萬一蹉跌、傷威損望之言乎？清水之盟，廷臣主之也，然不有戎狄豺狼、非盟可結之論乎？淮西之討，四年不克，宰相有罷兵之請矣，而誓不與賊俱生者何壯歟！澶淵之報，一夕五至，左右有南幸之謀矣，而勸帝親征者何决歟！夫事之成敗，未易定也，寧無精識遠見、早辨而預言之者？在聽而用之何如耳。聽之不審，用之不當，鮮不以佞為忠、以直為謗，而欲事之不敗，不可得也。孟子曰：「我知言。」知之必有道矣，其明言之，以觀通博之學。
問：治莫近於州縣之官，教莫先於學校之職，夫人能知之，今之君子蓋嘗留意矣。異時為長民者，類取之監學；其後也，病其迫遲暮而久沉困，於是以進士之選充州縣之正，所以重之也。而說者謂漸輕之勢，已有見于今。異時為師儒者，或
translation_en:
…yet was there not a warning that, should a setback occur, it would impair imperial prestige and diminish esteem? Court officials supported the covenant at Qingshui; yet was there not an argument that the Rong and Di were like jackals and wolves and could not be bound by a covenant? When the campaign against Huaixi had failed to secure victory after four years, the chief councilors requested that the troops be withdrawn. Yet how resolute was the man who swore that he would not live under the same heaven as the rebels! When reports from Chanyuan arrived five times in a single night, the emperor’s attendants proposed an imperial journey south. Yet how decisive was the man who urged the emperor to lead the campaign in person! The success or failure of an undertaking is not easy to determine beforehand. Surely there are people of penetrating judgment and foresight who discern the outcome early and predict it? All depends on how their advice is heard and put into practice. If one does not examine it carefully or act upon it appropriately, one will almost inevitably mistake flattery for loyalty and forthrightness for slander; to expect an undertaking not to fail under such circumstances is impossible. Mencius said, “I understand words.” There must be a way to attain such understanding. Explain it clearly, so that we may assess the breadth and depth of your learning.
Question: In government, no officials are closer to the people than those of the departments and counties; in education, no posts take precedence over those in the schools. Everyone can understand this, and gentlemen of the present day have surely given it their attention. Formerly, those appointed to govern the people were generally drawn from students of the Imperial University. Subsequently, concern arose that they were approaching old age and had long languished in straitened circumstances. Men selected from among metropolitan graduates (jinshi) were therefore appointed as department and county heads, the intention being to enhance the importance of these offices. Yet commentators say that signs of their gradual loss of standing are already apparent today. Formerly, those serving as Confucian teachers were sometimes…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
參以薦舉其後也苦其召奔競而積猥
冗於是杜辟薦之門開監學之選所以
矯之也而說者謂不職之弊殆有甚於
彼考黜嵗行所以懲也而說者謂適以
趣其無賴之心召用踵接所以勸也而
說者謂適以長其恣肆之念以貢舉之
有無為殿最而說者謂未必其功罪專
文藝之高下為考課而說者謂非所以
為賢否夫致法以造功先王所不廢而
===
以流品用人漢唐以来固用之矣績效
之著當時仁賢之名後世不亦有聞者
乎今何以使人用而皆當法立而無弊
諸生多出於學校而升自州縣若此者
可以言歟
問中國之有夷狄猶陽之有陰人類之有
禽獸不能以無也而北虜為患常甚然
嘗觀於漢事高帝百戰之餘威加海内
而平城之憂至其後世猶不能忘孝武
punctuated:
參以薦舉。其後也，苦其召奔競而積猥冗，於是杜辟薦之門，開監學之選，所以矯之也。而說者謂不職之弊，殆有甚於彼。考黜嵗行，所以懲也，而說者謂適以趣其無賴之心；召用踵接，所以勸也，而說者謂適以長其恣肆之念。以貢舉之有無為殿最，而說者謂未必其功罪；專文藝之高下為考課，而說者謂非所以為賢否。夫致法以造功，先王所不廢，而以流品用人，漢唐以来固用之矣。績效之著當時、仁賢之名後世，不亦有聞者乎？今何以使人用而皆當，法立而無弊？諸生多出於學校，而升自州縣，若此者可以言歟？

問：中國之有夷狄，猶陽之有陰、人類之有禽獸，不能以無也。而北虜為患常甚。然嘗觀於漢事，高帝百戰之餘，威加海内，而平城之憂，至其後世猶不能忘。孝武
translation_en:
…some were also selected through recommendation. Later, troubled that this encouraged competition for advancement and accumulated an excessive number of superfluous personnel, the authorities closed the door to recruitment by invitation and recommendation and opened selection to students of the Imperial University. This was intended to correct the problem. Yet commentators say that the resulting failure to discharge official duties is perhaps even worse than before. Annual evaluations and dismissals are intended to deter misconduct, yet commentators say that they merely encourage a shameless disposition. Appointments in continual succession are intended to encourage good service, yet commentators say that they merely foster unrestrained behavior. Whether or not an instructor produces candidates for the examinations determines his rating as inferior or superior, yet commentators say that this does not necessarily reflect his merit or fault. Performance evaluations depend exclusively on the relative quality of literary work, yet commentators say that this is no way to determine whether someone is worthy. Now, applying regulations to achieve results was something the former kings did not neglect; and employing men according to their categories of standing has certainly been practiced since the Han and Tang. Have we not heard of men whose achievements were conspicuous in their own time and whose reputations for benevolence and worth endured in later ages? How, today, can we ensure that everyone appointed is suitably employed and that regulations are established without abuses? Most of you students come from the schools and have advanced from the prefectures and counties. Can you speak to matters such as these?

Question: That China has the Yi and Di is like yang having yin, or humankind having birds and beasts alongside it: their existence cannot be eliminated. Yet the northern foes have always caused particularly severe trouble. Looking at the affairs of the Han, Emperor Gao, after his hundred battles, extended his might throughout the realm; nevertheless, the peril at Pingcheng remained unforgettable even to later generations. Emperor Xiaowu…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乘豐富之業師武臣力而邊警歲至略
無寧息竟寧以後漢事日非而羇縻塞
垣至于哀平朝獻不改非威力足制其
死命明矣然則夷狄之叛服初無與於
中國之盛衰歟前世有用柔能勝剛弱
能勝強為制御之術者信斯言也則敢
於抗盛強而拙於乘衰弱固夷狄之性
歟如劉敬之策則有女吳之深恥施賈
誼之餌則是徵令之倒置興衞霍之師
===
則犯窮黷之戒抗敵國之禮則乖王者
無外之義為斷臂散交之謀則狼心鼠
首未易可保為多防密備之計則一狼
千羊坐以自疲何如而可也自漢魏以
至于今鮮不以夷狄為意智計之士儒
先之碩其論多矣有經國用世之心者
固有考焉夫兼夷狄驅猛獸扶陽抑陰
聖賢之大義試以漢事言之則知所處
矣
punctuated: 乘豐富之業，師武臣力，而邊警歲至，略無寧息。竟寧以後，漢事日非，而羇縻塞垣，至于哀平，朝獻不改，非威力足制其死命明矣。然則夷狄之叛服，初無與於中國之盛衰歟？前世有用柔能勝剛、弱能勝強為制御之術者，信斯言也，則敢於抗盛強而拙於乘衰弱，固夷狄之性歟？如劉敬之策，則有女吳之深恥；施賈誼之餌，則是徵令之倒置；興衞霍之師，則犯窮黷之戒；抗敵國之禮，則乖王者無外之義；為斷臂散交之謀，則狼心鼠首，未易可保；為多防密備之計，則一狼千羊，坐以自疲。何如而可也？自漢魏以至于今，鮮不以夷狄為意。智計之士、儒先之碩，其論多矣。有經國用世之心者，固有考焉。夫兼夷狄、驅猛獸、扶陽抑陰，聖賢之大義。試以漢事言之，則知所處矣。
translation_en:
…inherited a rich and prosperous realm, made warfare his master and force his minister, yet alarms from the frontier came every year, with scarcely any respite. After the Jingning reign period, Han affairs deteriorated daily, yet the frontier peoples were held in loose allegiance, and through the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping their court visits and tribute offerings continued unchanged. Clearly, this was not because military might sufficed to hold their lives at its mercy. Was the rebellion or submission of the non-Chinese peoples, then, entirely unrelated to the strength or decline of the Central Kingdom? In earlier times, some adopted the principles that softness can overcome hardness and weakness can overcome strength as methods of controlling them. If these sayings are true, is it indeed the nature of these peoples to dare to resist the strong and flourishing, yet be inept at exploiting the weak and declining?

Following Liu Jing’s proposal would entail the profound humiliation of giving a daughter in marriage to Wu [?]; employing Jia Yi’s inducements would invert the proper relationship of those who exact tribute and issue commands. Raising armies like those of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing would violate the injunction against exhausting resources in reckless warfare. Observing diplomatic rites appropriate to equal states would contravene the principle that, for a true king, none lies outside his realm. Schemes to sever their arms and break up their alliances would be difficult to rely upon, given their wolfish hearts and ratlike vacillation. Plans for extensive defenses and meticulous preparations would leave a thousand sheep facing a single wolf, merely wearing themselves out. What course, then, would be acceptable?

From the Han and Wei dynasties down to the present, few have failed to give thought to the non-Chinese peoples. Men of intelligence and strategy, and the eminent Confucian scholars of earlier generations, have discussed the matter extensively. Those who aspire to order the state and put their talents to use in the world will surely have examined these discussions. Bringing the non-Chinese peoples under rule, driving away fierce beasts, supporting yang and restraining yin—these are the great principles of the sages and worthies. Discuss the matter through the affairs of the Han, so that your understanding of how to handle it may be known.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
立則見其參於前也在輿則見其倚於衡
也
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批文詞純正發明常若有見處
深得題意必老學之士也
同考試官教諭袁批義合傳註而文有發揮場
中如此作者不多見也
===
考試官侍講彭批能言於辭
考試官洗馬鄭批典雅可觀
隨吾身之所寓若斯理之有見盖忠信篤敬言
行之理也非吾心念念而不忘又豈能隨其所
在而常若有見也哉聖人告子張之意如此且
夫言必欲忠信也忠信不可頃刻而忘行必欲
篤敬也篤敬不可須臾而離方其佇立之時若
可忽也而忠信篤敬拳拳於念慮者無或忘一
舉目也恍若此理見於跬步之間與吾相參而
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「立則見其參於前也，在輿則見其倚於衡也。」

宋禮

同考試官訓導張批：「文詞純正，發明常若有見處，深得題意，必老學之士也。」

同考試官教諭袁批：「義合傳註，而文有發揮，場中如此作者不多見也。」

考試官侍講彭批：「能言於辭。」

考試官洗馬鄭批：「典雅可觀。」

隨吾身之所寓，若斯理之有見。盖忠信篤敬，言行之理也。非吾心念念而不忘，又豈能隨其所在而常若有見也哉？聖人告子張之意如此。且夫言必欲忠信也，忠信不可頃刻而忘；行必欲篤敬也，篤敬不可須臾而離。方其佇立之時，若可忽也，而忠信篤敬拳拳於念慮者無或忘。一舉目也，恍若此理見於跬步之間，與吾相參而
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“When standing, see them present before you; when riding in a carriage, see them resting against its crossbar.”

Song Li

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: “The language is pure and correct. His elucidation of the passage about constantly seeming to see these principles grasps the topic’s meaning profoundly. He must be a scholar of long learning.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “The meaning accords with the commentaries and annotations, while the composition develops it further. Writers of this caliber are seldom seen in the examination hall.”

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: “He expresses himself well in words.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: “Classically elegant and worthy of attention.”

Wherever my person may be, it is as though these principles were visibly present. For conscientiousness and trustworthiness, earnestness and reverence, are the principles governing speech and conduct. Unless my mind keeps them in thought at every moment without forgetting them, how could they constantly seem visible wherever I might be? Such was the Sage’s meaning in instructing Zizhang. Now, in speaking, one must seek to be conscientious and trustworthy: conscientiousness and trustworthiness must not be forgotten even for an instant. In acting, one must seek to be earnest and reverent: earnestness and reverence must not be departed from even for a moment. When standing still, one might suppose that one could relax one’s attention; yet conscientiousness and trustworthiness, earnestness and reverence, held devotedly in one’s thoughts, are never forgotten. At a single lifting of the eyes, it is as though these principles appeared within a step or half-step, standing alongside me and …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不舍焉及其在輿之際若可肆也而忠信篤敬
切切於心思者無少置一顧瞻也儼若此理倚
於車衡之上與吾同驅而不離焉夫忠信篤敬
本無形之可求無體之可覩今也立焉見之由
吾心不忘於佇立之頃而常目在之耳輿焉見
之由吾心不忘於在輿之時而常若有見耳不
言而忠信存不行而篤敬在雖欲頃刻離之而
不可得也吁心無往而不在理無適而不然然
後一言一行自不離於忠信篤敬而蠻貊可行
===
矣吾夫子以是為子張告其意不既深乎抑伊
尹之稱成湯於天之明命嘗以顧諟言之矣說
者謂湯之所以聖敬日躋者顧諟之功也顧諟
之言其參前倚衡之義歟雖深淺之不同其存
誠之無間一而已學者由子張參前倚衡之見
而進於湯之顧諟則作聖之功在是矣
堯以不得舜為己憂舜以不得禹皐陶為
己憂夫以百畝之不易為己憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠教人以善謂之忠
punctuated:
不舍焉。及其在輿之際，若可肆也，而忠信篤敬切切於心思者，無少置。一顧瞻也，儼若此理倚於車衡之上，與吾同驅而不離焉。夫忠信篤敬，本無形之可求，無體之可覩。今也立焉見之，由吾心不忘於佇立之頃，而常目在之耳；輿焉見之，由吾心不忘於在輿之時，而常若有見耳。不言而忠信存，不行而篤敬在，雖欲頃刻離之而不可得也。吁！心無往而不在，理無適而不然，然後一言一行自不離於忠信篤敬，而蠻貊可行矣。吾夫子以是為子張告，其意不既深乎？抑伊尹之稱成湯，於天之明命，嘗以顧諟言之矣。說者謂湯之所以聖敬日躋者，顧諟之功也。顧諟之言，其參前倚衡之義歟？雖深淺之不同，其存誠之無間，一而已。學者由子張參前倚衡之見，而進於湯之顧諟，則作聖之功在是矣。

堯以不得舜為己憂，舜以不得禹、皐陶為己憂。夫以百畝之不易為己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠。
translation_en:
…and never leave me. When riding in a carriage, one might think it permissible to relax; yet sincerity, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence, held urgently in one's thoughts, are never set aside even briefly. At a glance, it is as though this principle rests upon the carriage's crossbar, traveling with me and never departing. Sincerity, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence have no visible form to seek, no bodily substance to behold. That I now see them when standing is simply because my mind does not forget them while I stand, and my eyes remain fixed upon them. That I see them when riding is simply because my mind does not forget them while I ride, and it always seems as though they are visible. Even without speaking, sincerity and trustworthiness remain; even without acting, earnestness and reverence are present. Though I wished to depart from them for an instant, I could not. Ah! Only when the mind is present wherever one goes, and principle holds true wherever one turns, will every word and deed naturally accord with sincerity, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence, so that one may conduct oneself successfully even among the Man and Mo peoples. Was not our Master's intention profoundly significant when he thus instructed Zizhang?

Moreover, when Yi Yin praised Cheng Tang, he spoke of Tang's keeping Heaven's manifest mandate constantly in view. Commentators say that Tang's sage virtue and reverence advanced daily through the work of keeping it constantly in view. Does this expression not convey the meaning of seeing these principles standing before one and resting upon the carriage's crossbar? Though the depth of attainment differs, the uninterrupted preservation of sincerity is the same. If learners advance from Zizhang's vision of these principles standing before him and resting upon the crossbar to Tang's constant contemplation, herein lies the work of becoming a sage.

Yao regarded his failure to obtain Shun's service as his own concern; Shun regarded his failure to obtain the services of Yu and Gao Yao as his own concern. A man who regards the failure to cultivate his hundred mu of land as his own concern is a farmer. Sharing one's wealth with others is called kindness; teaching others goodness is called devotion.…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
爲天下得人者謂之仁
胡諒
同考試官訓導李批此作析理詳明遣詞簡古
非老於文學者不能故表而出之
同考試官教諭李批孟義能包括題意者鮮此
作以憂天下之大仁天下之大會意成文非稺手所及
考試官侍講彭批有關鍵有抑揚有議論
考試官洗馬鄭批措詞整健他作所不及
知聖人憂天下之大當知聖人仁天下之大而
===
其小者不足言也夫得人以治天下則足以仁
天下矣聖人安得不以不得人爲天下憂哉孟
子闢許行並耕之說其意如此且夫堯非不憂
民也而不事事以爲意其焦勞於朝夕者惟以
不得舜其人而已耳不得乎舜則民誰與治乎
舜非不憂民也而不屑屑以爲心其紆鬱於念
慮者惟以不得乎禹皐陶其人而已耳不得乎
禹皐則民誰與理乎夫以百畝之田播植未亟
而戚然其不寧者農夫之事也汗萊未闢而蹙
punctuated:
爲天下得人者，謂之仁。
胡諒。
同考試官訓導李批：此作析理詳明，遣詞簡古，非老於文學者不能，故表而出之。
同考試官教諭李批：孟義能包括題意者鮮，此作以憂天下之大、仁天下之大，會意成文，非稺手所及。
考試官侍講彭批：有關鍵，有抑揚，有議論。
考試官洗馬鄭批：措詞整健，他作所不及。
知聖人憂天下之大，當知聖人仁天下之大，而其小者不足言也。夫得人以治天下，則足以仁天下矣。聖人安得不以不得人爲天下憂哉？孟子闢許行並耕之說，其意如此。且夫堯非不憂民也，而不事事以爲意，其焦勞於朝夕者，惟以不得舜其人而已耳。不得乎舜，則民誰與治乎？舜非不憂民也，而不屑屑以爲心，其紆鬱於念慮者，惟以不得乎禹皐陶其人而已耳。不得乎禹皐，則民誰與理乎？夫以百畝之田，播植未亟，而戚然其不寧者，農夫之事也；汗萊未闢，而蹙
translation_en:
…To find worthy men for All under Heaven is called benevolence.
Hu Liang.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: This composition analyzes principles thoroughly and clearly, using concise, classically restrained language. Only someone seasoned in literary learning could achieve this; hence I have singled it out.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Few essays on the meaning of the Mencius encompass the full import of their topic. This composition brings together the magnitude of the sage’s concern for All under Heaven and the magnitude of his benevolence toward it, forming an essay from their connected meaning. This is beyond a novice’s reach.
Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor-in-waiting: It has a pivotal argument, modulation of emphasis, and reasoned discussion.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: Its wording is orderly and vigorous, beyond what the other compositions achieve.
To understand the magnitude of the sage’s concern for All under Heaven, one should understand the magnitude of his benevolence toward All under Heaven; lesser concerns scarcely merit mention. Finding worthy men to govern All under Heaven suffices to bring benevolence to it. How could the sage fail to regard the lack of worthy men as a cause for concern on behalf of All under Heaven? This was Mencius’s meaning when he refuted Xu Xing’s doctrine that rulers should till the fields alongside their subjects. Yao was not unconcerned for the people, but he did not occupy himself with every individual matter. What troubled and wearied him morning and evening was simply that he had not yet found a man such as Shun. Without Shun, with whom could he govern the people? Shun was not unconcerned for the people, but he did not burden his mind with petty details. What weighed upon his thoughts was simply that he had not yet found men such as Yu and Gao Yao. Without Yu and Gao Yao, with whom could he bring order to the people? To worry uneasily because the sowing and planting of a hundred mu of fields have not yet been completed is the farmer’s business; when the overgrown land [?] has not yet been cleared, to fret…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
然其不安者田父之職也豈以憂天下者而憂
百畝之憂哉彼以財而分人則及民者無所私
謂之惠可也然滯於狹小而不廣君子有不屑
焉以善而教人則愛民者有其實謂之忠可也
然局於有限而難久君子有不急焉惟若堯爲
天下而得熈載亮工之舜舜爲天下而得従欲
以治之禹臯則恩惠廣大而澤及於人人非仁
而何教化無窮而善被於世世又非仁而何豈
以仁天下者而先忠惠之務哉忠惠且不先而
===
况於耕乎是則聖人之所以憂天下者誠有在
矣雖然卑高之位既陳則小大之職斯異君之
不可並民而耕雖五尺童子知其爲非矣而許
行持區區之說鼓喙其間時君惑焉而如陳相
者又相與北面而師之孟子折以大義反復數
百言如對強敵然僅僅勝之則世衰道微邪說
之惑人也盖久矣向無孟子則處士之議豈直
洪水猛獸之災故曰功不在禹下
易
punctuated:
然其不安者，田父之職也。豈以憂天下者而憂百畝之憂哉？彼以財而分人，則及民者無所私，謂之惠可也；然滯於狹小而不廣，君子有不屑焉。以善而教人，則愛民者有其實，謂之忠可也；然局於有限而難久，君子有不急焉。惟若堯爲天下而得熈載亮工之舜，舜爲天下而得従欲以治之禹臯，則恩惠廣大而澤及於人人，非仁而何？教化無窮而善被於世世，又非仁而何？豈以仁天下者而先忠惠之務哉？忠惠且不先，而况於耕乎？是則聖人之所以憂天下者，誠有在矣。雖然，卑高之位既陳，則小大之職斯異。君之不可並民而耕，雖五尺童子知其爲非矣。而許行持區區之說，鼓喙其間，時君惑焉，而如陳相者又相與北面而師之。孟子折以大義，反復數百言，如對強敵然，僅僅勝之，則世衰道微，邪說之惑人也盖久矣。向無孟子，則處士之議豈直洪水猛獸之災？故曰：「功不在禹下。」

易
translation_en:
…and to feel uneasy over this is the farmer’s responsibility. How could one who takes thought for All-under-Heaven concern himself with the worries of a hundred mu of farmland? Someone who distributes wealth to others extends assistance to the people without selfish partiality; this may be called generosity. Yet it remains confined within a narrow compass and does not reach far, so the gentleman may disdain to undertake it. Someone who teaches others what is good gives substance to his love for the people; this may be called conscientious devotion. Yet its scope is limited and its effects are difficult to sustain, so the gentleman may regard it as no urgent priority. Only when, like Yao, one obtains for All-under-Heaven a Shun who can promote achievements and assist in accomplishing the work of government, or, like Shun, obtains a Yu and a Gao Yao who can govern in accordance with his wishes, does beneficence become so extensive that its blessings reach every person. What is this if not benevolence? Moral instruction then knows no bounds, and its goodness reaches generation after generation. What, again, is this if not benevolence? How could one who brings benevolence to All-under-Heaven give precedence to acts of conscientious devotion and generosity? If even these do not take precedence, how much less should plowing? Thus the sages’ concern for All-under-Heaven truly has its proper focus.

Nevertheless, once higher and lower positions have been established, greater and lesser responsibilities accordingly differ. Even a child five feet tall knows that it is wrong for a ruler to plow alongside the people. Yet Xu Xing upheld his petty doctrine and noisily advocated it among them. The rulers of the time were misled, while men like Chen Xiang joined together in facing north before him and taking him as their teacher. Mencius refuted him with the great principles of right, arguing back and forth for several hundred words as though confronting a formidable enemy, and only barely prevailed. Thus the age had declined and the Way had grown faint, and heterodox doctrines had evidently been misleading people for a long time. Had there been no Mencius, would the harm caused by the arguments of scholars out of office have been merely equal to that of floods and savage beasts? Hence it is said: “His achievement was no less than Yu’s.”

Book of Changes

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
泰小往大来吉亨彖曰泰小往大来吉亨
則是天地交而萬物通也上下交而其
志同也内陽而外陰内健而外順内君
子而外小人君子道長小人道消也
沈元
同考試官訓導張批題本平易作者不泛則畧是
篇說理明而辭不費可謂作者
同考試官教諭袁批此作發明泰義詳盡一結歸
本於君臣同志尤見學識他篇亦佳一薦何忝
===
考試官侍講彭批簡潔
考試官洗馬鄭批易義貴明潔此作得之
前聖畫泰之卦後聖係泰之辭故傳復申明之
也盖卦具通泰之義宜其占之吉亨也聖人既
畫卦而係辭吾夫子安得不申明之於後哉昔
伏羲畫卦交坤於乾之上名之曰泰盖取通泰
之義也文王係辭以為是卦坤往居外乾来居
内又自歸妹来六往居四九来居三皆小往而
大来也夫小往居外大来居内固有吉亨之道
punctuated:
泰，小往大来，吉亨。彖曰：「泰，小往大来，吉亨，則是天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。内陽而外陰，内健而外順，内君子而外小人。君子道長，小人道消也。」

沈元

同考試官訓導張批：「題本平易，作者不泛則畧。是篇說理明而辭不費，可謂作者。」

同考試官教諭袁批：「此作發明泰義詳盡，一結歸本於君臣同志，尤見學識。他篇亦佳，一薦何忝？」

考試官侍講彭批：「簡潔。」

考試官洗馬鄭批：「易義貴明潔，此作得之。」

前聖畫泰之卦，後聖係泰之辭，故傳復申明之也。盖卦具通泰之義，宜其占之吉亨也。聖人既畫卦而係辭，吾夫子安得不申明之於後哉？昔伏羲畫卦，交坤於乾之上，名之曰泰，盖取通泰之義也。文王係辭，以為是卦坤往居外，乾来居内；又自歸妹来，六往居四，九来居三，皆小往而大来也。夫小往居外，大来居内，固有吉亨之道
translation_en:
Tai (Peace): the small departs and the great comes; auspicious and successful. The Commentary on the Judgments says: “Tai: the small departs and the great comes; auspicious and successful. This means that Heaven and Earth interact and all things pass freely into communication; those above and those below interact and share the same purpose. Within is yang and without is yin; within is strength and without is compliance; within are noble men and without are petty men. The way of noble men grows, and the way of petty men wanes.”

Shen Yuan.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: “The topic itself is straightforward, but writers tend to be either diffuse or overly brief. This essay explains the principles clearly without wasting words. Its author may truly be called an accomplished writer.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “This composition elucidates the meaning of Tai thoroughly. Its conclusion traces everything back to the shared purpose of ruler and ministers, particularly revealing the author’s learning and understanding. His other essays are also fine. How could recommending him be undeserved?”

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor-in-waiting: “Concise and lucid.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Vice Director of the Library: “Essays on the meaning of the Changes prize clarity and concision. This composition achieves them.”

An earlier sage drew the hexagram Tai, and a later sage attached its statement; hence the Commentary further elucidates it. The hexagram embodies the meaning of free communication and peace, so it is fitting that its divinatory prediction should be auspicious and successful. Once the sages had drawn the hexagram and attached its statement, how could our Master fail to elucidate it afterward? Long ago, when Fuxi drew the hexagrams, he placed Kun above Qian in interaction and named it Tai, taking the sense of free communication and peace. When King Wen attached the statement, he considered that in this hexagram Kun departs to occupy the outer position, while Qian comes to occupy the inner position. Moreover, it derives from Guimei (The Marrying Maiden): the six departs to occupy the fourth position, and the nine comes to occupy the third. In both cases, the small departs and the great comes. Now, when the small departs to occupy the outer position and the great comes to occupy the inner position, there is indeed a way to auspiciousness and success …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矣占者陽剛豈不吉而且亨乎羲文聖人名卦
繫辭之意如此吾夫子傳彖又從而申明之謂
夫泰之小往大来而吉亨者則是天氣下交於
地地氣上達於天而品物流形各遂其發育之
性矣君推誠以任下臣竭誠以事上而君臣同
心共濟夫天下之事矣乾爲陽爲健而来居於
内坤爲陰爲順而往居於外乾陽爲君子而在
内是君子任用於上也坤陰爲小人而在外是
小人退處於下也君子在内則剛明用事而拔
===
茅連茹之吉可致其道之長爲何如小人在外
則陰邪屏迹而剥廬無號之凶可必其道之消
又何如吾夫子發明名卦係辭之㫖无餘蘊矣
大抵天地交而萬物通天地之泰也上下交而
其志同朝廷之泰也君子道長非天下之泰乎
以天下之泰推之朝廷之泰由朝廷之泰推而
爲天下之泰然則參賛調燮致治隆平以保泰
於無窮者則本乎君臣志同以致之也大易之
㫖淵乎微哉
punctuated:
矣。占者陽剛，豈不吉而且亨乎？羲文聖人名卦繫辭之意如此。吾夫子傳彖，又從而申明之，謂夫泰之小往大来而吉亨者，則是天氣下交於地，地氣上達於天，而品物流形，各遂其發育之性矣。君推誠以任下，臣竭誠以事上，而君臣同心，共濟夫天下之事矣。乾爲陽爲健而来居於内，坤爲陰爲順而往居於外。乾陽爲君子而在内，是君子任用於上也；坤陰爲小人而在外，是小人退處於下也。君子在内，則剛明用事，而拔茅連茹之吉可致，其道之長爲何如？小人在外，則陰邪屏迹，而剥廬無號之凶可必，其道之消又何如？吾夫子發明名卦係辭之㫖，无餘蘊矣。

大抵天地交而萬物通，天地之泰也；上下交而其志同，朝廷之泰也。君子道長，非天下之泰乎？以天下之泰推之朝廷之泰，由朝廷之泰推而爲天下之泰。然則參賛調燮，致治隆平，以保泰於無窮者，則本乎君臣志同以致之也。大易之㫖，淵乎微哉！
translation_en:
…indeed. If the diviner possesses yang firmness, will there not be good fortune and success alike? Such was the intent of the sages Fuxi and King Wen in naming the hexagram and attaching its statement. Our Master Confucius further elucidated it in his Commentary on the Judgment. He explained that in Tai (Peace), “the small departs and the great approaches,” bringing good fortune and success: Heaven’s vital force descends to mingle with Earth, and Earth’s vital force rises to reach Heaven. The myriad beings thus take form in the flow of transformation, each fulfilling its nature through growth and development. The ruler extends his sincerity in entrusting duties to his subordinates, and ministers exhaust their sincerity in serving their superior. Ruler and ministers thus share one mind and together accomplish the affairs of the realm. Qian represents yang and strength and comes to occupy the inner position; Kun represents yin and receptivity and departs to occupy the outer position. Qian’s yang represents noble men and is within: this means that noble men are employed in high positions. Kun’s yin represents petty men and is without: this means that petty men withdraw to low positions. When noble men are within, the firm and discerning conduct affairs, and the good fortune of “pulling up thatch grass with its intertwined roots” can be attained. How greatly their way will flourish! When petty men are without, the yin and perverse disappear from view, and the misfortunes of “stripping away the dwelling” and “having none to cry out to” are certain. How thoroughly their way will decline! Our Master Confucius elucidated the intent behind the naming of the hexagram and the attachment of its statement, leaving none of its implications unexplored.

Generally speaking, when Heaven and Earth interact and the myriad beings flourish, this is the peace of Heaven and Earth. When those above and below interact and share a common purpose, this is the peace of the court. When the way of noble men flourishes, is this not the peace of the realm? From the peace of the realm one may infer the peace of the court; from the peace of the court one may extend peace throughout the realm. Thus, participating in and assisting the transforming work of Heaven and Earth, harmonizing their forces, and bringing government to flourishing peace so as to preserve peace without end—all this is achieved on the basis of ruler and ministers sharing a common purpose. How profound and subtle is the meaning of the great Book of Changes!

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
富有之謂大業日新之謂盛德生生之謂
易
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批此題人能作之而發明親切
者絕少晚得是篇詞理俱到非造詣深者不能及此宜爲
本房之冠
同考試官教諭袁批此篇本顯仁蔵用立說深得
本旨誠易中之翹楚也健羨健羨
考試官侍講彭批文有發明
===
考試官洗馬鄭批理致精密其嘗究心易學者乎
聖人論造化生成之功必言陰陽不已之妙盖
造化之德業生成之功也然所以生成而不已
者豈非所謂易乎宜大傳聖人詳言之也且夫
道之流行於造化也有大業焉有盛德焉果何
以見之哉自其蔵用言之則歛化育於寂然之
中歸生意於至靜之内物雖萬類之不同俾各
保合其氣而無外物雖萬彙之不一俾各翕聚
其理而不遺其大而無外也如此得不謂之大
punctuated:
富有之謂大業，日新之謂盛德，生生之謂易。
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批：此題人能作之，而發明親切者絕少。晚得是篇，詞理俱到，非造詣深者不能及此，宜爲本房之冠。
同考試官教諭袁批：此篇本顯仁蔵用立說，深得本旨，誠易中之翹楚也。健羨，健羨！
考試官侍講彭批：文有發明。
考試官洗馬鄭批：理致精密，其嘗究心易學者乎？
聖人論造化生成之功，必言陰陽不已之妙。盖造化之德業，生成之功也。然所以生成而不已者，豈非所謂易乎？宜大傳聖人詳言之也。且夫道之流行於造化也，有大業焉，有盛德焉，果何以見之哉？自其蔵用言之，則歛化育於寂然之中，歸生意於至靜之内。物雖萬類之不同，俾各保合其氣而無外；物雖萬彙之不一，俾各翕聚其理而不遺。其大而無外也如此，得不謂之大
translation_en:
“Abundant possession is called great achievement; daily renewal is called flourishing virtue; generation upon generation is called change.”
Song Li
Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: Anyone can write on this topic, but very few elucidate it with precision and relevance. Late in the process I obtained this essay: both its language and its reasoning are fully accomplished. Only someone of profound attainment could reach this level. It deserves first place in this examining room.
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: This essay grounds its argument in “manifesting benevolence and concealing its operation,” penetrating deeply into the original meaning. It is truly outstanding among essays on the Book of Changes. How admirable, how admirable!
Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: The essay offers illuminating insights.
Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: Its reasoning is refined and precise. Surely its author has devoted himself to studying the Book of Changes?
When the sage discusses the work of creation in generating and completing things, he must speak of the subtle workings of yin and yang in their ceaseless activity. For the virtue and achievement of creation consist in its work of generating and completing things. Yet is not that by which it generates and completes things without ceasing precisely what is called change? It is fitting that the sage discusses this in detail in the Great Commentary. Now, as the Way flows through creation, there is great achievement and there is flourishing virtue. How, indeed, can these be discerned? Speaking in terms of its concealing its operation, it gathers transformation and nurture into quiescence and returns the impulse of life to utter stillness. Though things differ in their myriad kinds, it enables each to preserve and unite its vital force, excluding none; though things vary in their myriad categories, it enables each to gather together its principle, omitting none. Its greatness, which leaves nothing outside itself, is such as this: can it fail to be called great …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
業乎自其顯仁言之則大化運行於兩間和氣
充塞於上下與之氣以為生之質者不以古今
而有間賦之理以為性之原者不以終始而或
息其久而無窮也如此得不謂之盛德乎然造
化之所以蔵用者陰之為也蔵之未久而生意
顯著於外者不可遏則是陰變為陽而生生不
窮易書之姤變而為復者是已造化之所以顯
仁者陽之為也顯之未久而化工歸蔵於内者
不可見則陽變為陰而生生不已易書之復變
===
而為姤者是已陰陽相生變化無窮理與書一
而已聖人論造化之生成而推之於易有以哉
大抵有天地則有此變化有變化則有此生成
推其原固莫非陰陽之所為而實有自然流行
不倚於陰陽者存乎其間不然安能亘千萬古
變化生成相為循環不已如是哉故曰陰陽不
測之謂神
書
夙夜惟寅直哉惟清
punctuated:
業乎？自其顯仁言之，則大化運行於兩間，和氣充塞於上下，與之氣以為生之質者，不以古今而有間；賦之理以為性之原者，不以終始而或息。其久而無窮也如此，得不謂之盛德乎？然造化之所以蔵用者，陰之為也。蔵之未久，而生意顯著於外者不可遏，則是陰變為陽，而生生不窮，《易》書之姤變而為復者是已。造化之所以顯仁者，陽之為也。顯之未久，而化工歸蔵於内者不可見，則陽變為陰，而生生不已，《易》書之復變而為姤者是已。陰陽相生，變化無窮，理與書一而已。聖人論造化之生成而推之於《易》，有以哉！大抵有天地則有此變化，有變化則有此生成。推其原，固莫非陰陽之所為，而實有自然流行、不倚於陰陽者存乎其間。不然，安能亘千萬古，變化生成相為循環不已如是哉？故曰：「陰陽不測之謂神。」

書

夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。
translation_en:
…achievement? Speaking of its manifesting benevolence, the great transforming process operates between Heaven and Earth, and harmonious vital energy fills the regions above and below. Its bestowal of vital energy as the substance of life admits no interruption between antiquity and the present; its endowment of principle as the source of innate nature never ceases from beginning to end. Since its duration is thus inexhaustible, can it fail to be called abundant virtue? Yet creation’s concealing its operations is the work of yin. Before they have long been concealed, the impulse of life manifests outwardly and cannot be checked: this is yin changing into yang, with life generating life without end. This is what the transformation of Gou (Encounter) into Fu (Return) in the Book of Changes represents. Creation’s manifesting benevolence is the work of yang. Before it has long been manifest, the workings of transformation withdraw into concealment within and cannot be seen: this is yang changing into yin, with life generating life without cease. This is what the transformation of Fu into Gou in the Book of Changes represents. Yin and yang generate one another, and their transformations are inexhaustible. The principle and the book are one, nothing more. There is good reason that the sage, in discussing creation’s generation and completion of things, traced these back to the Changes!

Broadly speaking, wherever Heaven and Earth exist, these transformations exist; wherever transformations exist, this generation and completion exist. Tracing them to their source, all are indeed the work of yin and yang. Yet within them there truly exists something that flows of itself, without depending upon yin and yang. Otherwise, how could transformation and the generation and completion of things alternate in an unceasing cycle throughout countless ages in this way? Thus it is said: “That which is unfathomable in yin and yang is called the numinous.”

Book of Documents

“Morning and night, be reverent; be upright, be pure.”

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
張恕
同考試官訓導李批文理簡明筆力蒼古宜錄之
以式後學
同考試官教諭李批作此題者多以敬直平講而
清為之效殊非當時立言本旨此作見理明而遣辭當是
以錄之
考試官侍講彭批蓋於經文體貼不徒註脚生義
考試官洗馬鄭批得當時命官語意
聖君告典禮之官欲其端行禮之本蓋必寅直
===
清而後可以行其禮也秩宗典事神之禮所以
交於神明可不知所務哉宜帝舜以是而命伯
夷也蓋謂典三禮而有事於神明必端其本而
後可以交於神明是故時而夙也雖或非承祀
宗廟之時而嚴恭以度凛乎祖考之予顧蓋自
早以達於昏暮翼翼其無間也時而夜也雖或
非有事乎郊社之際而祗肅以承儼乎上帝之
女臨蓋自夜以接于旦朝夔夔其靡懈也于焉
必有以直乎内而不使私曲之或存不啻矢之
punctuated:
張恕

同考試官訓導李批：文理簡明，筆力蒼古，宜錄之以式後學。

同考試官教諭李批：作此題者，多以敬直平講，而清為之效，殊非當時立言本旨。此作見理明而遣辭當，是以錄之。

考試官侍講彭批：蓋於經文體貼，不徒註脚生義。

考試官洗馬鄭批：得當時命官語意。

聖君告典禮之官，欲其端行禮之本，蓋必寅、直、清，而後可以行其禮也。秩宗典事神之禮，所以交於神明，可不知所務哉？宜帝舜以是而命伯夷也。蓋謂典三禮而有事於神明，必端其本，而後可以交於神明。是故時而夙也，雖或非承祀宗廟之時，而嚴恭以度，凛乎祖考之予顧，蓋自早以達於昏暮，翼翼其無間也；時而夜也，雖或非有事乎郊社之際，而祗肅以承，儼乎上帝之女臨，蓋自夜以接于旦朝，夔夔其靡懈也。于焉必有以直乎内，而不使私曲之或存，不啻矢之
translation_en:
Zhang Shu

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: The argument is concise and clear, and the writing vigorous and archaic. It should be included as a model for later students.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Most who write on this topic discuss reverence and uprightness on the same level, treating purity as their effect. This is quite contrary to the original intent of the words when they were spoken. This composition understands the principle clearly and expresses it aptly; hence its inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: It closely attends to the canonical text, rather than merely deriving interpretations from the commentary.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian of the Heir Apparent: It captures the meaning and tenor of the words spoken when the official was appointed.

When the sage ruler addressed the official in charge of ritual, he wished him to set right the foundation of ritual practice. For only with reverence, uprightness, and purity could he perform the rites. The Grand Master of Ceremonies presides over the rites for serving the spirits, through which one communes with divine powers. Could he fail to understand what he must attend to? It was fitting that Emperor Shun should charge Bo Yi in these terms. The meaning is that, in presiding over the three classes of rites and serving divine powers, one must first set right the foundation; only then can one commune with them. Thus, in the early morning, even when it is not the time to offer sacrifices in the ancestral temple, he must conduct himself with solemn respect, awed as though his forebears were looking upon him. From morning until dusk, his vigilance must be uninterrupted. At night, even when it is not the occasion for sacrifices at the suburban altar or the altar of soil, he must attend with reverent solemnity, grave as though the Lord on High were present above him. From night until dawn, his reverent care must never slacken. In this he must find the means to make himself upright within, allowing no selfish crookedness to remain, no less than an arrow’s …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
棘而繩之引乃可以言乎直于焉必有以潔其
心而不使物欲之或汚不啻江漢之濯而澗沚
之湜乃可以言乎清如是則與天者游而鬼神
合德由是行其禮事其神不亦有感通之道哉
大抵禮敬而已敬則此心收斂而能直直則此
心虛明而能清故寅直清行禮之本而寅又直
清之本也若夫籩豆之事則有司存焉
伻來毖殷乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣曰明禋
拜手稽首休享
===
胡諒
同考試官訓導李批寫出周公述成王遣使毖殷
命寧之意宛如也讀之令人心目豁然
同考試官教諭李批塲中多為此題所窘惟是篇
辭理明暢𨗳然出衆其壁經中之巨擘歟
考試官侍講彭批於文義訓詁皆明白
考試官洗馬鄭批辭意通暢
大臣述賢王因勅殷之使隆錫命之禮盖謹毖
庶殷固以繋安危之慮而命寧周公則委重之
punctuated:
棘而繩之引，乃可以言乎直。于焉必有以潔其心，而不使物欲之或汚，不啻江漢之濯而澗沚之湜，乃可以言乎清。如是，則與天者游而鬼神合德。由是行其禮、事其神，不亦有感通之道哉？大抵禮，敬而已。敬則此心收斂而能直，直則此心虛明而能清。故寅直清，行禮之本，而寅又直清之本也。若夫籩豆之事，則有司存焉。
伻來毖殷，乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣，曰明禋。拜手稽首，休享。
胡諒
同考試官訓導李批：寫出周公述成王遣使毖殷、命寧之意，宛如也。讀之令人心目豁然。
同考試官教諭李批：塲中多為此題所窘，惟是篇辭理明暢，𨗳然出衆，其壁經中之巨擘歟！
考試官侍講彭批：於文義訓詁皆明白。
考試官洗馬鄭批：辭意通暢。
大臣述賢王因勅殷之使隆錫命之禮。盖謹毖庶殷，固以繋安危之慮，而命寧周公，則委重之
translation_en:
…straightness and the tautness of a stretched cord: only then can one speak of uprightness. Here one must also purify one’s heart, allowing no contamination by material desires, as though washed in the Jiang and Han rivers and made as clear as the waters of mountain streams. Only then can one speak of purity. In this way one associates with Heaven and shares the virtue of ghosts and spirits. Performing rites and serving the spirits on this basis, does one not possess a means of eliciting their response and communicating with them? In general, ritual is simply reverence. Through reverence the heart is collected and becomes upright; through uprightness it becomes open and luminous, and thus pure. Hence reverence, uprightness, and purity are the foundation of performing rites, while reverence is itself the foundation of uprightness and purity. As for the matters of sacrificial baskets and stands, there are officials responsible for those.
“He sent an envoy to caution the people of Yin, and then commanded that I be reassured with two vessels of fragrant black-millet wine, saying that they were for a pure sacrifice. I bowed with clasped hands and touched my head to the ground, acknowledging the gracious offering.”
Hu Liang.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: “This brings out most faithfully the meaning of the Duke of Zhou’s account of King Cheng sending an envoy to caution the people of Yin and commanding that he be reassured. Reading it opens the mind and clears the vision.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “Many in the examination hall were stymied by this topic. This essay alone is lucid and fluent in both expression and reasoning, standing conspicuously above the rest. Surely it is a foremost achievement among essays on the ‘Wall Classic’ [?]!”
Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: “Both the meaning of the text and the interpretation of its words are clear.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian of the Heir Apparent: “The wording and ideas are fluent and clear.”
A great minister recounts how a worthy king, on the occasion of sending an envoy to admonish the people of Yin, made his bestowal of gifts and commands especially solemn. For carefully cautioning the multitude of Yin certainly concerned his anxiety over security and peril, while commanding that the Duke of Zhou be reassured expressed the entrusting of weighty responsibility …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
意也周公詳述其事而其君臣之際有可觀矣
昔成王甫畢事於新邑遂退即于宗周留後之
責既付於周公毖殷之事復馳於專使誠以殷
民之遐逖固雖舊矣今則密邇王室申之以文
告所以益堅其式化之念殷士之臣我亦有年
矣今則周公初政重之以戒勅所以益勵其承
叙之心然訓儆殷人固所當急而慰荅周公尤
不可緩於是因毖殷之使致綏寧之命有物以
備其儀有辭以達其敬言乎其物則釀以秬黍
===
和以鬱鬯其尊以中所謂卣也其數以二所謂
朋也是儀也降灌之所須宗廟之盛禮獻之於
公豈非備非常之儀哉言乎其辭則以謂致潔
盡敬以將誠有齊明之德焉拜手稽首而休享
有嘉薦之道焉是敬也嚴於承祀之際陳於昭
假之時施之於公豈非致非常之敬哉周公述
成王之遣使錫命詞詳而不殺亦惟其儀與敬
之非常耳不然則酒醴尊罍之間豈足以煩周
公之齒頰哉又因是而有見焉周公於成王之
punctuated:
意也。周公詳述其事，而其君臣之際有可觀矣。
昔成王甫畢事於新邑，遂退即于宗周。留後之責既付於周公，毖殷之事復馳於專使。誠以殷民之遐逖固雖舊矣，今則密邇王室，申之以文告，所以益堅其式化之念；殷士之臣我亦有年矣，今則周公初政，重之以戒勅，所以益勵其承叙之心。然訓儆殷人固所當急，而慰荅周公尤不可緩。於是因毖殷之使，致綏寧之命，有物以備其儀，有辭以達其敬。言乎其物，則釀以秬黍，和以鬱鬯，其尊以中，所謂卣也；其數以二，所謂朋也。是儀也，降灌之所須，宗廟之盛禮，獻之於公，豈非備非常之儀哉？言乎其辭，則以謂致潔盡敬以將誠，有齊明之德焉；拜手稽首而休享，有嘉薦之道焉。是敬也，嚴於承祀之際，陳於昭假之時，施之於公，豈非致非常之敬哉？周公述成王之遣使錫命，詞詳而不殺，亦惟其儀與敬之非常耳。不然，則酒醴尊罍之間，豈足以煩周公之齒頰哉？又因是而有見焉：周公於成王之
translation_en:
…was the intention. The Duke of Zhou recounts the affair in detail, revealing something worthy of contemplation in the relationship between ruler and minister.
Formerly, when King Cheng had just completed his business in the new city, he withdrew to Zongzhou. Having entrusted the Duke of Zhou with responsibility for remaining behind, he also dispatched a special envoy to admonish the people of Yin. Indeed, although the people of Yin had long been far removed [?], they were now close to the royal house. Reiterating instructions through a written proclamation would further strengthen their resolve to follow its transforming influence. The officers of Yin, too, had served us as subjects for years; now, however, the Duke of Zhou was beginning his administration. Reinforcing the instructions with admonitions would further encourage their willingness to accept the established order. Yet, urgent though instructing and warning the people of Yin certainly was, reassuring and acknowledging the Duke of Zhou could still less be delayed. Accordingly, through the envoy sent to admonish Yin, the king conveyed a charge of reassurance, providing objects to complete the ceremony and words to express his respect.
As for the objects, the wine was brewed from black millet and blended with aromatic herbs. Its vessels were of medium size, the vessels called you; their number was two, constituting what was called a peng, or pair. These ceremonial provisions were required for libations inviting the spirits to descend—a grand rite of the ancestral temple. In presenting them to the duke, was the king not furnishing an extraordinary ceremonial gift? As for the words, they spoke of achieving purity and showing the utmost reverence to convey sincerity, thereby displaying the virtue of purity and illumination; and of bowing with hands lowered and forehead to the ground to make a splendid offering, thereby observing the proper way of presenting worthy gifts. Such reverence was solemnly maintained when performing sacrifices and displayed when the spirits manifestly arrived. In extending it to the duke, was the king not expressing extraordinary respect?
The Duke of Zhou’s account of King Cheng’s dispatch of an envoy to confer this charge is detailed and unabridged solely because the ceremony and the respect it expressed were extraordinary. Otherwise, how could matters of wine and sacrificial vessels have warranted the Duke of Zhou’s speaking at such length? From this a further insight emerges: the Duke of Zhou, with regard to King Cheng’s…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
錫命盖不敢宿而禋于文武矣是周公之存也
且不敢以秬鬯之奉自安則其没也廟之以天
子之禮公其顧歆乎故君子之愛人孝子之事
親惟其當而已使成王之賜伯禽之受非誣則
其於周公也亦淺矣
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼既同上入執宫功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乗屋其始播
===
百穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌
陰四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭九月肅霜十
月滌場朋酒斯饗曰殺羔羊躋彼公堂
稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
李溥
同考試官教諭胡批此題傳釋明白場中作者區
區於禦寒備暑之說殊非大旨此篇深得邠民相與警戒
為農勸戒為君之意必熟於是經者宜置高選
同考試官學正裘批此作以邠民警戒勸戒立說
punctuated:
錫命，盖不敢宿而禋于文武矣。是周公之存也，且不敢以秬鬯之奉自安，則其没也，廟之以天子之禮，公其顧歆乎？故君子之愛人，孝子之事親，惟其當而已。使成王之賜、伯禽之受非誣，則其於周公也亦淺矣。

詩
九月築場圃，十月納禾稼，黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫！我稼既同，上入執宫功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯，亟其乗屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。九月肅霜，十月滌場。朋酒斯饗，曰殺羔羊。躋彼公堂，稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆！

李溥

同考試官教諭胡批：此題傳釋明白，場中作者區區於禦寒備暑之說，殊非大旨。此篇深得邠民相與警戒為農、勸戒為君之意，必熟於是經者，宜置高選。

同考試官學正裘批：此作以邠民警戒勸戒立說，
translation_en:
…the royal grant and charge, he presumably did not dare to let a night pass before making a pure offering to Kings Wen and Wu. Thus, while the Duke of Zhou was alive, he did not dare to rest content with receiving the black-millet sacrificial liquor for himself. After his death, then, would the duke turn toward and accept offerings made to him in a temple with the rites proper to the Son of Heaven? Thus, when a gentleman loves another, or a filial son serves his parents, all that matters is doing what is fitting. If the accounts of King Cheng’s bestowal and Bo Qin’s acceptance are not false, their understanding of the Duke of Zhou was shallow indeed.

Book of Odes
In the ninth month we prepare the threshing ground in the garden;
in the tenth month we bring in the crops:
broomcorn and foxtail millet, late-ripening and early-ripening grain,
grain, hemp, beans, and wheat.
Ah, we farmers!
Our crops are now gathered;
we go up into the settlement to work on the houses.
By day you gather thatching grass;
by night you twist ropes.
Hurry up onto the roofs to thatch them;
then you must begin sowing the hundred grains.
In the second month we cut ice with resounding blows;
in the third month we store it in the icehouse.
Early in the fourth month,
we offer a lamb and sacrifice with chives.
In the ninth month the frost is sharp;
in the tenth month we clear the threshing ground.
With paired vessels of wine we hold a feast,
and slaughter lambs.
We ascend the lord’s hall
and raise those rhinoceros-horn cups:
may he live ten thousand years, without end!

Li Pu

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: The commentary explains this passage clearly. Writers in the examination hall confined themselves to discussions of warding off cold and preparing for heat, which entirely miss its main purport. This essay deeply grasps the meaning of the people of Bin admonishing one another in their work as farmers and offering encouragement and admonition for their ruler’s sake. Its author must be thoroughly familiar with this classic and should be ranked among the best.

Comment by Associate Examiner Qiu, School Instructor: This composition bases its argument on the warnings, encouragement, and admonitions of the people of Bin…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
深合題意且筆力老健必非膚淺之學也可嘉可嘉
考試官侍講彭批篇末數語殊有餘味
考試官洗馬鄭批邠人憂勤忠愛之意溢于
言表善說詩者也
邠民爲農而相警戒有憂勤之意爲君而相勸
戒有忠愛之心夫賴以養生者在農而所以得
安於農者則君也邠民方以農事相與警戒遽
以君事相與勸戒誠知所本而風俗淳厚也歟
周公備述以教成王宜矣想夫邠人之意謂夫
===
時維九月場可治矣則種藝之圃築堅而場之
焉時維十月場已治矣則禾稼之穫自田而納
之焉黍稷重穋所納非一類也禾麻菽麥所登
非一種也於是嗟嘆以爲我農之力於田者其
稼既聚矣我室之在邑者可以上入而執其修
治之功矣彼茅所以供苫覆者晝焉而往取索
所以爲繆葺者宵焉而是綯兼晝夜之不息急
乘屋以致功盖以嗣歲復来播穀復始而不暇
於此矣夫當農事之甫畢又念農事之將始不
punctuated:
深合題意，且筆力老健，必非膚淺之學也。可嘉，可嘉！
考試官侍講彭批：篇末數語，殊有餘味。
考試官洗馬鄭批：邠人憂勤忠愛之意溢于言表，善說詩者也。
邠民爲農而相警戒，有憂勤之意；爲君而相勸戒，有忠愛之心。夫賴以養生者在農，而所以得安於農者則君也。邠民方以農事相與警戒，遽以君事相與勸戒，誠知所本而風俗淳厚也歟！周公備述以教成王，宜矣。想夫邠人之意，謂夫時維九月，場可治矣，則種藝之圃，築堅而場之焉；時維十月，場已治矣，則禾稼之穫，自田而納之焉。黍稷重穋，所納非一類也；禾麻菽麥，所登非一種也。於是嗟嘆以爲我農之力於田者，其稼既聚矣；我室之在邑者，可以上入而執其修治之功矣。彼茅所以供苫覆者，晝焉而往取；索所以爲繆葺者，宵焉而是綯。兼晝夜之不息，急乘屋以致功，盖以嗣歲復来，播穀復始，而不暇於此矣。夫當農事之甫畢，又念農事之將始，不
translation_en:
…accords profoundly with the meaning of the topic. Moreover, the writing is mature and vigorous; this surely reflects no shallow learning. Commendable, commendable!
Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: The few words at the end of the essay leave a particularly rich lingering impression.
Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: The anxious diligence and loyal affection of the people of Bin overflow beyond the words. This writer is skilled at interpreting the Book of Poetry.
When the people of Bin admonished one another about farming, they showed anxious diligence; when they exhorted and admonished one another concerning their lord, they showed loyal affection. For farming is what sustains life, while the lord enables people to farm in peace. Having just admonished one another about agricultural affairs, the people of Bin immediately exhorted one another concerning service to their lord. Surely they understood the foundations on which they depended, and their customs were simple and generous! It was fitting that the Duke of Zhou should recount all this to instruct King Cheng. We may imagine the people of Bin expressing their thoughts thus:
It is the ninth month, and the threshing ground can be prepared. The garden plots where crops were grown are beaten firm and made into a threshing ground. It is the tenth month, and the threshing ground is ready. The harvested crops are brought in from the fields. Broomcorn millet and foxtail millet, late-ripening and early-ripening grain—the produce brought in is of more than one kind. Grain, hemp, beans, and wheat—the harvest is of more than one variety. Then they sigh and say: We farmers have labored in the fields, and our crops are now gathered. We can go up into our homes in the settlement and undertake their repair. By day we go and gather the thatch needed for roofing; by night we twist the ropes needed for binding and mending. Working without rest through day and night, we hasten to climb onto the roofs and finish the work, because the coming year will soon arrive, grain sowing will begin again, and we shall have no leisure for these tasks.
Thus, just as the farming work is finished, they already think of its beginning again, not…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
待督責自相警戒其憂勤之意何如哉然猶未
也又以爲二陽之月之日爲公而伐氷冲冲焉
三陽之月之日取氷而納之凌陰焉誠以四陽
之月其日之蚤君將獻羔韭以祭司寒之神遂
啓氷而先寢廟之薦矣至於九月時已氣肅而
霜降十月則當速畢其塲功於是酒則尊兩壺
以爲饗牲必兼羔羊而特殺將携以往升公之
堂舉兕觥之觫祝吾君之壽祝壽而曰萬壽則
極其數之盈也萬壽而曰無疆則申其意於不
已也夫汲汲於趨公之役又惓惓於享上之心
相勸以亟相戒以預其忠愛之意何如哉嗟夫
此邠俗之舊而公劉后稷之化其王業之始基
歟成王周公之際則固已彌文矣稼穡艱難之
事君民相與之真淳厚朴野之習其不得而接
於耳目者有矇瞍朝夕之誦焉於是周公之慮
盖深遠矣
豈弟君子民之父母
倪天民
punctuated:
待督責，自相警戒，其憂勤之意何如哉！然猶未也，又以爲二陽之月之日，爲公而伐氷冲冲焉；三陽之月之日，取氷而納之凌陰焉。誠以四陽之月，其日之蚤，君將獻羔韭以祭司寒之神，遂啓氷而先寢廟之薦矣。至於九月，時已氣肅而霜降；十月，則當速畢其塲功。於是酒則尊兩壺以爲饗，牲必兼羔羊而特殺，將携以往升公之堂，舉兕觥之觫，祝吾君之壽。祝壽而曰萬壽，則極其數之盈也；萬壽而曰無疆，則申其意於不已也。夫汲汲於趨公之役，又惓惓於享上之心，相勸以亟，相戒以預，其忠愛之意何如哉！嗟夫！此邠俗之舊，而公劉后稷之化，其王業之始基歟！成王周公之際，則固已彌文矣。稼穡艱難之事、君民相與之真、淳厚朴野之習，其不得而接於耳目者，有矇瞍朝夕之誦焉。於是周公之慮，盖深遠矣。

豈弟君子，民之父母。
倪天民
translation_en:
…without waiting for supervision or reprimand, they caution and admonish one another. How great their anxious diligence! Yet this is not all. They further consider that, in the month of the second yang, they must hew ice for their lord with resounding blows; in the month of the third yang, they must take the ice and store it in the icehouse. For early in the month of the fourth yang, their lord will offer a lamb and chives in sacrifice to the spirit presiding over cold, then open the icehouse, giving precedence to offerings in the ancestral temples. By the ninth month, the air has grown chill and frost descends; in the tenth month, they must hasten to finish their work on the threshing grounds. They then set out two jars of wine for a feast and slaughter sheep, including lambs, especially for the occasion. Bringing these, they ascend their lord’s hall, raise the rhinoceros-horn cup [?], and wish their lord long life. To wish him “ten thousand years” is to express the fullest possible number; to add “without limit” extends their intention without end. Eager to hasten to their lord’s service, and devoted in their desire to present offerings to their ruler, they urge one another to act promptly and admonish one another to prepare in advance. How great their loyalty and affection!

Ah! These were the old customs of Bin and the transforming influence of Gong Liu and Hou Ji. Were they not the first foundation of the royal enterprise? By the time of King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou, cultural refinement had already increased. The hardships of sowing and reaping, the sincerity of relations between ruler and people, and their honest, generous, simple, and rustic ways—whatever of these could no longer be encountered directly through eye and ear could still be heard in the blind musicians’ morning and evening recitations. In this, the Duke of Zhou’s foresight was indeed profound and far-reaching.

“The amiable and gracious gentleman is the father and mother of the people.”
Ni Tianmin

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭胡批此本康公戒成王之詩以豈
第望之塲中作者多背本旨此篇意氣舂容辭理平實深
得進戒之意允宜錄出
同考試官學正裘批詩千卷餘作者紛無定見晚
得此篇如獲明珠於瓦礫也用錄以破羣疑
考試官侍講彭批有勸戒微婉之意
考試官洗馬鄭批得旨
大臣之戒君惟欲其德有以子乎民也夫豈弟
者子民之德也爲人君者不有是德何以爲民
===
之父母哉昔召康公之戒成王如此意謂君人
之德莫貴乎豈弟也豈而和順從容藹然春陽
之可掬弟而易直子諒坦然大道之無陂所以
強敎之而陶吾民於德化者此也所以悅安之
而躋吾民於平康者此也夫然則可謂豈弟君
子矣豈弟之君子豈不爲民之父母乎夫父母
之於子有敎之之道焉今也胥誨胥告雖父母
之成其子者不越是矣非民之父母而何父母
之於子有養之之道焉今也以拊以畜雖父母
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭胡批：此本康公戒成王之詩，以豈第望之。塲中作者多背本旨，此篇意氣舂容，辭理平實，深得進戒之意，允宜錄出。

同考試官學正裘批：詩千卷餘，作者紛無定見。晚得此篇，如獲明珠於瓦礫也，用錄以破羣疑。

考試官侍講彭批：有勸戒微婉之意。

考試官洗馬鄭批：得旨。

大臣之戒君，惟欲其德有以子乎民也。夫豈弟者，子民之德也。爲人君者不有是德，何以爲民之父母哉？昔召康公之戒成王如此，意謂君人之德，莫貴乎豈弟也。豈而和順從容，藹然春陽之可掬；弟而易直子諒，坦然大道之無陂。所以強敎之而陶吾民於德化者，此也；所以悅安之而躋吾民於平康者，此也。夫然，則可謂豈弟君子矣。豈弟之君子，豈不爲民之父母乎？夫父母之於子，有敎之之道焉。今也胥誨胥告，雖父母之成其子者，不越是矣，非民之父母而何？父母之於子，有養之之道焉。今也以拊以畜，雖父母
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: This was originally a poem in which Duke Kang admonished King Cheng, expressing the hope that he would be joyful and kindly [?]. Most candidates in the examination hall departed from its original meaning. This essay is composed and unhurried in spirit, plain and sound in language and reasoning, and thoroughly grasps the intention of offering admonition. It certainly merits inclusion.

Associate Examiner Qiu, School Instructor, comments: Among more than a thousand papers on the Poetry [?], the writers were at odds, without a settled understanding. Finding this essay late in the process was like finding a luminous pearl among broken tiles and rubble. I have therefore selected it to dispel the many doubts.

Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: It conveys encouragement and admonition subtly and gently.

Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: It grasps the meaning.

When a great minister admonishes his ruler, he wishes only that the ruler possess the virtue needed to treat the people as his children. Joyfulness and kindliness are precisely the virtues by which one treats the people as one's children. If a ruler lacks these virtues, how can he be the father and mother of the people? Such was Duke Kang of Shao's admonition to King Cheng in former times. Its meaning was that, among the virtues of one who rules others, none is more precious than joyfulness and kindliness. Joyfulness makes him harmonious, compliant, and composed, with a warmth like spring sunlight that one could gather in one's hands; kindliness makes him amiable, upright, loving, and trustworthy, as level and open as a great road without unevenness. These are the qualities by which he diligently instructs our people and molds them through moral transformation; these are the qualities by which he brings them contentment and security and advances them toward peace and well-being. Thus he may indeed be called a joyful and kindly gentleman. Would not such a gentleman be the father and mother of the people? Parents have a way of teaching their children. Now he instructs and counsels all the people; even parents, in bringing their children to maturity, do no more than this. What, then, is he if not the father and mother of the people? Parents have a way of nurturing their children. Now he cherishes and sustains the people; even parents …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之字其子者不過是矣非民之父母而何民之
戴之亦豈不尊之如父愛之如母哉召公之於
成王其願幸之意深矣抑成王以幼冲之資撫
盈成之運於修德愛民之事或未之知也故召
公有卷阿之戒公劉之咏而此篇又以豈弟君
民言之此老臣忠愛之心也厥後成王果爲繼
體守成之令主而成鳧鷖旣醉之太平良有以
哉
春秋
===
晋侯入曹執曹伯畀宋人晋侯齊師宋
師秦師及楚人戰于城濮楚師敗績
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衞子莒
子盟于踐土並僖公二十八年
徐佑
同考試官訓導沈批能體傳意發揚明道不計功
之旨筆勢英偉超越衆作麟經魁選屬之子矣
考試官侍講彭批盡略浮豔之辭有得謹嚴之意
考試官洗馬鄭批文有斷制工得書法微意佳作也
punctuated:
之字其子者，不過是矣，非民之父母而何？民之戴之，亦豈不尊之如父、愛之如母哉？召公之於成王，其願幸之意深矣。抑成王以幼冲之資，撫盈成之運，於修德愛民之事，或未之知也。故召公有《卷阿》之戒、《公劉》之咏，而此篇又以豈弟君民言之，此老臣忠愛之心也。厥後成王果爲繼體守成之令主，而成《鳧鷖》《旣醉》之太平，良有以哉！
春秋
晋侯入曹，執曹伯，畀宋人。晋侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績。公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衞子、莒子，盟于踐土。並僖公二十八年。
徐佑
同考試官訓導沈批：能體傳意，發揚明道不計功之旨。筆勢英偉，超越衆作，麟經魁選屬之子矣。
考試官侍講彭批：盡略浮豔之辭，有得謹嚴之意。
考試官洗馬鄭批：文有斷制，工得書法微意，佳作也。
translation_en:
…in nurturing their children, do no more than this. How, then, could he be anything but the father and mother of the people? In upholding him, would the people not revere him as a father and love him as a mother? Duke Shao’s hopes for King Cheng were indeed profound. Yet King Cheng, being young and tender in years and presiding over an era of established prosperity, perhaps did not yet understand the cultivation of virtue and love for the people. Thus Duke Shao offered the admonition of “The Winding Mound” (Juan a) and the song of “Duke Liu” (Gong Liu), while this poem again speaks of being a kindly and amiable ruler of the people [?]. Such was this old minister’s loyal and loving heart. Thereafter King Cheng indeed became an excellent ruler who inherited the throne and preserved its achievements, bringing about the great peace celebrated in “Wild Ducks and Gulls” (Fu yi) and “Already Drunk” (Ji zui). Surely there was good reason for this!

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Marquis of Jin entered Cao, seized the Earl of Cao, and handed him over to the men of Song. The Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought against the men of Chu at Chengpu. The army of Chu suffered a crushing defeat. The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and they made a covenant at Jiantu. All these entries are from the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.

Xu You

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Assistant Instructor: He grasps the meaning of the commentary and develops its principle of illuminating the Way without calculating achievements. His writing is powerful and outstanding, surpassing the other compositions. First place in the Classic of the Unicorn—the Spring and Autumn Annals—belongs to this candidate!

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: He entirely dispenses with superficial, ornate language and captures the spirit of scrupulous rigor.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: The composition displays judgment and control, skillfully capturing the subtle meaning of the Annals’ manner of recording events. An excellent work.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
惟伯主虐内致外之事不可訓故伯主攘外服
内之功不足多此可見晋文以暴譎而成伯其
功雖多而道不足尚也春秋所以備書而致意
焉夫自齊功不續宋事無成荆楚益肆其憑陵
中國盖幾於左袵有晋文者出治曹而恤宋攘
楚而安夏亦春秋之深幸也何乃謂其功雖多
而道不足尚耶道不外乎仁而暴不可以言仁
也曹未狎政莫知所承公不脩辭令以撫曹而
遽入其國遂執其君暴矣暴而不仁於道何如
===
道不離乎正而譎不可以言正也楚方圍宋簡
書可畏公不仗大義以服楚而執曹畀宋怒楚
致師譎矣譎而不正於道又何如道既不足功
多何為故城濮之戰楚勢披靡若可以為功矣
然視諸仗義而執言聲罪以致討者不有間乎
揆之於道固仲尼之徒所羞稱也踐土之盟諸
侯景從宜可以言功矣然視諸以德而服人以
善而養人者不亦遠乎揆之於道固三王之世
所不容也春秋於入曹畀宋之役不以微辭諱
punctuated:
惟伯主虐内致外之事不可訓，故伯主攘外服内之功不足多。此可見晋文以暴譎而成伯，其功雖多，而道不足尚也。《春秋》所以備書而致意焉。夫自齊功不續，宋事無成，荆楚益肆其憑陵，中國盖幾於左袵。有晋文者出，治曹而恤宋，攘楚而安夏，亦《春秋》之深幸也。何乃謂其功雖多而道不足尚耶？道不外乎仁，而暴不可以言仁也。曹未狎政，莫知所承，公不脩辭令以撫曹，而遽入其國，遂執其君，暴矣！暴而不仁，於道何如？
