道不離乎正，而譎不可以言正也。楚方圍宋，簡書可畏，公不仗大義以服楚，而執曹畀宋，怒楚致師，譎矣！譎而不正，於道又何如？道既不足，功多何為？故城濮之戰，楚勢披靡，若可以為功矣。然視諸仗義而執言、聲罪以致討者，不有間乎？揆之於道，固仲尼之徒所羞稱也。踐土之盟，諸侯景從，宜可以言功矣。然視諸以德而服人、以善而養人者，不亦遠乎？揆之於道，固三王之世所不容也。《春秋》於入曹畀宋之役，不以微辭諱
translation_en:
Since a hegemon’s acts of oppressing states within the Chinese realm to provoke those outside it cannot serve as a model, his achievements in repelling outsiders and bringing the states within into submission do not deserve much praise. This shows that Duke Wen of Jin became hegemon through violence and deception: although his achievements were many, his way was unworthy of esteem. This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals records these matters fully and conveys its judgment through them. After Qi’s achievements ceased to be sustained and Song’s undertaking came to nothing, Jing-Chu grew ever more unrestrained in its aggression. The central states were almost reduced to wearing their robes fastened on the left, in the manner of outsiders. Then Duke Wen of Jin arose, chastised Cao and aided Song, repelled Chu and brought peace to the Chinese states. This, too, was a source of profound relief from the perspective of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why, then, say that although his achievements were many, his way was unworthy of esteem? The Way cannot be separated from benevolence, and violence cannot be called benevolent. Cao was not yet accustomed to its government, and its people did not know whose authority to follow [?]. The duke did not frame diplomatic communications to conciliate Cao, but abruptly invaded its territory and then seized its ruler. This was violence! Being violent and without benevolence, how did he measure up to the Way?

The Way cannot be separated from rectitude, and deception cannot be called upright. Chu was then besieging Song, and the written summons to military aid imposed an obligation to be taken seriously. The duke did not rely on the great principles of righteousness to bring Chu into submission. Instead, he seized Cao and handed it over to Song, provoking Chu into sending its army. This was deception! Being deceitful and without rectitude, how, again, did he measure up to the Way? If he fell short of the Way, what use were his many achievements? Thus, at the battle of Chengpu, Chu’s forces broke and fled: this might seem to count as an achievement. Yet was there not a difference between this and acting upon righteousness with a just cause, proclaiming an offender’s crimes and undertaking a punitive expedition? Measured against the Way, this was certainly something that the followers of Zhongni—Confucius—would be ashamed to praise. At the covenant of Jiantu, the regional lords followed him like shadows: this, surely, might be called an achievement. Yet was it not far removed from bringing people into submission through virtue and nurturing them through goodness? Measured against the Way, this was certainly something that would not have been tolerated in the age of the Three Kings. In its account of the campaign to invade Cao and hand it over to Song, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not conceal the matter through veiled wording…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而城濮踐土之文復以常辭書然則聖人明道
不計功之意可見矣抑觀文公戰城濮而盟踐
土伯業成矣由是休兵息民脩德行禮猶可以
救始事之失何踐土之盟血未乾又合諸侯以
會温城濮之大勞甫息又率諸侯以圍許禮煩
而威黷一盛而即衰矣吁此其所以為晋文也
歟
楚公子貞伐鄭襄公八年公會晋侯宋公衛
侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
===
子齊世子光伐鄭同盟于戲九年公會
晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世子
光滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭戍鄭
虎牢楚公子貞救鄭十年公會晋侯宋
公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭同盟于亳城
北公會晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子
光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐
鄭會于蕭魚十一年
punctuated:
而城濮、踐土之文，復以常辭書。然則聖人明道不計功之意可見矣。抑觀文公戰城濮而盟踐土，伯業成矣。由是休兵息民，脩德行禮，猶可以救始事之失。何踐土之盟血未乾，又合諸侯以會温；城濮之大勞甫息，又率諸侯以圍許？禮煩而威黷，一盛而即衰矣。吁！此其所以為晋文也歟？
楚公子貞伐鄭。襄公八年。
公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭，同盟于戲。九年。
公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，戍鄭虎牢。楚公子貞救鄭。十年。
公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，同盟于亳城北。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。十一年。
translation_en:
…Yet the entries concerning Chengpu and Jiantu are again recorded in ordinary language. Thus we can discern the Sage’s intention to clarify the Way without reckoning achievements. Consider further: when Duke Wen fought at Chengpu and concluded the covenant at Jiantu, his hegemony was established. Had he thereafter rested his troops, given the people respite, cultivated virtue, and practiced ritual propriety, he could still have remedied the errors of his initial undertakings. Why, before the blood of the covenant at Jiantu had dried, did he again assemble the feudal lords to meet at Wen? Why, when the great exertions at Chengpu had scarcely ended, did he again lead the feudal lords to besiege Xu? Ritual became burdensome, and the exercise of might excessive; no sooner had his power reached its height than it declined. Alas! Is this what made Duke Wen of Jin the man he was?
Prince Zhen of Chu attacked Zheng. Eighth year of Duke Xiang.
The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi 齊, in attacking Zheng. They jointly concluded a covenant at Xi. Ninth year.
The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They stationed a garrison at Hulao in Zheng. Prince Zhen of Chu came to Zheng’s aid. Tenth year.
The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They jointly concluded a covenant north of Bocheng. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. Eleventh year.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
呂傑
同考試官訓導沈批立論謹嚴而不遺傳註措詞
健順而自有準繩紛紛盆盎中有此古罍洗能不為之拭目
考試官侍講彭批就中提掇善言之從違為說
異於衆作
考試官洗馬鄭批辭嚴理正必熟於傳者
違嘉謀而致討者春秋示其譏從嘉謀而善勝
者春秋著其美此見鄭簡舍子展之言而不能
息爭晉悼行知罃之策而足以復伯也何則策
===
士謀臣天生賢以立國也善言嘉猷賢承天以
賛君也天之所命而君有從違焉則國之盛衰
隨見矣是故鄭之賢卿莫賢於子展當楚囊伐
鄭之日鄭伯欲從之際展也進言以决向背以
謂五會之信不可以違遼遠之師不能以久完
守而老楚仗信以待晉豈非謀之善哉使鄭簡
信而從之必無噬臍之悔矣何乃惑於子駟遂
及楚盟告絕之使方馳諸侯之師己集恐懼行
成而鄭之為鄭幾不能以國矣春秋之譏違善
punctuated:
呂傑

同考試官訓導沈批：立論謹嚴，而不遺傳註；措詞健順，而自有準繩。紛紛盆盎中有此古罍洗，能不為之拭目？

考試官侍講彭批：就中提掇善言之從違為說，異於衆作。

考試官洗馬鄭批：辭嚴理正，必熟於傳者。

違嘉謀而致討者，春秋示其譏；從嘉謀而善勝者，春秋著其美。此見鄭簡舍子展之言而不能息爭，晉悼行知罃之策而足以復伯也。何則？策士謀臣，天生賢以立國也；善言嘉猷，賢承天以賛君也。天之所命，而君有從違焉，則國之盛衰隨見矣。是故鄭之賢卿，莫賢於子展。當楚囊伐鄭之日，鄭伯欲從之際，展也進言以决向背，以謂五會之信不可以違，遼遠之師不能以久，完守而老楚，仗信以待晉，豈非謀之善哉？使鄭簡信而從之，必無噬臍之悔矣。何乃惑於子駟，遂及楚盟？告絕之使方馳，諸侯之師己集，恐懼行成，而鄭之為鄭，幾不能以國矣。春秋之譏，違善
translation_en:
Lü Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: The argument is careful and rigorous, yet neglects nothing in the commentaries and annotations; the wording is vigorous and fluent, yet observes its own standards. Amid a jumble of ordinary bowls and jars, here are ancient ritual vessels—a lei wine jar and a xi basin. How could one fail to rub one’s eyes in admiration?

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: From this material he singles out the acceptance or rejection of sound counsel as the basis of his argument, distinguishing it from the other essays.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: The language is rigorous and the reasoning correct. He must be thoroughly familiar with the commentaries.

For those who reject good counsel and thereby bring punitive attack upon themselves, the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses censure; for those who follow good counsel and achieve victory skillfully, it records praise. This shows how Duke Jian of Zheng, discarding Zizhan’s advice, could not put an end to conflict, whereas Duke Dao of Jin, implementing Zhi Ying’s strategy, was able to restore his hegemony. Why is this? Strategists and counselors are worthy men whom Heaven brings forth to establish states; sound advice and excellent plans are the means by which worthy men serve Heaven and assist their rulers. Whether rulers follow or reject what Heaven has ordained, the flourishing or decline of their states becomes apparent accordingly.

Thus, among Zheng’s worthy ministers, none was worthier than Zizhan. When Nang of Chu attacked Zheng, and the Earl of Zheng was about to submit to him, Zizhan offered advice to settle which side Zheng should support. He argued that the pledges made at five meetings could not be broken, and that an army far from home could not remain long: maintain the defenses intact and wear down Chu, and uphold good faith while awaiting Jin. Was this not excellent counsel? Had Duke Jian of Zheng trusted and followed it, he would surely have avoided the regret of biting his own navel—regret that comes too late. Why, then, was he misled by Zisi and consequently entered into a covenant with Chu? His envoy announcing the severance of relations had only just set off when the armies of the feudal lords had already assembled. In fear, he sought peace, and Zheng, as a state, could scarcely continue to exist. The censure in the Spring and Autumn Annals is a warning against rejecting sound …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
言之戒也若夫晋之賢佐莫賢於知罃當肆眚
圍鄭之時荀偃决戰之頃罃也獻策以陳利害
以謂暴骨以逞則克不可命以逸待勞則楚不
能争許盟還師以敝乎楚分軍率銳以逆其来
豈非謀之善哉使悼公忽而違之則失善勝之
道矣然而寧違荀偃卒許鄭成三駕示威楚不
戰而自屈一會推誠鄭心服而不叛従容得志
而晋之為伯盛莫越於此矣春秋之美用善言
之效也吁鄭之事無足論矣従嘉謀而成伯功
===
豈惟悼公為然齊桓創伯甞従管仲之諫以懷
鄭晋文繼伯甞従先軫之謀以克楚昔之英君
明辟以善言而興事建勲者多矣雖然發言盈
庭誰執其咎非知言之君子其孰能擇於斯
禮記
天子七廟諸侯五大夫三士一天子之豆
二十有六諸公十有六諸侯十有二上
大夫八下大夫六
盧幹
punctuated:
言之戒也。若夫晋之賢佐，莫賢於知罃。當肆眚圍鄭之時，荀偃决戰之頃，罃也獻策以陳利害，以謂暴骨以逞，則克不可命；以逸待勞，則楚不能争。許盟還師以敝乎楚，分軍率銳以逆其来，豈非謀之善哉？使悼公忽而違之，則失善勝之道矣。然而寧違荀偃，卒許鄭成。三駕示威，楚不戰而自屈；一會推誠，鄭心服而不叛。従容得志，而晋之為伯，盛莫越於此矣。《春秋》之美，用善言之效也。吁！鄭之事無足論矣。従嘉謀而成伯功，豈惟悼公為然？齊桓創伯，甞従管仲之諫以懷鄭；晋文繼伯，甞従先軫之謀以克楚。昔之英君明辟，以善言而興事建勲者多矣。雖然，「發言盈庭，誰執其咎？」非知言之君子，其孰能擇於斯？

禮記
天子七廟，諸侯五，大夫三，士一。天子之豆二十有六，諸公十有六，諸侯十有二，上大夫八，下大夫六。

盧幹
translation_en:
…a warning against rejecting sound counsel. As for the worthy advisers of Jin, none was worthier than Zhi Ying. When an amnesty was proclaimed and Zheng was besieged, and Xun Yan resolved to fight, Ying offered a plan explaining the advantages and dangers. He argued that if they exposed their soldiers’ bones merely to gratify their ambitions, victory could not be assured; but if they awaited an exhausted enemy with rested troops, Chu could not contend with them. To accept a covenant and withdraw the army so as to wear down Chu, then divide their forces and lead picked troops to meet its advance—was this not an excellent plan? Had Duke Dao disregarded and rejected it, he would have lost the means of securing victory through sound strategy. Instead, he chose to go against Xun Yan and ultimately granted Zheng peace. Three expeditions displayed his might, and Chu yielded without fighting; at a single meeting he showed his sincerity, and Zheng submitted wholeheartedly and did not rebel. He achieved his aims with ease, and Jin’s hegemony never flourished more greatly than at this time. The praise accorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals reflects the results of heeding sound counsel.

Ah! Zheng’s conduct scarcely merits further discussion. Was Duke Dao alone in achieving hegemony by following good advice? When Duke Huan of Qi first established his hegemony, he followed Guan Zhong’s remonstrance to win Zheng over. When Duke Wen of Jin succeeded to the hegemony, he followed Xian Zhen’s plan to defeat Chu. Many outstanding rulers and enlightened sovereigns of antiquity accomplished great undertakings and won distinction through sound counsel. Yet, “Words fill the court; who will take responsibility for their consequences?” Who but a gentleman capable of discerning the worth of words could choose among them?

Record of Rites
The Son of Heaven has seven ancestral temples; the feudal lords, five; the grandees, three; and the servicemen, one. The Son of Heaven has twenty-six pedestal dishes; the dukes, sixteen; the feudal lords, twelve; the senior grandees, eight; and the junior grandees, six.

Lu Gan

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭蕭批此題論廟豆之數見禮有以
多爲貴作者盖知之詞理俱到不泛不畧如此篇者則亦不
多得也
考試官侍講彭批器數儀節之間禮家所謹此
能悉之
考試官洗馬鄭批敷析詳明
隨其分而制廟豆之數此禮之以多爲貴也盖
禮莫大於分也先王制廟豆之數得不各隨其
尊卑而爲之等殺也哉記禮器者謂先王之制
===
禮有以多爲貴者以廟制言之廟所以祀先也
而天子諸侯大夫士之廟有差等焉是故天子
則三昭三穆與太祖之廟而七也諸侯則二昭
二穆與太祖之廟而五也大夫則一昭一穆與
太祖之廟而三焉下士則無昭無穆而祖禰共
一廟焉所以然者由尊而卑爲之差等耳其獨
隆於天子者非特以誠深孝篤而然盖不如是
無以致尊祖之義盡親親之仁也禮之見於廟
制者如此以豆數言之豆所以薦羞也而天子
punctuated:
同考試官教諭蕭批：此題論廟豆之數，見禮有以多爲貴。作者盖知之，詞理俱到，不泛不畧，如此篇者則亦不多得也。
考試官侍講彭批：器數儀節之間，禮家所謹，此能悉之。
考試官洗馬鄭批：敷析詳明。
隨其分而制廟豆之數，此禮之以多爲貴也。盖禮莫大於分也，先王制廟豆之數，得不各隨其尊卑而爲之等殺也哉？記《禮器》者謂先王之制禮，有以多爲貴者。以廟制言之，廟所以祀先也，而天子、諸侯、大夫、士之廟有差等焉。是故天子則三昭三穆與太祖之廟而七也；諸侯則二昭二穆與太祖之廟而五也；大夫則一昭一穆與太祖之廟而三焉；下士則無昭無穆，而祖禰共一廟焉。所以然者，由尊而卑爲之差等耳。其獨隆於天子者，非特以誠深孝篤而然，盖不如是，無以致尊祖之義，盡親親之仁也。禮之見於廟制者如此。以豆數言之，豆所以薦羞也，而天子
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: This topic discusses the numbers of ancestral temples and dou offering vessels, showing that in ritual there are instances in which greater numbers are esteemed. The author evidently understands this. Both expression and reasoning are fully developed, neither vague nor cursory. Essays such as this are seldom found.
Comment by Examiner Peng, Hanlin Reader-in-waiting: The numbers of ritual vessels and the forms of ceremonial observance are matters that specialists in ritual treat with care. This essay comprehensively explains them.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: The exposition and analysis are detailed and clear.
To determine the numbers of ancestral temples and dou offering vessels according to each person's allotted rank is an instance of ritual esteeming greater numbers. In ritual, nothing is more important than distinctions of rank. When the former kings determined the numbers of temples and offering vessels, could they have failed to establish graduated differences according to each person's higher or lower standing? The author of “Ritual Vessels” states that, in the former kings' establishment of ritual, there were instances in which greater numbers were esteemed. Consider the system of ancestral temples. Temples serve to offer sacrifices to ancestors, and there are graded differences in the temples allotted to the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords, the great officers, and the servicemen. Thus, the Son of Heaven has three temples of the zhao generation and three of the mu generation, together with the temple of the founding ancestor, making seven. The feudal lords have two zhao and two mu temples, together with the temple of the founding ancestor, making five. The great officers have one zhao and one mu temple, together with the temple of the founding ancestor, making three. Lower servicemen have neither separate zhao nor separate mu temples; grandfather and father share a single temple. The reason for this is simply to establish gradations from the most exalted to the lowliest. That the Son of Heaven alone receives the fullest provision is not merely because his sincerity is profound and his filial devotion earnest. Without this provision, he could not fully realize the duty of honoring ancestors or fulfill the benevolence of loving one's kin. Such is ritual as manifested in the system of ancestral temples. As for the numbers of dou vessels, these serve to present offerings of food, and the Son of Heaven …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
公侯大夫之豆亦有隆殺焉是故天子朔食之
豆二十有六則朝踐八饋食八加豆八羞豆二
也諸公相朝堂上之豆十有六則朝事八而無
加豆饋食八而無羞豆也諸侯相朝堂上之豆
則朝事六饋食六凡十有二焉主國食使臣之
豆則上大夫八下大夫六焉所以然者亦惟自
尊而卑為之隆殺耳具獨尊於天子者非特以
備味多品而然盖不如是無以極九州之美備
四時之和也禮之見於豆數者又如此吁以分
===
之尊卑爲數之多寡先王制禮之意不其至歟
大抵禮所以辨上下而定民志也故先王縁情
以制宜随宜以爲貴或多或寡各當其位而不
相紊各稱其情而不相悖不然則尊卑無序貴
賤無等而上下不相安其何以致天下之治哉
故曰安上治民莫善於禮
子民如父母有憯怛之愛有忠利之教親
而尊安而敬威而愛富而有禮惠而能
散
punctuated:
公侯大夫之豆亦有隆殺焉。是故天子朔食之豆二十有六，則朝踐八、饋食八、加豆八、羞豆二也。諸公相朝堂上之豆十有六，則朝事八而無加豆，饋食八而無羞豆也。諸侯相朝堂上之豆，則朝事六、饋食六，凡十有二焉。主國食使臣之豆，則上大夫八、下大夫六焉。所以然者，亦惟自尊而卑為之隆殺耳。具獨尊於天子者，非特以備味多品而然，盖不如是，無以極九州之美、備四時之和也。禮之見於豆數者又如此。吁！以分之尊卑爲數之多寡，先王制禮之意，不其至歟！大抵禮所以辨上下而定民志也。故先王縁情以制宜，随宜以爲貴，或多或寡，各當其位而不相紊，各稱其情而不相悖。不然，則尊卑無序，貴賤無等，而上下不相安，其何以致天下之治哉？故曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮。」

子民如父母，有憯怛之愛，有忠利之教，親而尊，安而敬，威而愛，富而有禮，惠而能散。
translation_en:
…the dou vessels of dukes, marquises, and grand masters likewise vary in number according to rank. Thus, the Son of Heaven has twenty-six dou vessels for his meal on the first day of the month: eight for the morning presentation, eight for the food offering, eight additional vessels, and two for delicacies. When dukes pay court visits to one another, there are sixteen dou vessels in the hall: eight for the morning service, without additional vessels, and eight for the food offering, without vessels for delicacies. When the feudal lords pay court visits to one another, the dou vessels in the hall comprise six for the morning service and six for the food offering, twelve in all. When a host state entertains an envoy, there are eight dou vessels for a senior grand master and six for a junior grand master. The reason for this, too, is simply to establish graded quantities descending from higher to lower rank. The special preeminence accorded to the Son of Heaven [?] is not merely a matter of providing a full range of flavors and numerous dishes. Without this, there would be no way to bring together the finest produce of the Nine Provinces and provide the harmonious flavors of all four seasons. Such, again, is how ritual is manifested in the number of dou vessels. Ah! To determine greater or smaller quantities according to higher or lower status—was not the intention of the former kings in establishing ritual most perfect?

In general, ritual serves to distinguish superiors from inferiors and to settle the people's aspirations. Thus, the former kings established fitting arrangements in accordance with human feelings and esteemed what suited the circumstances. Whether the quantities were greater or smaller, each accorded with its proper station without confusion, and each suited the feelings involved without conflict. Otherwise, higher and lower ranks would lack order, the noble and the humble would lack distinctions, and superiors and inferiors would not dwell together in peace. How, then, could order be brought to the realm? Hence the saying: “For securing those above and governing the people, nothing excels ritual.”

Care for the people as your children, as their father and mother, with deeply compassionate love and instruction that is devoted to their welfare: be affectionate yet dignified, at ease yet reverent, imposing yet loving, wealthy yet observant of ritual, benevolent and ready to distribute your resources.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
方榮
同考試官教諭蕭批表記此題傳註明白作者臆
說紛紛令人厭觀此卷體認真切發明教養之道通貫
無遺非熟於禮者不能本房之冠舍子其誰
考試官侍講彭批文意通貫
考試官洗馬鄭批辭暢而理亦足可取
聖人論聖君之子民盡教養之道而無偏也盖
教養兼盡而無偏子民之道也此聖君所以能
盡乎仁也歟昔吾夫子論君道之難於盡仁而
===
及此謂夫虞舜之君天下也心乎斯民猶父母
之於子而教養之兼盡焉以言其養則慘怛之
心發於至誠真猶母之愛其子也如拯民於洪
水之災洽民于好生之德非責報於人非要譽
於衆其養之盡其道也何如以言其教則忠利
之道本乎實心真猶父之教其子也如命官以
教人倫制器以利民用有教人以善之實有通
變宜民之功其教之盡其道也又何如惟其愛
也則有以致其親而和之於內豈不猶母之親
punctuated:
方榮

同考試官教諭蕭批：「《表記》此題，傳註明白，作者臆說紛紛，令人厭觀。此卷體認真切，發明教養之道，通貫無遺。非熟於禮者不能。本房之冠，舍子其誰？」
考試官侍講彭批：「文意通貫。」
考試官洗馬鄭批：「辭暢而理亦足，可取。」

聖人論聖君之子民，盡教養之道而無偏也。盖教養兼盡而無偏，子民之道也。此聖君所以能盡乎仁也歟！昔吾夫子論君道之難於盡仁，而及此，謂夫虞舜之君天下也，心乎斯民，猶父母之於子，而教養之兼盡焉。以言其養，則慘怛之心發於至誠，真猶母之愛其子也。如拯民於洪水之災，洽民于好生之德，非責報於人，非要譽於衆，其養之盡其道也何如！以言其教，則忠利之道本乎實心，真猶父之教其子也。如命官以教人倫，制器以利民用，有教人以善之實，有通變宜民之功，其教之盡其道也又何如！惟其愛也，則有以致其親，而和之於內，豈不猶母之親
translation_en:
Fang Rong

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “For this topic from ‘The Record of Exemplary Conduct’ (Biaoji), the commentaries and annotations are clear. Yet writers offer a profusion of conjectural explanations that make tiresome reading. This paper shows a genuine and penetrating understanding, elucidating the way of instructing and nurturing the people comprehensively, without omission. Only someone thoroughly versed in ritual could accomplish this. Who but you could rank first in this examining room?”
Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: “The ideas are coherent throughout.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Editorial Director: “The language flows freely, and the reasoning is also adequate. Worth accepting.”

The sage discusses how a sage ruler treats the people as his children, fully carrying out both instruction and nurture without partiality toward either. For fulfilling both instruction and nurture without partiality is the way to treat the people as one’s children. Is this not how the sage ruler fully realizes benevolence? When our Master once discussed how difficult it is to fulfill benevolence completely in the way of rulership, he came to this point. He meant that when Shun of Yu ruled all under Heaven, his concern for the people was like that of parents for their children, and he fully provided both instruction and nurture.

As for his nurture, his compassionate heart arose from the utmost sincerity, truly like a mother’s love for her child. Thus he rescued the people from the calamity of the great flood and suffused them with his virtue of cherishing life. He neither demanded repayment from others nor sought praise from the multitude. How completely he fulfilled the way of nurturing them!

As for his instruction, his faithful devotion to their benefit was rooted in a sincere heart, truly like a father’s instruction of his child. Thus he appointed officials to teach human relationships and fashioned implements to serve the people’s needs. There was the substance of teaching people goodness, and the achievement of adapting to change for the people’s benefit. How completely, too, he fulfilled the way of instructing them!

Precisely through his love, he could bring about their affection and foster harmony within them. Was this not like a mother’s affection…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乎惟其教也則有以致其尊而率之於外豈不
猶父之尊乎親而有所尊則和靖以安而莊敬
之心于焉而存尊而有所親則德威惟威而慈
愛之念于焉而著安而敬則富而能節於物而
驕奢之患無有焉威而愛則惠而能周於物而
偏黨之私無有焉吁尊親兼盡教養無偏此有
虞聖人所以能用中於民而盡君道之仁也歟
抑考表記此章言君道之難於盡仁惟舜可以
爲德之至然此言愛教之事特舜之粗迹耳果
===
極致乎下文言君子化之皆爲全德特舜之德
廣耳果聖人之道化止於君子而已哉讀者詳
之
第貳場
論
聖人太極之全體
楊本清
同考試官訓導沈批論場欲觀士子性理實學
作者類為浮泛之辭無所發明惟是作議論精明文章醇
punctuated:
乎？惟其教也，則有以致其尊而率之於外，豈不猶父之尊乎？親而有所尊，則和靖以安，而莊敬之心于焉而存；尊而有所親，則德威惟威，而慈愛之念于焉而著。安而敬，則富而能節於物，而驕奢之患無有焉；威而愛，則惠而能周於物，而偏黨之私無有焉。吁！尊親兼盡，教養無偏，此有虞聖人所以能用中於民而盡君道之仁也歟！抑考《表記》，此章言君道之難於盡仁，惟舜可以爲德之至。然此言愛教之事，特舜之粗迹耳，果極致乎？下文言君子化之，皆爲全德，特舜之德廣耳，果聖人之道化止於君子而已哉？讀者詳之。

第貳場
論
聖人太極之全體
楊本清

同考試官訓導沈批：論場欲觀士子性理實學，作者類為浮泛之辭，無所發明。惟是作議論精明，文章醇
translation_en:
…for a mother? Through his teaching, he could elicit their reverence and guide their outward conduct: was this not like the reverence accorded a father? When affection includes reverence, there is harmony, tranquility, and security, while a solemn and respectful disposition remains. When reverence includes affection, virtue itself inspires awe, while thoughts of kindness and love become manifest. With security and respect, there can be wealth accompanied by restraint in material things, without the evils of arrogance and extravagance. With awe and love, generosity can extend to all, without the selfishness of favoritism. Ah! Bringing both reverence and affection to fulfillment, and neglecting neither teaching nor nurture—was this not how the sage of Youyu could apply the mean to the people and fully realize the benevolence proper to rulership?

Yet consider the chapter “Record of Exemplary Conduct” in the Book of Rites. This passage speaks of the difficulty a ruler faces in fully realizing benevolence; only Shun may be said to have attained the utmost virtue. But the acts of love and teaching mentioned here are merely the outward traces of Shun’s conduct. Do they really constitute its highest attainment? The following passage says that the noble men were transformed by him and all attained complete virtue. This merely shows the breadth of Shun’s virtue. Could the transforming influence of the sage’s Way really have extended only to noble men? Readers should consider this carefully.

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage Embodies the Great Ultimate in Its Entirety”
Yang Benqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Assistant Instructor: The discourse session is intended to reveal the candidates’ substantive learning concerning human nature and principle. Writers generally produce vague and superficial language, elucidating nothing. This composition alone offers incisive and clear argument, and its prose is pure…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
古盖嘗潜心濂溪考亭之學者歟
考試官侍講彭批作論者驁於誇多鬪靡之習
簡切如此者亦未必不佳也
考試官洗馬鄭批理學精深非可臆說此作見
理明白措辭醇正其積學之士乎宜在優選
論曰太極者何陰陽之道也陰陽者何動静之
迹也聖人者何人之至而天地之參也聖人所
以參天地而成位乎中者全動静之德一太極
之本然而已盖自上天之載而言之則所謂造
===
化之樞紐品彙之根柢者此太極也自其在人
而言之則中正仁義所謂天之命人之性動静
之德者聖人固無毫髮之不盡而亦豈能有毫
髮之加哉是之謂太極之全體盖嘗觀於穹壤
之間矣何者而非太極之所形何者而非太極
之所妙形者其氣之著也妙者其理之所以然
也真精之合而萬物化生靈秀所鍾而在人獨
異故曰中曰正曰仁曰義
凡黔首之輩靡不全然中正仁義雖曰稟賦未
punctuated:
古，盖嘗潜心濂溪、考亭之學者歟？
考試官侍講彭批：作論者驁於誇多鬪靡之習，簡切如此者亦未必不佳也。
考試官洗馬鄭批：理學精深，非可臆說。此作見理明白，措辭醇正，其積學之士乎？宜在優選。
論曰：太極者何？陰陽之道也。陰陽者何？動静之迹也。聖人者何？人之至而天地之參也。聖人所以參天地而成位乎中者，全動静之德，一太極之本然而已。盖自上天之載而言之，則所謂造化之樞紐、品彙之根柢者，此太極也。自其在人而言之，則中正仁義，所謂天之命、人之性、動静之德者，聖人固無毫髮之不盡，而亦豈能有毫髮之加哉？是之謂太極之全體。盖嘗觀於穹壤之間矣，何者而非太極之所形？何者而非太極之所妙？形者，其氣之著也；妙者，其理之所以然也。真精之合而萬物化生，靈秀所鍾而在人獨異，故曰中、曰正、曰仁、曰義。
凡黔首之輩，靡不全然。中正仁義，雖曰稟賦未
translation_en:
…classical in style. Surely the author has devoted himself to the learning of Lianxi [Zhou Dunyi] and Kaoting [Zhu Xi]?
Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: Writers of discourses are given to vaunting [?] their profusion of words and competing in ornate expression. A piece as concise and pertinent as this may well have its merits.
Examiner Zheng, Palace Librarian, comments: The learning of principle is profound and cannot be expounded through conjecture. This piece shows a clear understanding of principle, and its wording is sound and correct. Is its author not a scholar of accumulated learning? It deserves a place among the superior selections.
The discourse reads: What is the Supreme Ultimate? It is the Way of yin and yang. What are yin and yang? They are the traces of activity and stillness. What is a sage? The utmost perfection of humanity, forming a triad with Heaven and Earth. What enables the sage to form this triad with Heaven and Earth and take his place between them is simply that he fully embodies the virtues of activity and stillness and is one with the inherent reality of the Supreme Ultimate. Speaking in terms of the workings of Heaven above, what is called the pivot of transformation and the root of all kinds of things is this Supreme Ultimate. Speaking in terms of its presence in human beings, it is centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness—what are called Heaven’s mandate, human nature, and the virtues of activity and stillness. The sage assuredly realizes these without the slightest omission; yet how could he add even the slightest thing to them? This is what is meant by the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety. I have contemplated what lies between heaven and earth: what is there that is not a manifestation of the Supreme Ultimate? What is there in which its wondrous operation is absent? Manifestation is the evident expression of its vital energy; wondrous operation is the principle whereby it is so. Through the union of the true and the vital essences, the myriad things are generated through transformation. Spiritual potency and refinement converge uniquely in human beings. Hence we speak of centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness.
Among the common people, there is none who does not possess these in full. As for centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, although it is said that their endowment has not …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
嘗不同也而不能不奪於情偽之相感利害之
相攻中或失於偏倚正或失於邪回仁或至於
殘忍義或至於無耻支離决裂而違太極遠矣
况可謂太極之全體乎雖曰性分未有不兼也
然清濁之相揉純駁之相雜或正也而未必得
於中或仁也而未必諧於義虧欠間隔而於太
極之本然有不完矣又可謂太極之全體乎惟
聖人得夫秀而秀者其行之也中其處之也正
不假脩為而從容乎中道其發之也仁其裁之
===
也義不待勉强而自然其無疵故太極動而生
陽則誠之通也繼之者善也元亨之德也萬物
之所資以始也而聖人之動而為仁為中者以
之太極靜而生陰則誠之復也成之者性也利
貞之德也萬物之所以各正性命也而聖人之
靜而為義為正者以之萬物體統一太極是太
極無一物而不包而聖人渾然一理之具於心
者非太極之全體乎一物各具一太極是太極
無一物之不在而聖人泛應曲當之見於用者
punctuated: 嘗不同也，而不能不奪於情偽之相感、利害之相攻，中或失於偏倚，正或失於邪回，仁或至於殘忍，義或至於無耻，支離决裂，而違太極遠矣。况可謂太極之全體乎？雖曰性分未有不兼也，然清濁之相揉、純駁之相雜，或正也而未必得於中，或仁也而未必諧於義，虧欠間隔，而於太極之本然有不完矣。又可謂太極之全體乎？惟聖人得夫秀而秀者，其行之也中，其處之也正，不假脩為而從容乎中道；其發之也仁，其裁之也義，不待勉强而自然其無疵。故太極動而生陽，則誠之通也，繼之者善也，元亨之德也，萬物之所資以始也，而聖人之動而為仁為中者以之。太極靜而生陰，則誠之復也，成之者性也，利貞之德也，萬物之所以各正性命也，而聖人之靜而為義為正者以之。萬物體統一太極，是太極無一物而不包，而聖人渾然一理之具於心者，非太極之全體乎？一物各具一太極，是太極無一物之不在，而聖人泛應曲當之見於用者
translation_en:
…have never differed, yet they cannot avoid being overpowered by the interplay of genuine and false feelings and the clash of benefit and harm. Centrality may lapse into partiality, correctness into perversity, benevolence into cruelty, and righteousness into shamelessness. Fragmented and torn apart, they depart far from the Supreme Ultimate. How, then, could they be called the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety? Although none lacks any of these qualities within the endowment of human nature, the clear and turbid mingle, and the pure and impure intermingle. Thus one may be correct without necessarily attaining centrality, or benevolent without necessarily according with righteousness. Through deficiencies and divisions, the original condition of the Supreme Ultimate is incompletely realized. How, again, could this be called the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety?

Only the sage receives the finest of the finest essence. In action he is central; in his disposition he is correct. Without relying on cultivation, he moves at ease along the central Way. In his expression he is benevolent; in his judgments he is righteous. Without awaiting deliberate effort, he is naturally without flaw. Thus, when the Supreme Ultimate moves and generates yang, this is the unfolding of sincerity; what continues it is goodness. These are the virtues of origination and flourishing, upon which the myriad things depend for their beginnings; and this is what the sage follows when, in movement, he manifests benevolence and centrality. When the Supreme Ultimate is still and generates yin, this is the return of sincerity; what completes it is nature. These are the virtues of benefit and constancy, through which the myriad things each attain their proper nature and allotted destiny; and this is what the sage follows when, in stillness, he manifests righteousness and correctness.

The myriad things, taken as a whole, are one Supreme Ultimate: thus there is nothing that the Supreme Ultimate does not encompass. Is not the one principle, present as an undivided whole in the sage’s mind, the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety? Each individual thing possesses a Supreme Ultimate in its entirety: thus there is nothing in which the Supreme Ultimate is absent. And the sage’s responding to all things and fitting each particular circumstance, as manifested in his functioning…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
又非太極之全體乎中也仁也而太極之用以
行正也義也而太極之體以立由是而有以一
天下之動由是而有以立斯人之極所以與天
地合其德日月合其明四時合其序鬼神合其
吉凶首出庶物而為人之至也歟是知陰陽成
象而天道立矣天一太極也剛柔成質而地道
立矣地一太極也仁義成德而人道立矣聖人
一太極也天地聖人雖三才之不同其實一太
極而已噫聖人合動靜之德故為太極之全體
===
其未至於聖人者夫何如曰脩之而已脩之何
如曰持敬寡欲而已寡之又寡以至於無則靜
虛動直而聖可學矣雖然此非愚之言也考亭
之論也濂溪周子之意也
表
擬
詔加崇闕里釋奠禮樂衍聖公謝表
蕭瓛
同考試官教諭胡批表得體
punctuated:
又非太極之全體乎？中也，仁也，而太極之用以行；正也，義也，而太極之體以立。由是而有以一天下之動，由是而有以立斯人之極，所以與天地合其德，日月合其明，四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶，首出庶物而為人之至也歟！是知陰陽成象而天道立矣，天一太極也；剛柔成質而地道立矣，地一太極也；仁義成德而人道立矣，聖人一太極也。天地聖人，雖三才之不同，其實一太極而已。噫！聖人合動靜之德，故為太極之全體。其未至於聖人者，夫何如？曰：「脩之而已。」脩之何如？曰：「持敬寡欲而已。」寡之又寡，以至於無，則靜虛動直，而聖可學矣。雖然，此非愚之言也，考亭之論也，濂溪周子之意也。

表

擬詔加崇闕里釋奠禮樂衍聖公謝表

蕭瓛

同考試官教諭胡批：「表得體。」
translation_en:
…is this not also the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate? Through centrality and benevolence, the functioning of the Supreme Ultimate proceeds; through correctness and righteousness, its substance is established. Through these, the sage can unify all activity under Heaven and establish the ultimate standard for humankind. Thus his virtue accords with Heaven and Earth, his brightness with the sun and moon, his ordering with the four seasons, and his good and ill fortune with the spirits. He stands foremost among all beings and is the utmost realization of humanity!

From this we know that yin and yang form images, and the Way of Heaven is established: Heaven is one Supreme Ultimate. The hard and soft form material substance, and the Way of Earth is established: Earth is one Supreme Ultimate. Benevolence and righteousness constitute virtue, and the human Way is established: the sage is one Supreme Ultimate. Though Heaven, Earth, and the sage differ as the Three Powers, in reality they are simply one Supreme Ultimate. Ah! The sage unites the virtues of activity and stillness and thus embodies the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate. What, then, should those who have not yet attained sagehood do? The answer is: “Simply cultivate themselves.” How should they cultivate themselves? The answer is: “Simply maintain reverence and diminish desires.” Diminish them again and again until none remain; then one will be empty in stillness and upright in activity, and sagehood can be learned. Yet these are not my humble words: they are the arguments of Kaoting (Zhu Xi) and the meaning intended by Master Zhou of Lianxi (Zhou Dunyi).

Memorial

Draft memorial of thanks by the Duke for Perpetuating the Sage, on an imperial edict enhancing the rites and music of the offering ceremony to Confucius at Queli.

By Xiao Huan 蕭瓛.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: “The memorial conforms to the proper form.”

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正裘批駢儷可觀
考試官侍講彭批作儷語而有渾成意表如是可已
考試官洗馬鄭批典則可嘉
臣某言伏蒙
聖恩遣官祭告闕里加崇釋奠禮樂者伏以
端己無爲丕闡右文之至治自
天有命肅昭崇德之盛儀洙泗增輝雲仍動色
臣惶懼惶懼頓首頓首竊惟闕里有太牢
之祠肇於前漢辟雝用六羽之獻昉自盛
===
唐自是以還每致其意厥名暨物與次俱
升然近代於章服已崇而釋奠之禮樂猶
殺隆文異數盖有待於
聖明重道尊師示莫加於今昔建白雖由於臣
下施行一斷於
宸衷損益稱情從違協志豆籩登薦上同
郊社之規羽籥在陳非復王侯之制聲容斯備
氣象一新兹盖伏遇
皇帝陛下
punctuated:
同考試官學正裘批：駢儷可觀。
考試官侍講彭批：作儷語而有渾成意，表如是可已。
考試官洗馬鄭批：典則可嘉。
臣某言：伏蒙聖恩，遣官祭告闕里，加崇釋奠禮樂者。伏以端己無爲，丕闡右文之至治；自天有命，肅昭崇德之盛儀。洙泗增輝，雲仍動色。臣惶懼惶懼，頓首頓首。竊惟闕里有太牢之祠，肇於前漢；辟雝用六羽之獻，昉自盛唐。自是以還，每致其意，厥名暨物，與次俱升。然近代於章服已崇，而釋奠之禮樂猶殺。隆文異數，盖有待於聖明。重道尊師，示莫加於今昔。建白雖由於臣下，施行一斷於宸衷。損益稱情，從違協志。豆籩登薦，上同郊社之規；羽籥在陳，非復王侯之制。聲容斯備，氣象一新。兹盖伏遇皇帝陛下，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Qiu, School Instructor, comments: “The parallel prose is worthy of admiration.”
Examiner Peng, Expositor-in-Waiting, comments: “The parallel phrasing conveys a naturally integrated meaning. A memorial composed thus is satisfactory.”
Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: “Its adherence to classical standards merits praise.”
Your servant, So-and-so, states: I have humbly received Your sacred favor in dispatching an official to announce through sacrifice at Queli the enhancement of the rites and music of the Offering to the Sage. I respectfully reflect that, by holding Yourself upright and governing without exertion, You have greatly manifested consummate governance that honors cultural learning; a command has come from Heaven, solemnly displaying splendid ceremonies that exalt virtue. The Zhu and Si rivers shine with added glory, and the Sage’s distant descendants are visibly moved. Your servant trembles in fear, trembles in fear, and knocks his head upon the ground, knocks his head upon the ground.
I humbly consider that sacrifices at Queli using the full complement of ox, sheep, and pig began in the Former Han; the performance of offerings with six ranks of feather-bearing dancers in the Imperial Academy began in the flourishing Tang. From that time onward, successive rulers devoted their attention to these matters, and both ceremonial designations and material provisions were progressively elevated. Yet in recent times, although ceremonial robes had already been accorded greater honor, the rites and music of the Offering to the Sage remained on a reduced scale. Enhanced ceremonial forms and exceptional distinctions evidently awaited Your enlightened sagacity. In honoring the Way and venerating the teacher, Your example is unsurpassed, past or present. Although the proposal came from Your servants below, its implementation rested entirely upon Your imperial decision. Additions and reductions fittingly express reverence; acceptance and rejection accord with Your intent. The offerings presented in ritual vessels and bamboo baskets now match the standards of the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and the sacrifices to the gods of soil; the feathers and flutes arrayed for the dance no longer follow merely the system prescribed for princes and lords. Music and ceremonial forms are thus complete, and the entire scene is renewed. This is because we have humbly encountered Your Majesty the Emperor…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
秉心淵塞
凝命穆清
敬德以先
用儒而治
潜心經幄得刪述之精微
垂意人文妙昭回之賁飾惟茲曠典遂出
明時
玉音渙發於九重
天使遠馳於六轡升堂薦告洋洋乎如聞金
===
石之聲夾道瞻趨欣欣然宛有堵墻之集
制實通於天下匪直魯宫士胥慶於寰中
矧惟孔氏臣某紹續前封因緣末系行其
禮奏其樂庸虛深愧於象賢月之恒日之
升感激徒能於華
祝臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
punctuated:
秉心淵塞，凝命穆清，敬德以先，用儒而治。潜心經幄，得刪述之精微；垂意人文，妙昭回之賁飾。惟茲曠典，遂出明時。玉音渙發於九重，天使遠馳於六轡。升堂薦告，洋洋乎如聞金石之聲；夾道瞻趨，欣欣然宛有堵墻之集。制實通於天下，匪直魯宫；士胥慶於寰中，矧惟孔氏！
臣某紹續前封，因緣末系。行其禮，奏其樂，庸虛深愧於象賢；月之恒，日之升，感激徒能於華祝。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱
translation_en:
…holds a heart profound and sincere, secures the Mandate in solemn purity, puts reverence for virtue first, and governs through Confucian scholars. Devoting himself to the classics in the imperial lecture chamber, he grasps the subtle profundities of Confucius’s editing and transmission; attending to cultural refinement, he wondrously adorns it with his encompassing radiance. Thus this exceptional rite has come forth in an enlightened age. His august words spread from the ninefold palace; the imperial envoy hastened far afield, driving with six reins. Ascending the hall to present offerings and announce the decree, we seemed to hear the swelling music of bells and chimes. Lining the road to watch the procession, the joyful crowds gathered like encircling walls. This ordinance indeed extends throughout the realm, not merely to the palace of Lu; scholars everywhere rejoice together—how much more so the Kong lineage!
Your servant, so-and-so, has succeeded to the former enfeoffment by virtue of belonging to a remote branch of the lineage. Performing these rites and presenting this music, mediocre and empty of merit as I am, I feel profound shame at failing to emulate my worthy ancestor. With gratitude, I can only offer the blessings of Hua: may you be like the waxing moon and the rising sun. Your servant cannot contain his utmost fervor and trembling reverence as he gazes toward Heaven and looks up to Your Sagely Majesty. I respectfully submit this memorial to express…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
高輝
同考試官訓導李批筆勢翩翩如天馬行空躡浮
雲而上征非復可施銜勒矣敬羨敬羨
同考試官教諭李批議論英發才氣偉然仰頌
===
聖祖之製覈論漢唐諸君反復頓挫隱然有一唱三嘆之音高薦何忝
考試官侍講彭批疎密輕重皆有意謂非苟然者
考試官洗馬鄭批五策皆可觀此篇尤善揄揚
文亦滂沛策塲之優者歟
性於天者不必其成於人務於大者無所
事於小聞大道之要則區區之文藝有不
足言而得於天質之美者亦豈規規於綴
緝者之所能及哉盖嘗觀於先哲之論矣
夫留意詞藻之末弊精文義之間此拘儒
punctuated:
謝以聞。
第叁塲。策。第一問。高輝。
同考試官訓導李批：筆勢翩翩，如天馬行空，躡浮雲而上征，非復可施銜勒矣。敬羨，敬羨！
同考試官教諭李批：議論英發，才氣偉然。仰頌聖祖之製，覈論漢唐諸君，反復頓挫，隱然有一唱三嘆之音。高薦何忝！
考試官侍講彭批：疎密輕重，皆有意謂，非苟然者。
考試官洗馬鄭批：五策皆可觀，此篇尤善揄揚，文亦滂沛，策塲之優者歟！
性於天者，不必其成於人；務於大者，無所事於小。聞大道之要，則區區之文藝有不足言，而得於天質之美者，亦豈規規於綴緝者之所能及哉？盖嘗觀於先哲之論矣。夫留意詞藻之末，弊精文義之間，此拘儒
translation_en:
…to express thanks and make this known to the throne.
Third Session. Policy Essays. First Question. Gao Hui.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: His brush moves gracefully, like a celestial horse coursing through the sky, treading the floating clouds and ascending ever higher: no bit or bridle can restrain it now. Admiration and envy, admiration and envy!
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: His arguments shine with brilliance, and his talent and spirit are magnificent. He reverently extols the institutions of the Sagely Founder and critically discusses the rulers of the Han and Tang. His repeated turns of argument and measured cadences subtly evoke the sound of one singer answered by three sighing voices. How could recommending him highly be undeserved!
Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor-in-waiting: The sparseness and density, the light and heavy touches, all convey deliberate meaning; none is casual.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian of the Heir Apparent: All five policy essays merit attention. This one is especially accomplished in its praise, and its prose flows abundantly. Surely it is among the finest essays in this policy examination!
What is endowed by Heaven need not depend upon human effort for its perfection; one who applies himself to great matters has no occasion to busy himself with small ones. Once one has learned the essentials of the Great Way, mere literary accomplishments scarcely merit discussion. And how could those who confine themselves to piecing words together match someone endowed with the excellence of a fine natural disposition? I have indeed examined the discussions of earlier wise men. To devote attention to the trifles of ornate diction and exhaust one's energies over textual meanings—this is what narrow-minded scholars…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
曲士之所攻非致治保邦之所急則謂帝
王之學與常人不同者是也然大學之道
修身為本天子庶人其理無二則謂帝王
之學與常人不異者亦是也漢唐以来盖
無足與於斯者高帝以明達之資豁大之
度奔走英豪宰制羣力舉措施為規摹宏
遠出詞吐論氣格開張使其本於身者有
先王講學之功談詩書者非陸賈叔孫生
之陋則大風之作且將有阜財解慍之念
===
而新語之奏豈足以少符其起居造誡之
心哉若夫孝武之好文學魏武之本諸生
唐太宗之才敏夙成玄宗之文譽自負皆
嘗致力於斯事而今昔所共推者至論其
得於天質之高則其視不事詩書者反有
間焉是以橫汾之作後世嘗譏其氣象之
委靡宫體之傳當時已病其純正之不足
曹氏之述作尤多開元之篇製具在品目
高下曾莫遁情使其有見於明良喜起之
punctuated: 曲士之所攻，非致治保邦之所急，則謂帝王之學與常人不同者是也。然大學之道，修身為本，天子庶人，其理無二，則謂帝王之學與常人不異者亦是也。漢唐以来，盖無足與於斯者。高帝以明達之資、豁大之度，奔走英豪，宰制羣力，舉措施為，規摹宏遠；出詞吐論，氣格開張。使其本於身者有先王講學之功，談詩書者非陸賈、叔孫生之陋，則《大風》之作，且將有阜財解慍之念，而《新語》之奏，豈足以少符其起居造誡之心哉？若夫孝武之好文學、魏武之本諸生、唐太宗之才敏夙成、玄宗之文譽自負，皆嘗致力於斯事，而今昔所共推者。至論其得於天質之高，則其視不事詩書者反有間焉。是以橫汾之作，後世嘗譏其氣象之委靡；宫體之傳，當時已病其純正之不足。曹氏之述作尤多，開元之篇製具在，品目高下，曾莫遁情。使其有見於明良喜起之
translation_en:
…the pursuits of narrow-minded scholars, rather than urgent necessities for bringing about good government and preserving the state: in this respect, it is correct to say that the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of ordinary people. Yet the Way of the Great Learning takes cultivation of the self as its foundation. For the Son of Heaven and the common people, this principle is the same; thus it is also correct to say that the learning of emperors and kings does not differ from that of ordinary people.

From the Han and Tang onward, scarcely anyone has been worthy to partake in such learning. Emperor Gao, with his perceptive intelligence and magnanimous disposition, set heroes to work and directed their combined strength. His undertakings were grand in conception and far-reaching; his utterances and arguments displayed expansive vigor and bearing. Had his cultivation of himself been grounded in the former kings’ diligent study, and had those who discussed the Book of Odes and Book of Documents with him risen above the limitations of Lu Jia and Master Shusun, then his composition of the Song of the Great Wind would have embodied a concern to enrich the people and dispel their resentment. How could the presentation of the New Discourses have even slightly satisfied his desire for admonitions concerning his daily conduct [?]?

As for Emperor Xiaowu’s fondness for literary learning, Emperor Wu of Wei’s origins as a classical student, Emperor Taizong of Tang’s precocious talent and acuity, and Emperor Xuanzong’s pride in his literary reputation, all devoted effort to this pursuit and have won acclaim both in their own times and since. Yet, judged by the loftiness of their innate endowments, they actually fell short of the ruler who did not occupy himself with the Odes and Documents. Thus later generations criticized the dispirited tenor of the poem on crossing the Fen River, while the lack of purity and rectitude in the circulating palace-style poetry was already deplored at the time. The writings of the Cao house are especially numerous, and the compositions of the Kaiyuan era remain extant: when ranked as higher or lower, their true qualities cannot be concealed. Had they perceived the lofty significance of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers rejoicing and rousing themselves to action…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
高致而相與爲允懷典學之實功且将進
而彷佛於六義六體之製豈特頡頏於終
馬褚虞燕許之間哉
天生
聖祖光啓
大明心學得於自然化筆妙於神授敷言之訓
衣被臣民昭回之光藻飾萬物愚嘗詮伏
草茅而竊窺其一二若君臣同游之一語
置之典謨訓誥之列泯乎其無以別也未
===
有外綱常而可以爲君之一言雖千百世
之後聖確乎其不可易也至於訓迪治官
昭陳政體旁盡物情下悉民志補先儒之
所未備正前世之所謬訛鑿鑿如五穀之
療飢布帛之衛寒不可一日而無也又嘗
聞之
先朝之舊臣故老矣以爲
聖心所屬翰墨時御略不駐思而頃刻數百言
意足辭止不復點竄是豈竭精弊神爭妍
punctuated:
高致，而相與爲允懷典學之實功，且将進而彷佛於六義六體之製，豈特頡頏於終馬褚虞燕許之間哉？
天生聖祖，光啓大明，心學得於自然，化筆妙於神授。敷言之訓，衣被臣民；昭回之光，藻飾萬物。愚嘗詮伏草茅，而竊窺其一二。若「君臣同游」之一語，置之典謨訓誥之列，泯乎其無以別也。「未有外綱常而可以爲君」之一言，雖千百世之後聖，確乎其不可易也。至於訓迪治官，昭陳政體，旁盡物情，下悉民志，補先儒之所未備，正前世之所謬訛，鑿鑿如五穀之療飢、布帛之衛寒，不可一日而無也。又嘗聞之先朝之舊臣故老矣，以爲聖心所屬，翰墨時御，略不駐思，而頃刻數百言，意足辭止，不復點竄。是豈竭精弊神，爭妍
translation_en:
…such lofty attainments, and together undertake the substantive work of sincerely cherishing the canonical teachings. They would then advance toward approximating the compositions embodying the six principles of poetry and the six forms of writing. Would they merely vie with Zhong [?], Ma, Chu, Yu, Yan, and Xu?
Heaven brought forth the sagely founder, who gloriously inaugurated the Great Ming. His learning of the mind came naturally, and the marvels of his transforming brush were divinely bestowed. The teachings conveyed in his words clothed his subjects; their radiant light adorned all things. I, in my humble obscurity among the grasses [?], have ventured to glimpse a little of this. Such a phrase as “ruler and ministers roaming together,” if placed among the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of the Book of Documents, would blend in indistinguishably. His statement, “No one can stand outside the cardinal bonds and constant virtues and yet be a ruler,” is so firmly established that even a sage a thousand or a hundred generations hence could not alter it. As for instructing officials in governance, clearly setting forth the principles of government, comprehensively addressing the circumstances of things, and fully understanding the aspirations of the people below, his writings supply what earlier Confucian scholars left incomplete and correct the errors of preceding ages. Their assured usefulness is like that of grain in relieving hunger or cloth in warding off cold: one cannot go a single day without them. I have also heard veteran ministers and elders of the former reign say that whenever his sagely mind turned to something and he took up brush and ink, he scarcely paused to think before producing several hundred words in an instant. When the meaning was fully expressed, the words ceased; he made no further revisions. Could those who exhaust their energies and wear out their spirits, competing in elegance …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
取工較一日之長者可望其萬一哉愚敢
曰
高皇帝之於文盖性之天者也
第二問
方榮
同考試官教諭蕭批理學一策有先儒成說學
者多不之講此篇發明詳盡末復言工夫次第知入德
之門必嘗用心於此者
考試官侍講彭批記憶儒先之論略無所遺
===
考試官洗馬鄭批敷對詳明足見學力
汗牛充棟天下之圖書富矣而闡明夫義
理者惟二三策而已耳際天蟠地天下之
義理廣矣而究極其精微者在方寸間而
已耳盖天下之學莫粹於性理天下之理
不外乎一心故欲究先儒之學當求諸書
欲求先儒之書當究諸心得於心則先儒
之理學可論矣太極西銘探極造化之秘
推明仁孝之理得千載之不傳發前聖之
punctuated:
取工、較一日之長者，可望其萬一哉？愚敢曰：高皇帝之於文，盖性之天者也。
第二問
方榮
同考試官教諭蕭批：理學一策，有先儒成說，學者多不之講。此篇發明詳盡，末復言工夫次第，知入德之門，必嘗用心於此者。
考試官侍講彭批：記憶儒先之論，略無所遺。
考試官洗馬鄭批：敷對詳明，足見學力。
汗牛充棟，天下之圖書富矣，而闡明夫義理者，惟二三策而已耳。際天蟠地，天下之義理廣矣，而究極其精微者，在方寸間而已耳。盖天下之學莫粹於性理，天下之理不外乎一心。故欲究先儒之學，當求諸書；欲求先儒之書，當究諸心。得於心，則先儒之理學可論矣。太極、西銘，探極造化之秘，推明仁孝之理，得千載之不傳，發前聖之
translation_en:
…seeking literary polish and competing for a moment’s superiority—could such writers hope to attain even a ten-thousandth of his achievement? I venture to say: Emperor Gao’s literary accomplishment arose from his Heaven-endowed nature.
Second Question
Fang Rong
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: On this policy question concerning the Learning of Principle, earlier Confucian scholars have established explanations, but students seldom study them. This essay elucidates the subject thoroughly and in detail. At the end it also discusses the successive stages of practical effort. The writer knows the gateway to entering into virtue and must have devoted thought to this subject.
Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: He recalls the discussions of earlier Confucian scholars, omitting virtually nothing.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Director of the Library: His response is detailed and clear, amply demonstrating the strength of his learning.
So numerous that they make oxen sweat when transported and fill buildings when stored, the books of the world are abundant indeed. Yet those that elucidate moral principles number only two or three works. Extending to the bounds of heaven and encompassing the earth, the moral principles of the world are vast indeed. Yet the means of fathoming their subtlest mysteries lies solely within the heart. For no learning in the world is purer than the study of human nature and principle, and no principle in the world lies outside the single heart. Thus, to investigate the learning of earlier Confucian scholars, one must seek it in their books; to seek understanding of their books, one must investigate it within one’s heart. Once one has grasped it in the heart, one can discuss their Learning of Principle. The Supreme Ultimate and the Western Inscription probe the deepest secrets of creation and transformation and elucidate the principles of benevolence and filial devotion. They recover what had gone untransmitted for a thousand years and bring to light what the sages of old …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
未發誠理學之宗也愚嘗因程朱之言究
二書之旨矣請陳其槩太極圖說首言陰
陽變化之原繼以人物稟受之序惟人也
得其秀而最靈純粹至善之性也是所謂
太極也形生神發其陽動陰靜之為乎五
性感動其陽變陰合而生五行之性乎曰
善惡生萬事出其成男成女萬物化生之
象乎終之以易者豈不以易之為書廣大
悉備而圖有以盡之歟首尾相因有緒而
===
不遺脉絡貫通有條而不紊朱子之言可
謂深得其旨矣彼謂傳於种放之徒近於
老氏之說者何足以知之西銘一篇始言
乾為父坤為母所謂理一也然乾坤者天
地之父母而父母者一身之父母非所謂
分殊乎民為同胞物為吾與自天下之父
母言之所謂理一也然謂之民則非真以
為吾之同胞謂之物則非真以為吾之同
類自一身之父母言之非所謂分殊乎至
punctuated:
未發，誠理學之宗也。愚嘗因程朱之言，究二書之旨矣，請陳其槩。《太極圖說》首言陰陽變化之原，繼以人物稟受之序。惟人也，得其秀而最靈，純粹至善之性也，是所謂太極也。形生神發，其陽動陰靜之為乎？五性感動，其陽變陰合而生五行之性乎？曰善惡生、萬事出，其成男成女、萬物化生之象乎？終之以《易》者，豈不以《易》之為書，廣大悉備，而圖有以盡之歟？首尾相因，有緒而不遺；脉絡貫通，有條而不紊。朱子之言，可謂深得其旨矣。彼謂傳於种放之徒、近於老氏之說者，何足以知之？
《西銘》一篇，始言乾為父、坤為母，所謂理一也。然乾坤者，天地之父母，而父母者，一身之父母，非所謂分殊乎？民為同胞，物為吾與，自天下之父母言之，所謂理一也。然謂之民，則非真以為吾之同胞；謂之物，則非真以為吾之同類。自一身之父母言之，非所謂分殊乎？至
translation_en:
…what the sages of former times had not articulated: these truly are foundational works of the learning of principle. Following the words of Cheng and Zhu, I have sought to fathom the purport of these two works. Allow me to set out their main outlines. The Explanation of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu shuo) begins with the source of the transformations of yin and yang, then proceeds to the sequence in which humans and other beings receive their endowments. Humans alone receive the finest of these and possess the greatest spiritual intelligence. Their nature, wholly pure and supremely good, is what is called the Supreme Ultimate. When bodily form comes into being and spiritual awareness develops, is this not the working of yang in activity and yin in stillness? When the five aspects of human nature are stimulated into activity, is this not the nature of the Five Phases, generated through the transformation of yang and the union of yin? When it says that good and evil arise and the myriad affairs emerge, is this not an image of the formation of males and females and the transformative generation of the myriad beings? Does it not conclude with the Book of Changes because that book is vast and all-embracing, and the diagram can encompass it in its entirety? Beginning and end follow from one another, forming an ordered sequence with nothing omitted; its threads run throughout, systematically arranged without confusion. Master Zhu’s words may indeed be said to grasp its purport profoundly. How could those who say that it was transmitted among such men as Chong Fang and is close to the teachings of Laozi be capable of understanding it?
The Western Inscription (Xi ming) begins by saying that Qian is the father and Kun the mother: this is what is meant by the unity of principle. Yet Qian and Kun are the parents of Heaven and Earth, while one’s own parents are the parents of one individual. Is this not what is meant by differentiation in particular relationships? The people are my siblings, and other beings are my companions: viewed from the standpoint of the parents of all under Heaven, this is what is meant by the unity of principle. Yet calling them ‘the people’ does not mean that they truly are my siblings; calling them ‘other beings’ does not mean that they truly are of my own kind. Viewed from the standpoint of one individual’s parents, is this not what is meant by differentiation in particular relationships? As for…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
若大舜之厎豫曾子之全歸則因事親之
誠以明事天之道皆理一而分殊也所謂
名虛理實者亦謂是耳程子之論可謂一
言蔽之矣彼謂語體而遺用平施而無稱
物者又何足以語此夫自孔孟不作理學
無傳縱橫於秦黃老於漢清談於晉辭章
於唐天下不知所謂理學者盖非一日也
至宋周張二夫子者出闡性命之旨開理
學之源而嘉惠後學至矣學者讀二書而
===
有得焉則自戒謹恐懼以脩性分之本然
存心養性以盡畏天之當然由是而造夫
仁義中正之地樂天踐形之域何有豈徒
誦說之而已哉執事幸有以教之
第叁問
倪天民
同考試官教諭胡 批此策正欲觀士子該博之學而
善答者甚不多見是篇考據精詳論議切當真策手也視
彼敷演問目者風斯下矣
punctuated:
若大舜之厎豫、曾子之全歸，則因事親之誠以明事天之道，皆理一而分殊也。所謂名虛理實者，亦謂是耳。程子之論，可謂一言蔽之矣。彼謂語體而遺用、平施而無稱物者，又何足以語此？夫自孔孟不作，理學無傳，縱橫於秦，黃老於漢，清談於晉，辭章於唐，天下不知所謂理學者，盖非一日也。至宋周張二夫子者出，闡性命之旨，開理學之源，而嘉惠後學至矣。學者讀二書而有得焉，則自戒謹恐懼以脩性分之本然，存心養性以盡畏天之當然，由是而造夫仁義中正之地、樂天踐形之域，何有？豈徒誦說之而已哉？執事幸有以教之。
第叁問
倪天民
同考試官教諭胡批：此策正欲觀士子該博之學，而善答者甚不多見。是篇考據精詳，論議切當，真策手也。視彼敷演問目者，風斯下矣。
translation_en:
…As for the great Shun’s bringing his parents to contentment and Zengzi’s returning his body intact at death, these illuminate the Way of serving Heaven through sincerity in serving one’s parents. In both, principle is one, while its particular manifestations differ. This, too, is what is meant by saying that the names are figurative but the principle is real. Master Cheng’s judgment may indeed be said to encompass it all in a single statement. How could those who claim that it discusses substance but neglects function, or extends its concern uniformly without weighing the distinctions among things, be qualified to discuss this?
Since Confucius and Mencius ceased to arise among us, the learning of principle had lacked transmission. Diplomatic strategizing prevailed in the Qin, the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi in the Han, pure conversation in the Jin, and literary composition in the Tang. The world’s ignorance of what is called the learning of principle was thus no recent development. Only in the Song did the two masters Zhou and Zhang emerge, elucidating the meaning of human nature and Heaven’s mandate and opening the wellspring of the learning of principle. Their beneficence toward later students was profound indeed. If students gain understanding from reading these two works, they will proceed through vigilance and apprehension to cultivate the original endowment of their nature, and through preserving the mind and nurturing their nature to fulfill the duty of revering Heaven. What difficulty would there then be in reaching the ground of benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness, and the realm of delighting in Heaven and fully realizing what their bodily form embodies? Could it be merely a matter of reciting and expounding these works? I would be grateful for your instruction.
Third Question
Ni Tianmin
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: This policy question was intended precisely to test the breadth of the candidates’ learning, yet very few answered it well. This essay is meticulous and detailed in its examination of evidence, and its arguments are apt and sound: its author is a true master of the policy essay. Compared with him, those who merely elaborate upon the wording of the question bow before the wind of his example.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正裘批此策條答不遺考論有據且
詞氣豐贍蔚然可觀蓋優於策學者寘之高等公論
攸歸
考試官侍講彭批比辭析事皆有條理
考試官洗馬鄭批論古人成敗歷歷如見益見其
情殆非穉學
不兼天下之智不足以用天下之言不用
天下之言不足以濟天下之事蓋天下之
事無窮而一人之見有限必用天下之言
===
斯能盡天下之智而天下之事無不濟矣
古之人君臨天下之大定天下之業孰不
樂聞忠讜之論為國家助哉顧用之何如
耳然非在我者有以兼天下之智又孰能
知而用之執事發策舉古人之用言下詢
愚生何足以知此然即其取舍之迹考其
成敗之迹不難知也夫六國之印遽銷於
子房一借箸之間高帝之悟速矣向使酈
生之說行則漢事不幾於去乎馬邑之誘
punctuated:
同考試官學正裘批：此策條答不遺，考論有據，且詞氣豐贍，蔚然可觀，蓋優於策學者。寘之高等，公論攸歸。

考試官侍講彭批：比辭析事，皆有條理。

考試官洗馬鄭批：論古人成敗，歷歷如見，益見其情，殆非穉學。

不兼天下之智，不足以用天下之言；不用天下之言，不足以濟天下之事。蓋天下之事無窮，而一人之見有限，必用天下之言，斯能盡天下之智，而天下之事無不濟矣。古之人君，臨天下之大，定天下之業，孰不樂聞忠讜之論，為國家助哉？顧用之何如耳。然非在我者有以兼天下之智，又孰能知而用之？執事發策，舉古人之用言，下詢愚生，何足以知此？然即其取舍之迹，考其成敗之迹，不難知也。夫六國之印，遽銷於子房一借箸之間，高帝之悟速矣。向使酈生之說行，則漢事不幾於去乎？馬邑之誘
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Qiu, an Instructor, comments: This policy essay answers each point without omission, grounding its investigations and arguments in evidence. Its language and spirit are also rich and ample, presenting an impressive display. The writer clearly excels in the study of policy essays. Placing it in a high rank accords with the consensus of impartial judgment.

Examiner Peng, an Expositor-in-waiting, comments: Both the arrangement of its language and its analysis of affairs are methodical.

Examiner Zheng, a Librarian, comments: Its discussion of the successes and failures of men of antiquity is so vivid that one seems to witness them, gaining still greater insight into their circumstances. This is surely no novice’s learning.

Unless one embraces the wisdom of all under Heaven, one cannot make use of the counsel of all under Heaven; unless one uses that counsel, one cannot accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven. For the affairs of the world are inexhaustible, whereas one person’s understanding is limited. Only by making use of the counsel of all under Heaven can one draw fully upon their wisdom, so that no affair in the world remains unaccomplished. Among the rulers of antiquity who presided over the vast realm and established its enduring foundations, who did not welcome loyal and forthright counsel to assist the state? The question is simply how they employed it. Yet unless one possesses the capacity to embrace the wisdom of all under Heaven, how can one recognize and employ such counsel? You, honored examiners, have posed a policy question, citing how men of antiquity employed counsel and condescending to inquire of this foolish student. How could I be qualified to understand this? Nevertheless, by examining the traces of what they accepted and rejected and investigating the record of their successes and failures, it is not difficult to understand.

The seals of the Six States were promptly melted down in the brief interval in which Zifang borrowed some chopsticks to explain his argument: how swiftly Emperor Gao realized his error! Had Scholar Li’s proposal been implemented, would the Han enterprise not have come close to ruin? The lure at Mayi…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
卒成於王恢屢廷辨之餘武帝之惑深矣
向使安國之計用則邊塵其至於屢驚乎
孫權之走操周瑜之策也若懾於長江共
之之語則何以成鼎足之勢晉武之平吴
羊祜之謀也若奪於秦凉為憂之論則何
以成混一之功苻堅南寇茍惟陽平之聽
則五將之奔可免矣何說於躬行天罰之
面諛而自速其亡邪宋文北侵茍惟慶之
之用則元嘉之政不衰矣何動於席卷趙
===
魏之浮談而自蹙其國邪勸伐高麗李勣
之逢君可罪也師出無功適足為太宗之
累使能受遂良之直言而不變寧有是哉
主盟吐蕃張延賞之誤國可責也刼盟見
辱亦足為德宗之玷使先知栁渾之料敵
而不疑豈至是哉帥兵淮西裴度欲勵諸
將也一皷而元濟成擒設其事沮於逢吉
則淮蔡之人終不知有生民之樂矣請幸
澶淵寇準欲破敵膽也一出而契丹奪氣
punctuated: 卒成於王恢屢廷辨之餘，武帝之惑深矣！向使安國之計用，則邊塵其至於屢驚乎？孫權之走操，周瑜之策也。若懾於「長江共之」之語，則何以成鼎足之勢？晉武之平吴，羊祜之謀也。若奪於「秦凉為憂」之論，則何以成混一之功？苻堅南寇，茍惟陽平之聽，則五將之奔可免矣。何說於「躬行天罰」之面諛，而自速其亡邪？宋文北侵，茍惟慶之之用，則元嘉之政不衰矣。何動於「席卷趙魏」之浮談，而自蹙其國邪？勸伐高麗，李勣之逢君可罪也。師出無功，適足為太宗之累。使能受遂良之直言而不變，寧有是哉？主盟吐蕃，張延賞之誤國可責也。刼盟見辱，亦足為德宗之玷。使先知栁渾之料敵而不疑，豈至是哉？帥兵淮西，裴度欲勵諸將也。一皷而元濟成擒，設其事沮於逢吉，則淮蔡之人終不知有生民之樂矣。請幸澶淵，寇準欲破敵膽也。一出而契丹奪氣，
translation_en:
…was finally adopted after Wang Hui’s repeated arguments at court: deep indeed was Emperor Wu’s delusion! Had Anguo’s plan been followed, would alarm over disturbances on the frontier have arisen so often? Sun Quan’s putting Cao Cao to flight was due to Zhou Yu’s strategy. Had he been intimidated by the assertion that “the Yangtze is shared by both sides,” how could he have established the balance of three powers, like the legs of a tripod? Emperor Wu of Jin’s conquest of Wu was due to Yang Hu’s plan. Had he been swayed by the argument that “Qin and Liang are cause for concern,” how could he have achieved unification? When Fu Jian invaded the south, had he listened only to the Duke of Yangping, the flight of the five generals could have been avoided. Why was he pleased by the flattery offered to his face about “personally carrying out Heaven’s punishment,” thereby hastening his own ruin? When Emperor Wen of Song invaded the north, had he followed Qingzhi’s counsel alone, the governance of the Yuanjia era would not have declined. Why was he moved by empty talk of “sweeping through Zhao and Wei,” thereby bringing distress upon his own state?

In urging an attack on Gaoli, Li Ji deserves condemnation for pandering to his ruler. The army’s fruitless expedition served only to burden Emperor Taizong’s reputation. Had the emperor accepted Suiliang’s frank advice and remained steadfast, could this have happened? In advocating a covenant with Tubo, Zhang Yanshang deserves blame for misleading the state. The treacherous assault at the covenant meeting and the resulting humiliation were also enough to stain Emperor Dezong’s reputation. Had he recognized beforehand the soundness of Liu Hun’s assessment of the enemy and entertained no doubts, could matters have reached this point?

In leading the troops in Huaixi, Pei Du sought to spur on the generals. At a single beat of the drum, Yuanji was taken captive. Had Fengji obstructed this undertaking, the people of Huai and Cai would never have known the joys of peaceful life. In requesting that the emperor proceed to Chanyuan, Kou Zhun sought to break the enemy’s courage. Once the emperor went forth, the Khitan lost heart…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
設其議移於欽若則大梁之危將不待靖
康而然矣嗚呼一言可以興邦一言可以
喪邦其安危之機成敗之分一係於言如
此為天下國家者可不以知言為務哉雖
然有權之平然後能知物之輕重有度之
精然後能知物之長短有吾心之權度然
後能知言之是非故曰人在堂上方能辨
堂下人曲直正謂是也欲知天下之言又
當以窮天下之理為本執事以為何如
===
第四問
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批此卷五策俱能條答治教
一篇於立法用人處盖有見乎其大者非徒區區於條
肄之末至於寫一時之弊宛然可見非諳涉之素而才
氣之充者殆不及此
同考試官教諭袁批有鋪叙委曲之雅辭有含蓄
不盡之餘意燕趙古稱多感慨之士信然
考試官侍講彭批中間議論有引其几而不竟
punctuated:
設其議移於欽若，則大梁之危將不待靖康而然矣。嗚呼！一言可以興邦，一言可以喪邦，其安危之機、成敗之分，一係於言如此，為天下國家者可不以知言為務哉？雖然，有權之平，然後能知物之輕重；有度之精，然後能知物之長短；有吾心之權度，然後能知言之是非。故曰：「人在堂上，方能辨堂下人曲直。」正謂是也。欲知天下之言，又當以窮天下之理為本。執事以為何如？

第四問
宋禮

同考試官訓導張批：此卷五策俱能條答，治教一篇，於立法用人處，盖有見乎其大者，非徒區區於條肄之末。至於寫一時之弊，宛然可見，非諳涉之素而才氣之充者，殆不及此。

同考試官教諭袁批：有鋪叙委曲之雅辭，有含蓄不盡之餘意。燕趙古稱多感慨之士，信然。

考試官侍講彭批：中間議論，有引其几而不竟
translation_en:
… Had his proposal been swayed by Qinruo, the peril that befell Daliang would not have waited until the Jingkang era to arise. Alas! A single utterance can make a state flourish; a single utterance can bring a state to ruin. The turning point between security and danger, the dividing line between success and failure, depends so entirely on what is said. Can those who govern the realm and the state fail to make discerning words their task? Yet only with an even balance can one determine the weight of things; only with an accurate measure can one determine their length. Only with a balance and measure within one's own mind can one discern whether words are right or wrong. Thus the saying, “Only when standing above in the hall can one distinguish who is right and who is wrong among those below,” means precisely this. To discern the words spoken throughout the realm, one must also take the thorough investigation of the principles of all things as one's foundation. What is your judgment, sir?

Fourth Question
Song Li

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: All five policy essays in this script answer the questions point by point. The essay on governance and moral instruction shows insight into the larger issues concerning the establishment of laws and the employment of men, rather than merely dwelling on the minutiae of regulations and practice [?]. Its depiction of contemporary abuses makes them vividly apparent. Someone without long familiarity with such matters and abundant talent could scarcely attain this level.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: There is elegant language that sets matters forth in all their intricacy, and there are further implications held in reserve, never fully exhausted. Yan and Zhao have been said since antiquity to abound in men of impassioned feeling. Truly so.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: Among the arguments here, some introduce the beginnings of a line of thought [?] but do not carry through …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
其目者豈風簷寸晷之間不能盡其說耶雖然可以
意得之矣
考試官洗馬鄭批論議切直卓有所見其識時
務者哉他日設施未必無可觀也
以馭吏之法為疎密而疎密之用常不繫
於法以用人之塗為輕重而輕重之勢常
必變其初盖天下無一法之無其弊而亦
無一塗之不足以得人雖周官六典之制
亦未必其盡宜於今而假令出於鄉舉里
===
選之目者亦豈必皆舉其職哉此愚所以
反覆於執事之問而有感焉夫為州縣者
有吏員也有監生也有進士也而議者以
為莫賢於進士任學校者或自鄉貢除或
自明經薦或由監學選而議者以為莫弊
於薦舉夫進士之科
朝廷所留意士夫所傾心其選授之初上下
嘗屬目焉今進士之選盛行矣而執事所
謂漸輕之勢已有見於今者愚固不敢謂
punctuated:
其目者，豈風簷寸晷之間不能盡其說耶？雖然，可以意得之矣。
考試官洗馬鄭批：論議切直，卓有所見，其識時務者哉！他日設施，未必無可觀也。
以馭吏之法為疎密，而疎密之用常不繫於法；以用人之塗為輕重，而輕重之勢常必變其初。盖天下無一法之無其弊，而亦無一塗之不足以得人。雖周官六典之制，亦未必其盡宜於今；而假令出於鄉舉里選之目者，亦豈必皆舉其職哉？此愚所以反覆於執事之問而有感焉。夫為州縣者，有吏員也，有監生也，有進士也，而議者以為莫賢於進士。任學校者，或自鄉貢除，或自明經薦，或由監學選，而議者以為莫弊於薦舉。夫進士之科，朝廷所留意，士夫所傾心，其選授之初，上下嘗屬目焉。今進士之選盛行矣，而執事所謂漸輕之勢，已有見於今者，愚固不敢謂
translation_en:
…their particulars. Could it be that, beneath the windswept eaves and in the scant time available, he could not fully explain his views? Even so, his meaning can be grasped.
Examiner Zheng, Librarian of the Heir Apparent, comments: His arguments are pertinent and forthright, displaying outstanding insight. Surely he understands the affairs of the day! When he puts his ideas into practice in the future, there may well be much to commend.
Methods of controlling subordinate officials are considered lax or strict, yet the effects of laxity and strictness often do not depend on the regulations themselves. Routes into official service are considered prestigious or humble, yet their relative standing inevitably changes from what it was at first. For there is no method in the world without its abuses, nor any route incapable of yielding suitable men. Even the system of the six codes in the Offices of Zhou would not necessarily be entirely appropriate today. And even if men entered service through nomination by their districts and selection by their villages, would they necessarily all discharge their duties? This is why I have pondered your question repeatedly and have been moved to reflect upon it.
Those who administer prefectures and counties include clerical personnel, Imperial University students, and metropolitan graduates (jinshi); yet commentators hold that none are more worthy than the metropolitan graduates. Those appointed to schools may receive appointments as provincial tribute candidates, be recommended for their mastery of the classics, or be selected from the Imperial University; yet commentators hold that no route is more beset by abuses than recommendation.
As for the metropolitan graduate examination, the court gives it careful attention, and scholars and officials set their hearts upon it. At the outset of selection and appointment through this route, those above and below alike watched closely. Now selection through the metropolitan graduate examination is widely practiced; yet, as to whether the gradual decline in standing of which you speak is already evident today, I certainly dare not say…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
無也薦舉之人夤緣以求知僥倖以苟得
其末流之壞士類嘗扼腕焉今薦舉之門
已杜矣而執事所謂不職之弊未有以賢
於彼者愚亦不敢謂無也至於責治於州
縣者其法不密於近時乎鋤芸櫛治無間
於嵗年升華躋要改觀於轉盻可謂急於
幽明之黜陟矣加意於學校者其法不因
仍於昔日乎責成之效惟在於貢舉考功
之課不及以吏事可謂專於師儒之責任
===
矣雖然知解印之不旋踵也則京兆之五
日必有以償其未愜之心而拱辰之一綱
尚幸其或吞舟之漏知召檄之不終朝也
則操轡策於上者必濶略於惠文之治而
屏聲氣於下者常惕息於吞𩺀之威夫豈
勸懲之本意哉若夫人材之產也有謂為
孝秀之淵有謂為荒之壤故或倚席不
講而功籍已盈或課授不輟而殿負自若
至其學問之察也外而風憲有比年之試
punctuated:
無也。薦舉之人，夤緣以求知，僥倖以苟得，其末流之壞，士類嘗扼腕焉。今薦舉之門已杜矣，而執事所謂不職之弊，未有以賢於彼者，愚亦不敢謂無也。至於責治於州縣者，其法不密於近時乎？鋤芸櫛治，無間於嵗年；升華躋要，改觀於轉盻，可謂急於幽明之黜陟矣。加意於學校者，其法不因仍於昔日乎？責成之效，惟在於貢舉；考功之課，不及以吏事，可謂專於師儒之責任矣。
雖然，知解印之不旋踵也，則京兆之五日，必有以償其未愜之心，而拱辰之一綱，尚幸其或吞舟之漏；知召檄之不終朝也，則操轡策於上者，必濶略於惠文之治，而屏聲氣於下者，常惕息於吞𩺀之威。夫豈勸懲之本意哉？若夫人材之產也，有謂為孝秀之淵，有謂為荒之壤，故或倚席不講，而功籍已盈；或課授不輟，而殿負自若。至其學問之察也，外而風憲有比年之試，
translation_en:
…that none exist. Those seeking recommendation cultivated connections to gain recognition and relied on chance to obtain appointments by whatever means they could. The degeneration of this practice in its later stages has long made scholars wring their hands in indignation. Now the avenue of recommendation has been closed, yet the failings in the discharge of office that you describe are no better than those under that system. I would not venture to deny this either. As for demanding good government from prefectures and counties, have the regulations not become more stringent in recent times? Weeding out and combing through their ranks proceeds without interruption, year after year; promotion to distinguished and important posts transforms a man's prospects in the blink of an eye. One may indeed say that demoting the incompetent and promoting the capable is pursued with urgency. As for the special attention given to schools, do the regulations not follow earlier practice? The results demanded consist solely in presenting candidates for the examinations; assessments of merit do not extend to administrative business. One may indeed say that their responsibilities are confined to those of scholarly teachers.
Nevertheless, knowing that he may have to relinquish his seal of office at any moment, a man with only “five days as Metropolitan Governor” will surely find some means to satisfy his unfulfilled desires, still hoping that Gongchen's single net [?] might let even a fish large enough to swallow a boat slip through. Knowing that a summons may arrive before the morning is over, those who hold the reins and whip above will inevitably be lax in administering the law, while those below, who suppress their voices and hold their breath, constantly tremble before the threat of being swallowed up [?]. Can this be the original purpose of encouragement and punishment? As for the production of talented men, some places are called deep reservoirs of filial and outstanding scholars, while others are called barren lands. Thus some teachers leave their teaching mats idle and give no lectures, yet their records of achievement are already full; others teach ceaselessly, yet remain burdened with poor assessments. As for examining their learning, outside the capital the censorial authorities conduct annual examinations…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
内而銓曹較一日之長故浮華之小技立
見而眞實之隱德難知文藝之一節可師
而範模之大本無係又豈建立之初心哉
凡此者有識之所同病而執事之所以不
能忘言也歟愚竊以為馭吏之法備矣而
執法以馭吏者有其要用人之塗嚴矣而
探本以作人者有所先知要之所在則知
救弊補偏雖不可無法而所以得失之相
乘利病之相半者非法之罪也知本之所
===
先則知辨材論德雖不能以不異而所以
輕重殊勢後先殊效者非所由以進之塗
之罪也方今
聖天子明道致法運之於上二三大臣揆道守
法贊之於下鳴琴製錦之賢棟梁榱桷之
頌固當見之一得獻愚多見其贅爾
第五問
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批場中多為夷狄一策所窘間
punctuated:
内而銓曹較一日之長，故浮華之小技立見，而眞實之隱德難知；文藝之一節可師，而範模之大本無係，又豈建立之初心哉？凡此者，有識之所同病，而執事之所以不能忘言也歟？愚竊以為，馭吏之法備矣，而執法以馭吏者有其要；用人之塗嚴矣，而探本以作人者有所先。知要之所在，則知救弊補偏，雖不可無法，而所以得失之相乘、利病之相半者，非法之罪也。知本之所先，則知辨材論德，雖不能以不異，而所以輕重殊勢、後先殊效者，非所由以進之塗之罪也。方今聖天子明道致法，運之於上；二三大臣揆道守法，贊之於下。鳴琴製錦之賢、棟梁榱桷之頌，固當見之。一得獻愚，多見其贅爾。
第五問
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批：場中多為夷狄一策所窘，間
translation_en:
…while within the central government the personnel-selection authorities judge superiority by a single day’s performance. Thus superficial accomplishments are immediately apparent, while genuine, unadvertised virtue is difficult to discern. Literary accomplishment, one particular skill, may serve as a standard, while the fundamental task of providing exemplary models is left unattached [?]. Can this have been the original intention in establishing these arrangements? These are problems that all discerning people deplore, and surely the reason that you, sir, cannot refrain from speaking of them.
In my humble opinion, the laws for controlling officials are comprehensive, but there is an essential principle for those who enforce them; the avenues for recruiting men are rigorously regulated, but those who seek the root of nurturing talent must give certain things priority. Understanding where that essential principle lies, one recognizes that, although laws are indispensable for remedying abuses and correcting imbalances, it is no fault of the laws that gains and losses follow upon one another, and benefits and harms appear in equal measure. Understanding what deserves priority at the root, one recognizes that, although assessments of talent and virtue cannot avoid differences, it is no fault of the avenues through which men advance that greater and lesser weight produce different circumstances, or that differing priorities produce different results.
Today the sagely Son of Heaven elucidates the Way and brings laws to perfection, putting them into operation above; his chief ministers consider the Way and uphold the laws, assisting him below. We should surely witness worthy administrators who govern as though playing the zither or weaving brocade, and hear praise of men who serve as the pillars and rafters of the state. In offering this single humble insight, I fear I have merely added superfluous words.
Fifth Question
Song Li
Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: Many candidates in the examination hall were stymied by the policy question concerning the Yi and Di peoples. Occasionally …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有答者亦不能悉此篇直以漢事論辨亹亹不已波瀾
疊出筆力老健讀之能不令人起敬
同考試官教諭袁批策塲羣作類皆疎略於夷
狄一問尤不知所謂纏繞絲棼無以自解此篇直寫其胸
中所欲言而事意完足無復闕遺至其歸宿亦寓深
意非淺學謭聞之士必矣
考試官侍講彭批反覆漢事甚熟而文亦粲然
考試官洗馬鄭批詞氣沛然不為問目所制能
文之士也塲中諸子無出其右者矣
===
畜夷狄猶禽獸然晝之於山澤不可也闢
撤垣毀而無以備之不可也畏其噬搏而
飲食之以冀其免已雖五尺之童知其不
可矣是故至則驅之馴則豢之而已漢之
事匈奴曠世歷年詘信異變彊弱相反然
大率嚴尤之所謂下策也高帝脫平城之
困約結和親文帝通關市之使增厚賂遺
然而寇盜不衰嫚倨彌甚虜騎至於回中
烽火通於甘泉是以文帝躬擐甲之勞肄
punctuated:
有答者，亦不能悉。此篇直以漢事論辨，亹亹不已，波瀾疊出，筆力老健，讀之能不令人起敬？
同考試官教諭袁批：策塲羣作，類皆疎略，於夷狄一問，尤不知所謂，纏繞絲棼，無以自解。此篇直寫其胸中所欲言，而事意完足，無復闕遺。至其歸宿，亦寓深意，非淺學謭聞之士必矣。
考試官侍講彭批：反覆漢事甚熟，而文亦粲然。
考試官洗馬鄭批：詞氣沛然，不為問目所制，能文之士也。塲中諸子，無出其右者矣。
畜夷狄猶禽獸然，晝之於山澤，不可也；闢撤垣毀而無以備之，不可也；畏其噬搏，而飲食之以冀其免已，雖五尺之童知其不可矣。是故至則驅之，馴則豢之而已。漢之事匈奴，曠世歷年，詘信異變，彊弱相反，然大率嚴尤之所謂下策也。高帝脫平城之困，約結和親；文帝通關市之使，增厚賂遺。然而寇盜不衰，嫚倨彌甚，虜騎至於回中，烽火通於甘泉。是以文帝躬擐甲之勞，肄
translation_en:
…those who did answer could not cover the matter fully. This essay proceeds directly through discussion and argument drawn from Han affairs, developing its case tirelessly, with wave upon wave of fresh turns. Its writing is mature and vigorous: how could reading it fail to inspire respect?
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: The policy essays submitted in this examination are generally sketchy. On the question concerning the barbarians in particular, the candidates scarcely know what they are saying, becoming entangled like a mass of tangled silk, unable to extricate themselves. This essay directly expresses what its author wishes to say, while fully covering both the facts and their significance, leaving nothing out. Its conclusion also contains profound meaning. Its author is certainly no man of shallow learning and limited knowledge.
Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: His repeated examination of Han affairs shows thorough familiarity, and his writing is also brilliant.
Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: His language and spirit flow abundantly, unconstrained by the question’s individual prompts. He is an accomplished writer. None of the candidates in this examination surpasses him.
Managing the barbarians is like keeping birds and beasts. To confine them in the mountains and marshes [?] is unacceptable; to open up the defenses and tear down the walls, leaving no means of guarding against them [?], is unacceptable. To fear their biting and striking, and therefore give them food and drink in the hope of escaping harm oneself—even a child five feet tall knows that this is unacceptable. Thus, when they come, drive them away; when they submit, maintain them: that is all.
The Han dealt with the Xiongnu over many generations and years. Submission and assertion varied, and the balance of strength and weakness reversed; yet their measures were generally what Yan You called the worst policy. Emperor Gao escaped the predicament at Pingcheng and concluded a peace-through-marriage agreement. Emperor Wen established intercourse through envoys and frontier markets and increased the generous gifts sent to them. Yet raids and plundering did not diminish, and their arrogance and insolence grew still worse. Enemy cavalry reached Huizhong, and beacon alarms extended to Ganquan. Consequently, Emperor Wen personally undertook the exertion of donning armor and practiced…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
上林之射當食思賢拊髀興喟是豈和好
之足恃哉武帝選將練兵深入窮追使衛
青霍去病之徒先後出入搴旗大漠之北
登臨瀚海之陰然而中國罷耗士馬物故
報復相當桀驁自若亦豈威武之足恃哉
孝宣承先世奮擊之威值匈奴百年之運
為權時施宜之計然後羈縻外属三世賓
庭盖高文武昭之前其盛強愁然以相抗
宣元成哀之後其削弱萎然而自屈與漢
===
盛衰略相終始至論漢興以来君臣之間
謀議所持計策所出則當時之得失而後
世之明效也雖其成敗亦有出於偶然而
圖為或不叶於道義然大略有可見矣劉
敬知冒頓非可以仁義說而欲結以婚姻
之好賈誼憤首足之倒懸而欲餌以金絮
采繒之奉前後相違卑陋無取若夫乗邊
之士至數十萬人固已羅絡山川而包囊險
翳其為防可謂周矣然疲於東西之奔命無
punctuated:
上林之射，當食思賢，拊髀興喟，是豈和好之足恃哉？武帝選將練兵，深入窮追，使衛青、霍去病之徒先後出入，搴旗大漠之北，登臨瀚海之陰。然而中國罷耗，士馬物故，報復相當，桀驁自若，亦豈威武之足恃哉？孝宣承先世奮擊之威，值匈奴百年之運，為權時施宜之計，然後羈縻外属，三世賓庭。盖高、文、武、昭之前，其盛強愁然以相抗；宣、元、成、哀之後，其削弱萎然而自屈，與漢盛衰略相終始。至論漢興以来，君臣之間謀議所持、計策所出，則當時之得失，而後世之明效也。雖其成敗亦有出於偶然，而圖為或不叶於道義，然大略有可見矣。

劉敬知冒頓非可以仁義說，而欲結以婚姻之好；賈誼憤首足之倒懸，而欲餌以金絮采繒之奉。前後相違，卑陋無取。若夫乗邊之士至數十萬人，固已羅絡山川而包囊險翳，其為防可謂周矣。然疲於東西之奔命，無
translation_en:
…archery in Shanglin Park; at his meals he thought of worthy men, slapped his thigh, and sighed. How could peaceful relations have been sufficient to rely upon? Emperor Wu selected generals and trained troops, penetrating deep into enemy territory and pursuing them to the utmost. He sent men such as Wei Qing and Huo Qubing on successive expeditions, capturing banners north of the great desert and advancing to the northern side of the Hanhai. Yet the central realm was exhausted and depleted, soldiers and horses perished, and retaliation on either side matched the other, while the enemy remained as unruly as ever. How, then, could military might have been sufficient to rely upon? Emperor Xiaoxuan inherited the awe inspired by the vigorous assaults of earlier reigns and encountered the turning of the Xiongnu’s century-long fortunes. He devised expedients suited to the circumstances, and only then were they loosely bound as external subjects, paying court for three generations. In the earlier period of Emperors Gao, Wen, Wu, and Zhao, the Xiongnu were flourishing and strong, confronting the Han in anxiety [?]; in the later period of Emperors Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, and Ai, they were diminished and weak, languishing and submitting of their own accord. Their rise and decline roughly coincided with those of the Han. As for the deliberations maintained and strategies proposed between rulers and ministers since the rise of the Han, these constituted the successes and failures of their own time and supplied clear evidence of their effects for later generations. Although their successes and failures sometimes arose from chance, and their designs and actions sometimes failed to accord with the Way and righteousness, their broad outlines can nevertheless be discerned.

Liu Jing knew that Modu could not be persuaded through benevolence and righteousness, yet wished to bind him through a marriage alliance. Jia Yi was indignant that head and feet had been turned upside down, yet wished to entice the Xiongnu with offerings of gold, silk floss, and colored silks. Their proposals contradicted their premises: they were ignoble and shallow, with nothing worth adopting. As for the soldiers stationed along the frontier, numbering several hundred thousand, they already formed a network across mountains and rivers, encompassing difficult and concealed terrain. Their defensive arrangements could indeed be called comprehensive. Yet they were exhausted by rushing east and west to answer commands, unable to…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
救吏民之侵掠安在其為防也西域之通至
三十餘國謂將斷其右臂而離其外交其為
謀可謂得矣然首鼠陰持於兩属反覆常
伺於弱疆安在其為謀也至於望之建敵
國不臣之議而荀悅有僭度失序之譏誠
以彼之自倨自侈倔疆於域中固不必彊而臣
之而来享来王使命之加遺亦不當抗而
尊之也故以愚論斷之衛青霍去病之舉
猶獸而欲盡之於山澤者也劉敬賈誼之
===
策畏其噬搏而飲食之者也其謂選武略
之臣修障隧之具属長戟勁努之械則知
撤關毀垣之不可而欲備之者也得陵廣
之材勇不若用充國之善勝賞甘陳之竒
節不若推魏尚之善守此又欲備之者之
所宜知也善乎班孟堅之言之也以為與
結約則耗費而見欺就征伐則勞師而招
寇是以外而不內疎而不戚其来也懲而
禦之其去也備而守之其靡服也隨宜而
punctuated: 救吏民之侵掠，安在其為防也？西域之通至三十餘國，謂將斷其右臂而離其外交，其為謀可謂得矣。然首鼠陰持於兩属，反覆常伺於弱疆，安在其為謀也？至於望之建敵國不臣之議，而荀悅有僭度失序之譏，誠以彼之自倨自侈，倔疆於域中，固不必彊而臣之；而来享来王，使命之加遺，亦不當抗而尊之也。故以愚論斷之，衛青、霍去病之舉，猶獸而欲盡之於山澤者也；劉敬、賈誼之策，畏其噬搏而飲食之者也。其謂選武略之臣，修障隧之具，属長戟勁努之械，則知撤關毀垣之不可而欲備之者也。得陵、廣之材勇，不若用充國之善勝；賞甘、陳之竒節，不若推魏尚之善守。此又欲備之者之所宜知也。善乎班孟堅之言之也！以為：與結約則耗費而見欺，就征伐則勞師而招寇。是以外而不內，疎而不戚。其来也，懲而禦之；其去也，備而守之；其靡服也，隨宜而
translation_en:
…save officials and commoners from raids and plunder—where, then, is the effectiveness of such defense? Relations were opened with more than thirty states in the Western Regions, supposedly to sever the enemy’s right arm and detach its foreign allies. This might be called a sound strategy. Yet these states wavered, secretly maintaining allegiance to both sides, repeatedly shifting as they watched the relative weakness and strength [?] of each. Where, then, is the effectiveness of such a strategy? As for Xiao Wangzhi’s proposal to treat them as an equal state rather than as subjects, Xun Yue criticized it as overstepping proper bounds and upsetting the established order. Indeed, though they are arrogant and extravagant, stubbornly asserting their strength within their own territory, there is no need to force them into subjection. Yet when they come to present tribute and acknowledge the sovereign, and envoys are dispatched with gifts, neither should they be elevated and honored as equals.

Thus, in my humble judgment, the campaigns of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing treated them as beasts to be exterminated in the mountains and marshes. The policies of Liu Jing and Jia Yi were those of men who, fearing the beasts’ bites and attacks, fed them.
