The proposal to select ministers skilled in military strategy, repair frontier forts and beacon towers [?], and assemble long halberds and powerful crossbows [?] recognized that dismantling the passes and demolishing the walls was unacceptable, and sought to prepare defenses against them. Obtaining the talent and courage of Li Ling and Li Guang is less valuable than employing Zhao Chongguo’s skill in securing victory; rewarding the extraordinary resolve of Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang is less valuable than promoting Wei Shang’s skill in defense. This, too, is something those who wish to prepare defenses should understand.

How well Ban Mengjian expressed it! He held that making treaties with them incurred expense and invited deception, while undertaking punitive campaigns exhausted the army and provoked raids. Therefore, they should be kept outside rather than brought within, held at a distance rather than treated as kin. When they come, punish and repel them; when they leave, make preparations and maintain defenses; when they yield in submission, act as circumstances require and…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
接之使在我有可恃之勢而在彼無得乗
之機亦庶乎其有見焉雖然書曰無怠無
荒四夷来王又曰惇德允元蠻夷率服漢
之諸臣豈足以與此
punctuated: 接之，使在我有可恃之勢，而在彼無得乗之機，亦庶乎其有見焉。雖然，《書》曰：「無怠無荒，四夷来王。」又曰：「惇德允元，蠻夷率服。」漢之諸臣，豈足以與此？
translation_en: …receive them [accordingly], so that on our side there is a dependable position of strength, and on their side there is no opportunity they can exploit—in this he came close to having true insight. Even so, the Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Without idleness or neglect, the four barbarian tribes will come to acknowledge the king's rule." And it also says: "Cultivate virtue and trust the good, and the southern and eastern barbarians will all submit." How could the various ministers of the Han dynasty be worthy of participating in this?

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄後序
上命臣璟臣教來考順天鄉試既
畢事臣教謹敘論其意於錄
後夫取人之不廢言也舊矣
書曰敷奏以言又曰詢事考
言文則言之成章而著者也
自漢以來充賦有司而登其
===
說於王庭者可考見已至于
今莫之有改蓋言之不可廢
也如此然以唐虞明良之盛
猶致意於靜庸之際而後世
之品藻文藝差次事功亦每
岐而論之則又以見言之難
將已
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄後序

上命臣璟、臣教來考順天鄉試。既畢事，臣教謹敘論其意於錄後。夫取人之不廢言也，舊矣。《書》曰：「敷奏以言。」又曰：「詢事考言。」文則言之成章而著者也。自漢以來，充賦有司而登其說於王庭者，可考見已。至于今，莫之有改，蓋言之不可廢也如此。然以唐虞明良之盛，猶致意於靜庸之際，而後世之品藻文藝、差次事功，亦每岐而論之，則又以見言之難將已。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Provincial Examination

His Majesty commanded your servants Jing 璟 and Jiao 教 to come and serve as Examiners for the Shuntian Provincial Examination. Now that the work is completed, I, your servant Jiao, respectfully discuss its significance at the end of the record. The practice of considering a person's words when selecting men for office is ancient. The Book of Documents says, “They presented their statements in words,” and also, “Examine their deeds and scrutinize their words.” Writing is speech formed into ordered compositions and set down in a visible form. Since the Han dynasty, instances of men being presented by the responsible authorities and submitting their views at the royal court can be traced in the records. Down to the present, this practice has remained unchanged. Such is the indispensability of words. Yet even amid the flourishing rule of enlightened sovereigns and worthy ministers under Yao and Shun, attention was still paid to the distinction between fine words and actual conduct. In later ages, too, the appraisal of literary accomplishment and the ranking of achievements in office have frequently been discussed separately. This further reveals the difficulty of judging men by words [?].

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
陛下在位今十有三年益明習
國家事方勵精求人以振庶功
小大之臣奔走恐懼仰承
威命而臣猥以文字充乏適當
任使大懼無以稱塞
明詔蓋鄉舉取士公卿輔相且
將階級焉事至重也其敢不
===
共況天府之士畿內之秀四
方游學之英宜有卓異以備
異時登簡顧臣之淺昧何足
以知之雖然畢力於文辭論
議之間而精察舉之任此臣
事力所及也若夫恢宏碩大
之器剛方敦厚之質疏通敏
punctuated: 陛下在位今十有三年，益明習國家事，方勵精求人，以振庶功。小大之臣奔走恐懼，仰承威命，而臣猥以文字充乏，適當任使，大懼無以稱塞明詔。蓋鄉舉取士，公卿輔相且將階級焉，事至重也，其敢不共？況天府之士，畿內之秀，四方游學之英，宜有卓異，以備異時登簡。顧臣之淺昧，何足以知之？雖然，畢力於文辭論議之間，而精察舉之任，此臣事力所及也。若夫恢宏碩大之器，剛方敦厚之質，疏通敏
translation_en:
Your Majesty has now occupied the throne for thirteen years and has become ever more thoroughly versed in the affairs of state. You are devoting your energies to seeking worthy men so that all undertakings may flourish. Your servants, high and low, hasten about their duties in fearful vigilance, reverently receiving your august commands. I, your unworthy servant, have been called upon to fill a vacancy on the strength of my literary ability. Now entrusted with this commission, I greatly fear that I have no means of adequately fulfilling your enlightened edict. For the selection of men through the Provincial Examination provides the steps by which high ministers and chief councillors will advance. This is a matter of the utmost importance: how could I dare fail to treat it reverently?
Moreover, among the scholars of the metropolitan prefecture—the outstanding men of the capital region and the finest of those who have travelled from all quarters to study—there should be men of exceptional distinction, ready for selection and advancement in the future. Yet how could my shallow understanding suffice to recognize them? Nevertheless, to exert all my strength in examining their literary compositions and arguments, and to discharge with discernment the responsibility of scrutiny and recommendation: this lies within the scope of my duties and abilities. As for men of broad and ample capacity, of upright and steadfast character, sincere and generous in disposition, and of penetrating and quick…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
達之才由是有得焉此則臣
之志也
翰林院侍講彭教謹序
punctuated:
達之才，由是有得焉，此則臣之志也。
翰林院侍講彭教謹序。
translation_en:
…and perceptive talents may thereby be obtained—this, then, is your servant's aspiration.
Respectfully prefaced by Peng Jiao 彭教, Expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

text: 順天府鄉試錄成化十三年
punctuated: 順天府鄉試錄，成化十三年。

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄序
國朝求賢於天下三歲一大比而
賓興之
京師天下之本而直隸州郡皆畿
甸也乃合諸生及太學之士試
之順天府其考校也必
詔詞臣主之其命題也必經
===
進而後頒其取士之數則視諸大
藩加十五重之也成化十三年
秋適維其期挟藝就試者二千
五百人雲集
闕下前此未有也府丞臣英以考
試官請於是洗馬臣環侍講臣
教承
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄序
國朝求賢於天下，三歲一大比而賓興之。京師，天下之本，而直隸州郡皆畿甸也，乃合諸生及太學之士試之順天府。其考校也，必詔詞臣主之；其命題也，必經進而後頒；其取士之數，則視諸大藩加十五，重之也。成化十三年秋，適維其期，挟藝就試者二千五百人，雲集闕下，前此未有也。府丞臣英以考試官請，於是洗馬臣環、侍講臣教承
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination

Our dynasty seeks out the worthy throughout the realm, holding a grand triennial competition to ceremonially recommend and promote them. The Capital is the foundation of the realm, and the directly attached subprefectures and prefectures are all part of the imperial domain; therefore, the government students from these regions and the scholars of the Directorate of Education are gathered together and examined at Shuntian Prefecture. As for the evaluation, an imperial edict always commands literary officials of the Hanlin Academy to preside over it; as for the examination questions, they must first be presented to the throne before being promulgated; and as for the quota of scholars selected, it exceeds that of the major provinces by forty-five, showing the great importance attached to it.

In the autumn of the thirteenth year of the Chenghua reign (1477), the scheduled time arrived. Those who brought their literary skills to sit for the examination numbered two thousand five hundred men, gathering like clouds beneath the Palace Towers—a scale unprecedented before this. The Vice Prefect of Shuntian, your servant Ying, petitioned for the appointment of Examiners. Thereupon, the Librarian of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, your servant Huan, and the Expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, your servant Jiao, received…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
上命涖其事翌日
陛辭入院時同考官學正臣淵登教
諭臣尚彜臣澄臣璧臣富訓導臣
岳臣存臣境監試官御史臣進
臣仁而提調則臣英也洎諸執
事咸集相與戒誓務精白一心
恪共乃事以仰副
===
朝廷委任之盛意闈棘三試之得
士百三十五人錄其名氏及文
之優者以
獻臣謹敘諸首竊惟政化與氣運
相爲流通而賢才係焉政化盛
則氣運盛氣運盛則賢才亦從
而盛唐虞之際萬邦黎獻共惟
punctuated:
上命涖其事。翌日，陛辭入院。時同考官學正臣淵登，教諭臣尚彜、臣澄、臣璧、臣富，訓導臣岳、臣存、臣境；監試官御史臣進、臣仁，而提調則臣英也。洎諸執事咸集，相與戒誓，務精白一心，恪共乃事，以仰副朝廷委任之盛意。闈棘三試之，得士百三十五人，錄其名氏及文之優者以獻。臣謹敘諸首。
竊惟政化與氣運相爲流通，而賢才係焉。政化盛，則氣運盛；氣運盛，則賢才亦從而盛。唐虞之際，萬邦黎獻共惟
translation_en:
…received His Majesty’s command to oversee the matter. The following day, they took leave of His Majesty and entered the examination compound. The Associate Examiners were your servant Yuandeng, a School Instructor; your servants Shangyi, Cheng, Bi, and Fu, County School Instructors; and your servants Yue, Cun, and Jing, Assistant Instructors. The examination monitors were your servants Jin and Ren, Investigating Censors, while your servant Ying served as Proctor. When all the other functionaries had assembled, they admonished one another and pledged to act with purity and singleness of purpose, respectfully discharging their duties so as to fulfill the court’s generous intent in entrusting them with these appointments. Within the thorn-enclosed examination compound, the candidates were examined in three sessions, and 135 men were selected. Their names and the best of their writings were recorded for presentation to His Majesty. Your servant has respectfully written this preface at the beginning.
I humbly reflect that governance and moral transformation interact with the movement of cosmic forces, and that the flourishing of worthy talent depends upon them. When governance and moral transformation flourish, cosmic forces flourish; when cosmic forces flourish, worthy talent flourishes accordingly. In the age of Tang and Yu, the many worthies of the myriad states were all …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
帝臣而周之藹藹吉士必於土
宇孔厚之日見之故其生也有
自来其出也有所為又將以資
國家之用隆太平之業而氣化
愈久而愈盛矣我
朝自
太祖高皇帝光啟文明之運
===
列聖相承至于
皇上重熈累洽百有餘年氣化益隆
賢才彙進熈
帝載而贊
皇猷者濟濟其盛矧京畿故燕趙之
地號多豪傑今四方萬國環視
內向衣冠禮樂聲明文物之華
punctuated:
帝臣，而周之藹藹吉士，必於土宇孔厚之日見之。故其生也有自来，其出也有所為，又將以資國家之用，隆太平之業，而氣化愈久而愈盛矣。
我朝自太祖高皇帝光啟文明之運，列聖相承，至于皇上，重熈累洽百有餘年，氣化益隆，賢才彙進，熈帝載而贊皇猷者，濟濟其盛。矧京畿，故燕趙之地，號多豪傑。今四方萬國環視內向，衣冠禮樂、聲明文物之華
translation_en:
…ministers of the sovereign; and the Zhou dynasty’s abundant worthy gentlemen appeared precisely when its dominion was vast. Thus, the birth of such men has its origins, and their emergence has its purpose: they will serve the needs of the state and advance the enterprise of great peace, so that the transforming vital forces grow ever more flourishing with time.
Since Emperor Taizu Gao inaugurated an age of luminous civilization for our dynasty, successive sage rulers have carried it forward down to His Majesty. For more than a hundred years, brilliance has followed brilliance and peace has accumulated upon peace. The transforming vital forces have grown increasingly abundant, and worthy talents have advanced together. Those who further the imperial undertakings and assist the sovereign’s plans are numerous indeed. How much more so in the metropolitan region, the former lands of Yan and Zhao, famed for their many outstanding men! Now the myriad states of the four quarters look toward it and turn inward in allegiance; the splendor of ceremonial dress, rites and music, illustrious institutions and cultural refinement…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
於是乎萃而瑰瑋卓絕之才揚
芳振烈相望後先諸士子生長
於斯觀光於斯得於漸摩涵育
之最先者能不顒顒而起乎詩
曰思皇多士生此王國王國克
生惟周之楨際
聖明之時預賢良之薦先天下之士
貢之
天子之庭何其幸歟行當捷春闈奉
大對而駸駸嚮用矣必思有以自
振上忠于
君而澤下加于民樹勳業于時佐
盛治於無窮庶幾爲
國之楨而趾美乎前修將天下後
punctuated: 於是乎萃，而瑰瑋卓絕之才，揚芳振烈，相望後先。諸士子生長於斯，觀光於斯，得於漸摩涵育之最先者，能不顒顒而起乎？《詩》曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，惟周之楨。」際聖明之時，預賢良之薦，先天下之士，貢之天子之庭，何其幸歟！行當捷春闈，奉大對，而駸駸嚮用矣。必思有以自振，上忠于君，而澤下加于民，樹勳業于時，佐盛治於無窮，庶幾爲國之楨，而趾美乎前修，將天下後
translation_en: … are gathered right here, and extraordinary, outstanding talents, spreading their fragrant reputation and rousing illustrious deeds, follow one after another in unbroken succession. All you scholars who were born and raised here, who behold the glory of the realm here, and who are the very first to benefit from its gradual refinement and nurturing cultivation—how could you not rise up with earnest aspiration? The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "How splendid are the many scholars, born in this royal domain! The royal domain is able to bear them; they are the pillars of Zhou." Encountering an era of sacred enlightenment, participating in the recommendation of the worthy and good, and being presented to the court of the Son of Heaven ahead of all the scholars of the realm—how fortunate that is! Soon you shall triumph in the spring Metropolitan Examination, present your great replies at the Palace Examination, and advance rapidly into official employment. You must reflect on how to rouse yourselves: above, be loyal to the Sovereign, and below, extend blessings to the people; establish meritorious achievements in this age, and assist the flourishing governance forevermore. In this way, you may perhaps become pillars of the State and follow in the fine footsteps of the worthies of old, so that all under heaven and future…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
世稱之曰邦畿之士也顧不偉
歟其毋庸庸無爲碌碌無聞自
負自棄於
明朝俾時之人多前修而不之齒
也
司經局洗馬鄭環謹序
punctuated:
世稱之曰：「邦畿之士也。」顧不偉歟？其毋庸庸無爲，碌碌無聞，自負自棄於明朝，俾時之人多前修而不之齒也。

司經局洗馬鄭環謹序。
translation_en:
… generations will praise them, saying, “These are scholars of the capital region.” Would this not be splendid? Let them not remain mediocre and inactive, undistinguished and unknown, failing themselves and abandoning their aspirations under this enlightened dynasty, so that their contemporaries esteem their worthy predecessors but refuse to count them among their number.

Preface respectfully written by Zheng Huan, Librarian in the Office of Classics and Documents.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
立則見其參於前也在輿則見其倚於衡
也
夫微之顯誠之不可揜如此夫
堯以不得舜為己憂舜以不得禹皐陶為
己憂夫以百畝之不易為己憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠教人以善謂之忠
為天下得人者謂之仁
===
易
泰小往大来吉亨彖曰泰小往大来吉亨
則是天地交而萬物通也上下交而其
志同也內陽而外陰內健而外順內君
子而外小人君子道長小人道消也
无平不陂无往不復艱貞无咎勿恤其孚
于食有福象曰无往不復天地際也
无所往其来復吉有攸往夙吉
富有之謂大業日新之謂盛德生生之謂
易
河出圖洛出書聖人則之
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

立則見其參於前也，在輿則見其倚於衡也。

夫微之顯，誠之不可揜，如此夫！

堯以不得舜為己憂，舜以不得禹皐陶為己憂。夫以百畝之不易為己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠，為天下得人者謂之仁。

易

泰，小往大来，吉亨。彖曰：「泰，小往大来，吉亨，則是天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。內陽而外陰，內健而外順，內君子而外小人，君子道長，小人道消也。」

无平不陂，无往不復。艱貞，无咎。勿恤其孚，于食有福。象曰：「无往不復，天地際也。」

无所往，其来復吉；有攸往，夙吉。

富有之謂大業，日新之謂盛德，生生之謂易。

河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

When standing, see it present before you; when riding in a carriage, see it resting against the crossbar.

Such is the manifestness of the subtle, and such is the impossibility of concealing sincerity!

Yao regarded failing to obtain Shun as his own cause for concern; Shun regarded failing to obtain Yu and Gao Yao as his own cause for concern. One who regards leaving his hundred mu of land untilled as his own cause for concern is a farmer. Sharing wealth with others is called generosity; teaching others goodness is called loyalty; obtaining worthy men for all under Heaven is called benevolence.

Book of Changes

Peace (Tai): the small departs and the great comes; auspicious and successful. The Commentary on the Judgment says: “In Peace, the small departs and the great comes; auspicious and successful. This means that Heaven and Earth interact and the myriad things communicate freely; those above and those below interact and share the same purpose. Within is yang and without is yin; within is strength and without is compliance; within are noble men and without are petty men. The way of noble men grows, and the way of petty men declines.”

There is no level ground without a slope, no departure without a return. Be steadfast amid difficulty, and there will be no blame. Do not worry about its trustworthiness; you will enjoy blessings in your sustenance. The Commentary on the Image says: “No departure without a return: this is the juncture of Heaven and Earth.”

If there is nowhere to go, returning is auspicious; if there is somewhere to go, an early start is auspicious.

Abundant possession is called a great undertaking; daily renewal is called flourishing virtue; generation upon generation is called change.

The Yellow River brought forth the Chart, and the Luo River brought forth the Writing; the sages took them as models.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
書
夙夜惟寅直哉惟清
任官惟賢才左右惟其人臣爲上爲德爲
下爲民其難其慎惟和惟一
伻來毖殷乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣曰明禋
拜手稽首休享
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
===
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼既同上入執宫功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乗屋其始播
百穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌
陰四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭九月肅霜十
月滌場朋酒斯饗曰殺羔羊躋彼公堂
稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
我田既臧農夫之慶
豈弟君子民之父母
猗與那與置我鼗鼓奏鼓簡簡衎我烈祖
punctuated:
書
夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。
任官惟賢才，左右惟其人。臣爲上爲德，爲下爲民，其難其慎，惟和惟一。
伻來毖殷，乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣，曰明禋。拜手稽首，休享。
六卿分職，各率其屬，以倡九牧，阜成兆民。

詩
九月築場圃，十月納禾稼：黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫，我稼既同，上入執宫功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乗屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。九月肅霜，十月滌場。朋酒斯饗，曰殺羔羊。躋彼公堂，稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆！
我田既臧，農夫之慶。
豈弟君子，民之父母。
猗與那與！置我鼗鼓，奏鼓簡簡，衎我烈祖，
translation_en:
Book of Documents
Be reverent morning and night; be upright and pure.
Appoint only the worthy and talented to office, and place only suitable men at your side. Ministers serve their sovereign above by fostering virtue, and those below by serving the people. Treat this task as difficult and exercise caution; maintain harmony and unity of purpose.
You sent instructions to exercise care in governing Yin, then ordered that I be reassured with two vessels of aromatic black-millet wine, declaring it to be for a pure sacrifice. I bow with hands together and touch my forehead to the ground, presenting this fine offering.
The six ministers divide their duties, each leading his subordinates to guide the governors of the nine regions and bring prosperity and good order to the myriad people.

Book of Odes
In the ninth month we prepare the threshing grounds and garden plots; in the tenth month we bring in the crops: broomcorn and foxtail millet, late-ripening and early-ripening grain, rice, hemp, beans, and wheat. Ah, we farmers! Once our crops are gathered, we go up to undertake work on the houses. By day you gather thatch; by night you twist ropes. Hurry to roof the houses, for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains. In the days of the second month, we cut ice with ringing blows; in the days of the third month, we store it in the icehouse. Early in the days of the fourth month, we offer a lamb and sacrifice chives. In the ninth month the frost is keen; in the tenth month we clear the threshing ground. With paired jars of wine we hold a feast and slaughter lambs. We ascend the lord’s hall and raise the rhinoceros-horn cup: may he live ten thousand years without end!
Our fields have yielded well: this is the farmers’ joy.
The gracious and amiable lord is the father and mother of the people.
Ah, how splendid, how abundant! Set out our pellet drums and drums; beat the drums with resounding strokes, gladdening our glorious ancestor…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
湯孫奏假綏我思成鞉鼓淵淵嘒嘒管
聲既和且平依我磬聲於赫湯孫穆穆
厥聲庸鼓有斁萬舞有奕我有嘉客亦
不夷懌自古在昔先民有作温恭朝夕
執事有恪顧予烝嘗湯孫之將
春秋
天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵〔隱公元年〕
翬帥師會宋公陳侯蔡人衞人伐鄭〔四年〕
〔年〕王人子突救衞〔莊公六年〕季子来歸〔閔〕
===
〔公元年〕
齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊公〕
〔十三年〕
晋侯入曹執曹伯畀宋人晋侯齊師宋
師秦師及楚人戰于城濮楚師敗績
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衞子莒
子盟于踐土〔並僖公二十八年〕
楚公子貞伐鄭〔襄公八年〕公會晋侯宋公
衞侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯
punctuated:
湯孫奏假，綏我思成。鞉鼓淵淵，嘒嘒管聲。既和且平，依我磬聲。於赫湯孫，穆穆厥聲。庸鼓有斁，萬舞有奕。我有嘉客，亦不夷懌？自古在昔，先民有作。温恭朝夕，執事有恪。顧予烝嘗，湯孫之將。

《春秋》
天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵。〔隱公元年〕
翬帥師會宋公、陳侯、蔡人、衞人伐鄭。〔四年〕
〔年〕王人子突救衞。〔莊公六年〕季子来歸。〔閔〕〔公元年〕
齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏。〔莊公〕〔十三年〕
晋侯入曹，執曹伯，畀宋人。晋侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績。公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衞子、莒子盟于踐土。〔並僖公二十八年〕
楚公子貞伐鄭。〔襄公八年〕公會晋侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯
translation_en:
…Tang’s descendant comes forward to present his offerings; grant peace to us and fulfill our wishes. The hand drums and great drums resound deeply; the pipes sound clear and high. Harmonious and balanced, they accord with our sounding stones. Ah, glorious is Tang’s descendant; solemn is his music. The great bells and drums sound in abundance; the myriad dance is splendid. We have honored guests: are they not content and delighted? From ancient times, our forebears established these practices: gentle and reverent morning and evening, respectful in performing their duties. Look favorably upon our winter and autumn sacrifices, the offerings presented by Tang’s descendant.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The Heavenly King sent the Steward, Xuan, to deliver funeral gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi. 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕
Hui led an army to join the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and men of Cai and Wei in attacking Zheng. 〔Fourth year.〕
〔“Year”: displaced annotation [?].〕 Zitu, an officer of the king, came to Wei’s rescue. 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 Jizi returned. 〔First year of Duke Min; the annotation is split in the transcription.〕
The Marquis of Qi and men of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu met at Beixing. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
The Marquis of Jin entered Cao, seized the Earl of Cao, and handed him over to the men of Song. The Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought the men of Chu at Chengpu; the Chu army was routed. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju in making a covenant at Jiantu. 〔All in the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.〕
Prince Zhen of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, and the Earl of Qi…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
小邾齊世子光伐鄭同盟于戲九年公
會晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世
子光滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭戍鄭
虎牢楚公子貞救鄭十年公會晋侯宋
公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭同盟于亳城北
公會晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會
于蕭魚十一年
===
禮記
天子七廟諸侯五大夫三士一天子之豆
二十有六諸公十有六諸侯十有二上
大夫八下大夫六
少事長賤事貴共帥時
是故君子無物而不在禮矣
子民如父母有憯怛之愛有忠利之教親
而尊安而敬威而愛富而有禮惠而能
散
punctuated:
小邾、齊世子光伐鄭，同盟于戲，九年。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，戍鄭虎牢；楚公子貞救鄭，十年。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，同盟于亳城北。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚，十一年。

禮記
天子七廟，諸侯五，大夫三，士一。天子之豆二十有六，諸公十有六，諸侯十有二，上大夫八，下大夫六。
少事長，賤事貴，共帥時。
是故君子無物而不在禮矣。
子民如父母，有憯怛之愛，有忠利之教，親而尊，安而敬，威而愛，富而有禮，惠而能散。
translation_en:
…[the ruler of] Xiao Zhu and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, attacked Zheng and jointly covenanted at Xi. Ninth year [of Duke Xiang]. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju and Zhu, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu in attacking Zheng. They garrisoned Hulao in Zheng. Zhen, a ducal son of Chu, came to Zheng’s aid. Tenth year. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu in attacking Zheng. They jointly covenanted north of Bocheng. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. Eleventh year.

Record of Rites (Liji)
The Son of Heaven has seven ancestral temples; the feudal lords, five; grand masters, three; and gentlemen, one. The Son of Heaven has twenty-six dou offering vessels; dukes, sixteen; other feudal lords, twelve; senior grand masters, eight; and junior grand masters, six.
The young serve their elders, and those of low status serve those of high status; all follow this order.
Thus, for the gentleman, nothing lies outside ritual propriety.
Cherish the people as parents cherish their children, with deeply compassionate love and teaching that is devoted to their welfare. Be affectionate yet dignified, at ease yet reverent, awe-inspiring yet loving, wealthy yet observant of ritual propriety, benevolent and willing to distribute your resources.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:

論
聖人太極之全體
詔誥表內科一道

translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse
“The sage embodies the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.”

One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose a hypothetical Han edict dispatching Grand Masters of Palace Leisure to travel throughout the empire on inspection.

Five Legal Judgments
The unauthorized establishment of official posts and appointment of personnel.
Failure to meet the appointed deadline when accompanying a military expedition.
The illicit casting of copper coins.
The fabrication of auspicious portents.
Improper adjudication of crimes.

Third Session

Policy Question

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
對時宜物先幾前用而又妙探本原識
達遠大如
三誥之論治大祀文之論理大哉
王言非秦漢以下帝王名能文學者所能及
也昔有以馬上得天下者而三侯之章
論者亦以為壯麗雄偉近古未有若汾
上之辭橫槊之賦貞觀開元之製作則
皆成於少習與學士大夫争長者然究
觀規模考論旨歸盖亦少貶矣是則所
===
謂文者豈無與於學歟昔人有謂帝王
之學與常人不同者豈或以此歟而又
有以為帝王之學與常人同者其說安
在夫仰瞻
聖祖之製而評隲近代諸君猶日月之於衆星
可覩也請敬陳之
問太極西銘相傳為理學之宗然或者謂
太極之傳出於种放無極之論近於老
氏西銘有平施而無稱物流於兼愛其
punctuated:
對時宜物，先幾前用，而又妙探本原，識達遠大。如《三誥》之論治，《大祀文》之論理，大哉王言！非秦漢以下帝王名能文學者所能及也。昔有以馬上得天下者，而《三侯》之章，論者亦以為壯麗雄偉，近古未有。若汾上之辭、橫槊之賦、貞觀開元之製作，則皆成於少習，與學士大夫争長者。然究觀規模，考論旨歸，盖亦少貶矣。是則所謂文者，豈無與於學歟？昔人有謂帝王之學與常人不同者，豈或以此歟？而又有以為帝王之學與常人同者，其說安在？夫仰瞻聖祖之製，而評隲近代諸君，猶日月之於衆星，可覩也。請敬陳之。
問：《太極》《西銘》相傳為理學之宗。然或者謂《太極》之傳出於种放，無極之論近於老氏；《西銘》有平施而無稱物，流於兼愛。其
translation_en:
…responding to the times and fitting things to their circumstances, anticipating incipient developments and acting before the need arises; moreover, they probe the root and source with subtlety, displaying far-reaching and expansive understanding. Consider the discussion of governance in the Three Pronouncements and the discussion of principle in the Text for the Great Sacrifice: how magnificent are these royal utterances! They are beyond the reach of those emperors from the Qin and Han onward who were renowned for literary ability and learning. In former times there was one who won the empire on horseback, yet critics also regarded his composition on the “Three Marquises” [?] as splendid and majestic, without precedent in recent antiquity. As for the verses composed beside the Fen River, the rhapsody declaimed with lance held crosswise, and the writings of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, all arose from practice in youth and competed for preeminence with the work of scholars and scholar-officials. Yet when we thoroughly examine their scope and assess their ultimate purport, they must, it seems, be ranked somewhat lower. Can what we call literary composition, then, have nothing to do with learning? Some men of old said that the learning of emperors differs from that of ordinary people: might this have been their reason? Others, however, have held that the learning of emperors is the same as that of ordinary people. On what grounds does their argument rest? When we look up reverently at the writings of our sagely founder and appraise the rulers of more recent ages, the distinction is as plain as that between the sun and moon and the multitude of stars. Please set forth your views with due reverence.
Question: The Supreme Ultimate and the Western Inscription have traditionally been regarded as foundational texts of the Learning of Principle. Some, however, maintain that the transmission of the Supreme Ultimate originated with Chong Fang, and that its discussion of the Limitless approaches the teachings of Laozi; they also maintain that the Western Inscription advocates equal benevolence without weighing the distinctions among things, thereby lapsing into indiscriminate love. Their…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
說亦有所見歟而又有稱其首尾相因
脉絡貫通理一分殊名虛理實者說者
謂數語足以盡二書之旨諸生苟以為
然幸為我一二言之
問書曰汝則有大疑謀及卿士謀及庶人
古之人舉事興為未有不詢之下者然
甲可乙否言人人殊將以為可用而用
之不可用而舍之矣然固有因而成功
亦有因而僨事者是則吾何適從試舉
===
古人一二事與諸士子論之撓楚之計
則借箸之籌不同於豎儒之說馬邑之
役則老將之見不附於習胡事者之謀
曹魏之下江陵有畫策拒之者矣彼長
江共之之言何見晋武之議平吳有上
表請之者矣彼以秦涼為憂者何謂苻
堅決投鞭斷流之策而太極之議寧不
謂其然宋文銳席卷趙魏之志而步兵
之諫嘗不以為可高麗之伐大臣勸之
punctuated:
說亦有所見歟？而又有稱其首尾相因、脉絡貫通、理一分殊、名虛理實者，說者謂數語足以盡二書之旨。諸生苟以為然，幸為我一二言之。
問：《書》曰：「汝則有大疑，謀及卿士，謀及庶人。」古之人舉事興為，未有不詢之下者。然甲可乙否，言人人殊，將以為可用而用之，不可用而舍之矣。然固有因而成功，亦有因而僨事者，是則吾何適從？試舉古人一二事，與諸士子論之。撓楚之計，則借箸之籌不同於豎儒之說；馬邑之役，則老將之見不附於習胡事者之謀。曹魏之下江陵，有畫策拒之者矣，彼長江共之之言何見？晋武之議平吳，有上表請之者矣，彼以秦涼為憂者何謂？苻堅決投鞭斷流之策，而太極之議寧不謂其然？宋文銳席卷趙魏之志，而步兵之諫嘗不以為可。高麗之伐，大臣勸之，
translation_en:
…did this view also have some grounds? Yet others praise these works for the way their beginnings and endings follow from one another, their threads of reasoning run throughout, their principle is one while its particular manifestations differ, and their terms are abstract while their principles are substantial. Commentators say that these few phrases suffice to encompass the purport of the two works. If you students agree, kindly explain this to me in a few words.
Question: The Book of Documents says: “When you have a great doubt, consult the high ministers and officers, and consult the common people.” Whenever the ancients undertook an enterprise, they invariably consulted those below them. Yet one person approves and another objects, and everyone says something different. Presumably one adopts what one judges usable and discards what one judges unusable. Nevertheless, following advice has sometimes brought success and sometimes brought affairs to ruin. Whom, then, should we follow? Let us take a few incidents involving the ancients and discuss them with you candidates. In the plan to weaken Chu, the strategy illustrated with borrowed chopsticks differed from the proposal of the paltry scholar. In the operation at Mayi, the veteran general’s judgment did not accord with the plan of the man familiar with the affairs of the Hu. When Cao Wei advanced upon Jiangling, someone devised a strategy to resist it. What insight lay behind the assertion that the Yangzi River was shared by both sides? When Emperor Wu of Jin discussed pacifying Wu, someone submitted a memorial requesting the campaign. What did those who regarded Qin and Liang as grounds for anxiety mean? Fu Jian resolved upon the strategy of “casting whips into the river to block its flow”; did the deliberations in the Taiji Hall not affirm that it was so [?]? Emperor Wen of Song was intent upon sweeping through Zhao and Wei, yet the remonstrance of the Infantry Commandant did not consider this advisable. As for the expedition against Gaoli, the high ministers urged it…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
也然不有萬一蹉跌傷威損望之言乎
清水之盟廷臣主之也然不有戎狄豺
狼非盟可結之論乎淮西之討四年不
克宰相有罷兵之請矣而誓不與賊俱
生者何壯歟澶淵之報一夕五至左右
有南幸之謀矣而勸帝親征者何决歟
夫事之成敗未易定也寧無精識遠見
早辨而預言之者在聽而用之何如耳
聽之不審用之不當鮮不以佞為忠以
===
直為謗而欲事之不敗不可得也孟子
曰我知言知之必有道矣其明言之以
觀通博之學
問治莫近於州縣之官教莫先於學校之
職夫人能知之今之君子盖嘗留意矣
異時為長民者類取之監學其後也病
其迫遲暮而久沉困於是以進士之選
充州縣之正所以重之也而說者謂漸
輕之勢已有見于今異時為師儒者或
punctuated:
也。然不有「萬一蹉跌，傷威損望」之言乎？清水之盟，廷臣主之也，然不有「戎狄豺狼，非盟可結」之論乎？淮西之討，四年不克，宰相有罷兵之請矣，而誓不與賊俱生者何壯歟！澶淵之報，一夕五至，左右有南幸之謀矣，而勸帝親征者何决歟！夫事之成敗，未易定也，寧無精識遠見、早辨而預言之者？在聽而用之何如耳。聽之不審，用之不當，鮮不以佞為忠、以直為謗，而欲事之不敗，不可得也。孟子曰：「我知言。」知之必有道矣，其明言之，以觀通博之學。
問：治莫近於州縣之官，教莫先於學校之職，夫人能知之，今之君子盖嘗留意矣。異時為長民者，類取之監學，其後也，病其迫遲暮而久沉困，於是以進士之選充州縣之正，所以重之也。而說者謂漸輕之勢，已有見于今。異時為師儒者，或
translation_en:
…Yet were there not warnings that “should even a single misstep occur, it would impair imperial prestige and diminish esteem”? Court officials supported the treaty at Qingshui; yet was there not the argument that “the Rong and Di are jackals and wolves, whom no treaty can bind”? When the campaign against Huaixi had failed to achieve victory after four years, chief councilors requested that the fighting cease. Yet how resolute was the man who swore he would not live in the same world as the rebels! When reports from Chanyuan arrived five times in a single night, the emperor’s attendants proposed an imperial journey south. Yet how decisive was the man who urged the emperor to lead the campaign in person!
Success or failure in affairs is not easily determined. Surely there are people of keen discernment and foresight who distinguish the issues early and predict the outcome. It depends only on how their words are heard and put into practice. If one listens without careful scrutiny and acts inappropriately, one can scarcely avoid taking flattery for loyalty and frankness for slander. To wish nevertheless that affairs should not fail is to wish for the impossible. Mencius said, “I understand words.” There must be a method for understanding them. Explain it clearly, so that we may assess the breadth and depth of your learning.
Question: In government, no officials are closer to the people than those of the subprefectures and counties; in education, no duties take precedence over those of the schools. Everyone can understand this, and the gentlemen of the present day have surely given it thought. Formerly, those appointed to govern the people were generally drawn from the Imperial University and the schools. Later, concern arose that they were approaching old age after long languishing in straitened circumstances. Thus men selected from among the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) were appointed as heads of subprefectures and counties, with the intention of lending weight to these posts. Yet commentators say that a tendency toward their gradual depreciation is already apparent today. Formerly, those serving as teachers sometimes…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
參以薦舉其後也苦其召奔競而積猥
冗於是杜辟薦之門開監學之選所以
矯之也而說者謂不職之弊殆有甚於
彼考黜歲行所以懲也而說者謂適以
趣其無賴之心召用踵接所以勸也而
說者謂適以長其恣肆之念以貢舉之
有無為殿最而說者謂未必其功罪專
文藝之高下為考課而說者謂非所以
為賢否夫致法以造功先王所不廢而
===
以流品用人漢唐以来固用之矣績效
之著當時仁賢之名後世不亦有聞者
乎今何以使人用而皆當法立而無弊
諸生多出於學校而升自州縣若此者
可以言歟
問中國之有夷狄猶陽之有陰人類之有
禽獸不能以無也而北虜為患常甚然
嘗觀於漢事高帝百戰之餘威加海内
而平城之憂至其後世猶不能忘孝武
punctuated:
參以薦舉。其後也，苦其召奔競而積猥冗，於是杜辟薦之門，開監學之選，所以矯之也。而說者謂不職之弊，殆有甚於彼。考黜歲行，所以懲也，而說者謂適以趣其無賴之心；召用踵接，所以勸也，而說者謂適以長其恣肆之念。以貢舉之有無為殿最，而說者謂未必其功罪；專文藝之高下為考課，而說者謂非所以為賢否。夫致法以造功，先王所不廢，而以流品用人，漢唐以來固用之矣。績效之著當時，仁賢之名後世，不亦有聞者乎？今何以使人用而皆當，法立而無弊？諸生多出於學校，而升自州縣，若此者可以言歟？

問：中國之有夷狄，猶陽之有陰、人類之有禽獸，不能以無也。而北虜為患常甚。然嘗觀於漢事，高帝百戰之餘，威加海内，而平城之憂，至其後世猶不能忘。孝武
translation_en:
…with some also recruited through recommendation. Later, troubled that this encouraged competitive pursuit of office and an accumulation of unsuitable and supernumerary personnel, the authorities closed the avenue of recruitment by invitation and recommendation and opened selection from the Imperial University and government schools. This was intended to correct the problem. Yet critics say that failures to discharge official duties have perhaps become even worse than before. Annual assessments and dismissals are intended to deter misconduct, yet critics say that they merely spur men toward shamelessness. Appointments follow one another in succession to encourage them, yet critics say that these merely foster self-indulgence and presumption. They are ranked lowest or highest according to whether they produce candidates for advancement through the examinations, yet critics say that this does not necessarily reflect their merits or faults. Their performance assessments depend exclusively on the quality of literary work, yet critics say that this is no means of judging their worthiness or unworthiness. Now, implementing regulations to achieve results was something the former kings did not neglect; and employing men according to their categories and grades has certainly been practiced since the Han and Tang. Have we not heard of men whose achievements were conspicuous in their own day and whose reputations for benevolence and worth endured in later ages? How, today, can we ensure that everyone appointed is suitably employed and that regulations are established without abuses? You students mostly come from government schools and have advanced from the prefectures and counties. Can you speak to matters such as these?

Question: That the Central Kingdom has barbarians is like yang having yin, or humankind having birds and beasts: their existence cannot be eliminated. Yet the northern barbarians have continually caused especially grave trouble. Looking at the affairs of the Han, however, Emperor Gao, after his hundred battles, extended his might throughout the realm; nevertheless, the ordeal at Pingcheng could not be forgotten even by his descendants. Emperor Xiaowu…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乗豐富之業師武臣力而邊警歲至略
無寧息竟寧以後漢事日非而羇伏塞
垣至于哀平朝獻不改非威力足制其
死命明矣然則夷狄之叛服初無與於
中國之盛衰歟前世有用柔能勝剛弱
能勝強為制御之術者信斯言也則敢
於抗盛強而拙於乗衰弱固夷狄之性
歟如劉敬之策則有女吳之深耻施賈
誼之餌則是徵令之倒置興衛霍之師
===
則犯窮黷之戒抗敵國之禮則乖王者
無外之義為斷臂散交之謀則狼心鼠
首未易可保為多防密備之計則一狼
千羊坐以自疲何如而可也自漢魏以
至于今鮮不以夷狄為意智計之士儒
先之碩其論多矣有經國用世之心者
固有考焉夫兼夷狄驅猛獸扶陽抑陰
聖賢之大義試以漢事言之則知所處
矣
punctuated: 乗豐富之業，師武臣力，而邊警歲至，略無寧息。竟寧以後，漢事日非，而羇伏塞垣，至于哀平，朝獻不改，非威力足制其死命明矣。然則夷狄之叛服，初無與於中國之盛衰歟？前世有用柔能勝剛、弱能勝強為制御之術者，信斯言也，則敢於抗盛強，而拙於乗衰弱，固夷狄之性歟？如劉敬之策，則有女吳之深耻；施賈誼之餌，則是徵令之倒置；興衛霍之師，則犯窮黷之戒；抗敵國之禮，則乖王者無外之義；為斷臂散交之謀，則狼心鼠首，未易可保；為多防密備之計，則一狼千羊，坐以自疲。何如而可也？自漢魏以至于今，鮮不以夷狄為意，智計之士、儒先之碩，其論多矣。有經國用世之心者，固有考焉。夫兼夷狄、驅猛獸、扶陽抑陰，聖賢之大義。試以漢事言之，則知所處矣。
translation_en:
…inherited a prosperous and abundant realm and relied upon military might and the exertions of his ministers, yet alarms on the frontier came every year, with scarcely any respite. After the Jingning era, the affairs of the Han deteriorated daily, yet the northern barbarians remained under restraint and submissive along the frontier, continuing their court visits and tribute offerings down to the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping. Clearly, this was not because military force sufficed to hold their lives at its mercy. Was the rebellion or submission of the barbarians, then, wholly unrelated to the strength or decline of the Central Kingdom? In earlier times, some adopted the principles that softness can overcome hardness and weakness can overcome strength as techniques for controlling them. If these sayings are true, is it indeed the nature of the barbarians to dare to resist the flourishing and strong, yet be inept at taking advantage of the declining and weak?

To follow Liu Jing’s policy would entail the profound humiliation of giving a daughter in marriage to Wu [?]; to employ Jia Yi’s inducements would reverse the proper direction of exactions and commands; to raise armies like those of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing would violate the injunction against exhausting resources through incessant warfare; to accord them the ceremonial treatment of an equal state would violate the principle that the king recognizes no one as outside his realm. To devise plans to sever their arms and break up their alliances would leave us dealing with wolfish hearts and ratlike heads, whose reliability could not readily be assured. To devise numerous defenses and close precautions would be like setting a thousand sheep against one wolf, merely wearing ourselves out. What course, then, would be effective?

From the Han and Wei down to the present, few have failed to concern themselves with the barbarians. Men of intelligence and strategic skill, and the great Confucian scholars of earlier times, have discussed the matter extensively. Those intent on ordering the state and putting their abilities to use in the world will surely have examined these discussions. Bringing the barbarians under one rule, driving away fierce beasts, supporting yang and restraining yin: these are the great principles of the sages and worthies. Discuss the matter through the affairs of the Han, and the appropriate course of action will become clear.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
立則見其參於前也在輿則見其倚於衡
也
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批
文詞純正發明常若有見處
深得題意必老學之士也
同考試官教諭袁批
義合傳註而文有發揮塲
中如此作者不多見也
===
考試官侍講彭批
能𫠦於辭
考試官洗馬鄭批
典雅可觀
隨吾身之所寓若斯理之有見盖忠信篤敬言
行之理也非吾心念念而不忘又豈能隨其所
在而常若有見也哉聖人告子張之意如此且
夫言必欲忠信也忠信不可頃刻而忘行必欲
篤敬也篤敬不可須臾而離方其佇立之時若
可忽也而忠信篤敬拳拳於念慮者無或忘一
舉目也恍若此理見於跬步之間與吾相參而
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「立則見其參於前也，在輿則見其倚於衡也。」
宋禮

同考試官訓導張批：
「文詞純正，發明常若有見處，深得題意，必老學之士也。」
同考試官教諭袁批：
「義合傳註，而文有發揮，塲中如此作者不多見也。」
考試官侍講彭批：
「能𫠦於辭。」
考試官洗馬鄭批：
「典雅可觀。」

隨吾身之所寓，若斯理之有見。盖忠信篤敬，言行之理也。非吾心念念而不忘，又豈能隨其所在而常若有見也哉？聖人告子張之意如此。且夫言必欲忠信也，忠信不可頃刻而忘；行必欲篤敬也，篤敬不可須臾而離。方其佇立之時，若可忽也，而忠信篤敬拳拳於念慮者，無或忘。一舉目也，恍若此理見於跬步之間，與吾相參而
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When standing, see them present before you; when riding in a carriage, see them resting against its crossbar.”
Song Li

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor:
“The language is pure and correct. His elucidation of the sense of ‘constantly seeming to see them’ grasps the topic’s meaning profoundly. He must be a scholar of long experience.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor:
“The meaning accords with the commentaries and annotations, while the composition develops it further. Writers like this are seldom seen in the examination hall.”

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor:
“Capable in expression [?].”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian:
“Classically elegant and worthy of appreciation.”

Wherever my person may be, it is as though this principle were visible. Loyalty, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence are the principles governing speech and conduct. Unless my mind keeps them in thought without ever forgetting them, how could they constantly seem visible wherever I happen to be? Such is the meaning of the Sage’s instruction to Zizhang. Now, speech must be loyal and trustworthy: loyalty and trustworthiness must not be forgotten even for an instant. Conduct must be earnest and reverent: earnestness and reverence must not be departed from even for a moment. While standing still, one might think that one could be heedless; yet loyalty, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence, held devotedly in one’s thoughts, are never forgotten. At a single lifting of the eyes, this principle seems to appear within a step or two, standing alongside me and…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
不舍焉及其在輿之際若可肆也而忠信篤敬
切切於心思者無少置一顧瞻也儼若此理倚
於車衡之上與吾同驅而不離焉夫忠信篤敬
本無形之可求無體之可覩今也立焉見之由
吾心不忘於佇立之頃而常目在之耳輿焉見
之由吾心不忘於在輿之時而常若有見耳不
言而忠信存不行而篤敬在雖欲頃刻離之而
不可得也吁心無往而不在理無適而不然然
後一言一行自不離於忠信篤敬而蠻貊可行
===
矣吾夫子以是為子張告其意不既深乎抑伊
尹之稱成湯於天之明命嘗以顧諟言之矣說
者謂湯之所以聖敬日躋者顧諟之功也顧諟
之言其參前倚衡之義歟雖深淺之不同其存
誠之無間一而已學者由子張參前倚衡之見
而進於湯之顧諟則作聖之功在是矣
堯以不得舜為己憂舜以不得禹臯陶為
己憂夫以百畝之不易為己憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠教人以善謂之忠
punctuated:
不舍焉。及其在輿之際，若可肆也，而忠信篤敬切切於心思者無少置。一顧瞻也，儼若此理倚於車衡之上，與吾同驅而不離焉。夫忠信篤敬，本無形之可求，無體之可覩。今也立焉見之，由吾心不忘於佇立之頃，而常目在之耳；輿焉見之，由吾心不忘於在輿之時，而常若有見耳。不言而忠信存，不行而篤敬在，雖欲頃刻離之而不可得也。吁！心無往而不在，理無適而不然，然後一言一行自不離於忠信篤敬，而蠻貊可行矣。吾夫子以是為子張告，其意不既深乎？抑伊尹之稱成湯，於天之明命，嘗以顧諟言之矣。說者謂湯之所以聖敬日躋者，顧諟之功也。顧諟之言，其參前倚衡之義歟？雖深淺之不同，其存誠之無間，一而已。學者由子張參前倚衡之見，而進於湯之顧諟，則作聖之功在是矣。

堯以不得舜為己憂，舜以不得禹、臯陶為己憂。夫以百畝之不易為己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠。
translation_en:
…and never leaves me. When riding in a carriage, one might think it permissible to relax; yet sincerity, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence remain urgently present in one's thoughts, never set aside even briefly. At a glance, it is as though this principle rests upon the carriage's crossbar, traveling alongside me without departing. Sincerity, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence have no shape to seek out, no bodily form to behold. That I now see them while standing is simply because my mind does not forget them while I stand, and my gaze remains fixed upon them. That I see them while riding is simply because my mind does not forget them while I ride, and it is always as though they were visible. Even without speaking, sincerity and trustworthiness remain; even without acting, earnestness and reverence are present. Though I wished to depart from them for a moment, I could not. Ah! Only when the mind is present wherever one goes, and this principle holds wherever one may be, will every word and deed naturally accord with sincerity, trustworthiness, earnestness, and reverence, enabling one to conduct oneself successfully even among the Man and Mo peoples. Was not our Master's intention profoundly meaningful when he instructed Zizhang in this way?

Moreover, in praising Cheng Tang, Yi Yin spoke of his keeping Heaven's luminous mandate constantly in view. Commentators say that Tang's sagely reverence advanced daily through this practice of keeping it in view. Does this expression not convey the same meaning as seeing the principle standing before one and resting upon the carriage's crossbar? Although these differ in depth, they are alike in preserving sincerity without interruption. If learners proceed from Zizhang's vision of the principle standing before him and resting upon the crossbar to Tang's constant regard for Heaven's mandate, the work of becoming a sage lies herein.

Yao regarded failing to obtain Shun's service as his own concern; Shun regarded failing to obtain the service of Yu and Gao Yao as his own concern. One who regards the failure to cultivate his hundred mu of land as his own concern is a farmer. Sharing one's wealth with others is called generosity; teaching others goodness is called conscientious devotion.…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
爲天下得人者謂之仁
胡諒
同考試官訓導李批此作析理詳明遣詞簡古
非老於文學者不能故表而出之
同考試官教諭李批孟義能包括題意者鮮此
作以憂天下之大仁天下之大會意成文非穉手所及
考試官侍講彭批有關鍵有抑揚有議論
考試官洗馬鄭批措詞整健他作所不及
知聖人憂天下之大當知聖人仁天下之大而
===
其小者不足言也夫得人以治天下則足以仁
天下矣聖人安得不以不得人爲天下憂哉孟
子闢許行並耕之說其意如此且夫堯非不憂
民也而不事事以爲意其焦勞於朝夕者惟以
不得舜其人而已耳不得乎舜則民誰與治乎
舜非不憂民也而不屑屑以爲心其紆鬱於念
慮者惟以不得乎禹臯陶其人而已耳不得乎
禹臯則民誰與理乎夫以百畝之田播植未亟
而戚然其不寧者農夫之事也汗萊未闢而蹙
punctuated:
爲天下得人者，謂之仁。
胡諒
同考試官訓導李批：「此作析理詳明，遣詞簡古，非老於文學者不能，故表而出之。」
同考試官教諭李批：「孟義能包括題意者鮮。此作以憂天下之大、仁天下之大，會意成文，非穉手所及。」
考試官侍講彭批：「有關鍵，有抑揚，有議論。」
考試官洗馬鄭批：「措詞整健，他作所不及。」
知聖人憂天下之大，當知聖人仁天下之大，而其小者不足言也。夫得人以治天下，則足以仁天下矣。聖人安得不以不得人爲天下憂哉？孟子闢許行並耕之說，其意如此。且夫堯非不憂民也，而不事事以爲意；其焦勞於朝夕者，惟以不得舜其人而已耳。不得乎舜，則民誰與治乎？舜非不憂民也，而不屑屑以爲心；其紆鬱於念慮者，惟以不得乎禹、臯陶其人而已耳。不得乎禹、臯，則民誰與理乎？夫以百畝之田，播植未亟，而戚然其不寧者，農夫之事也；汗萊未闢，而蹙
translation_en:
…To secure worthy men for all under Heaven is called benevolence.

Hu Liang

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This composition analyzes principles thoroughly and clearly, using concise and classically elegant language. Only someone seasoned in literary study could accomplish this; hence I have singled it out.”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Few essays on the Mencius encompass the full meaning of their topic. This composition brings together the greatness of concern for all under Heaven and the greatness of benevolence toward all under Heaven, weaving their meaning into an essay. This is beyond the reach of a novice.”

Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: “It has pivotal connections, modulation, and reasoned argument.”

Examiner Zheng, Librarian in the Household of the Heir Apparent, comments: “Its wording is orderly and vigorous, beyond what other compositions achieve.”

Knowing the greatness of the sages’ concern for all under Heaven, one should recognize the greatness of their benevolence toward all under Heaven; lesser matters scarcely merit discussion. Securing worthy men to govern all under Heaven suffices to extend benevolence throughout it. How could the sages fail to regard the lack of worthy men as a cause for concern on behalf of all under Heaven? This was Mencius’s meaning in refuting Xu Xing’s doctrine that rulers should till the fields alongside their people.

Yao was certainly concerned for the people, but he did not occupy his mind with every individual matter. What troubled and wearied him morning and evening was simply that he had not secured a man such as Shun. Without Shun, with whom could he govern the people? Shun was certainly concerned for the people, but he did not burden his mind with petty details. What weighed upon his thoughts was simply that he had not secured men such as Yu and Gao Yao. Without Yu and Gao Yao, with whom could he bring order to the people?

To be distressed and uneasy because the sowing and planting of a hundred mu of fields have not yet been completed is the farmer’s business. When the overgrown land [?] has not yet been cleared, to frown…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
然其不安者田父之職也豈以憂天下者而憂
百畝之憂哉彼以財而分人則及民者無所私
謂之惠可也然滯於狹小而不廣君子有不屑
焉以善而教人則愛民者有其實謂之忠可也
然局於有限而難久君子有不急焉惟若堯為
天下而得熈載亮工之舜舜為天下而得從欲
以治之禹皐則恩惠廣大而澤及於人人非仁
而何教化無窮而善被於世世又非仁而何豈
以仁天下者而先忠惠之務哉忠惠且不先而
===
况於耕乎是則聖人之所以憂天下者誠有在
矣雖然卑高之位既陳則小大之職斯異君之
不可並民而耕雖五尺童子知其為非矣而許
行持區區之說鼓喙其間時君惑焉而如陳相
者又相與北面而師之孟子折以大義反復數
百言如對強敵然僅僅勝之則世衰道微邪說
之惑人也盖久矣向無孟子則處士之議豈直
洪水猛獸之災故曰功不在禹下
易
punctuated:
然其不安者，田父之職也。豈以憂天下者而憂百畝之憂哉？彼以財而分人，則及民者無所私，謂之惠可也；然滯於狹小而不廣，君子有不屑焉。以善而教人，則愛民者有其實，謂之忠可也；然局於有限而難久，君子有不急焉。惟若堯為天下而得熈載亮工之舜，舜為天下而得從欲以治之禹皐，則恩惠廣大，而澤及於人人，非仁而何？教化無窮，而善被於世世，又非仁而何？豈以仁天下者而先忠惠之務哉？忠惠且不先，而况於耕乎？是則聖人之所以憂天下者，誠有在矣。雖然，卑高之位既陳，則小大之職斯異。君之不可並民而耕，雖五尺童子知其為非矣。而許行持區區之說，鼓喙其間，時君惑焉；而如陳相者，又相與北面而師之。孟子折以大義，反復數百言，如對強敵然，僅僅勝之。則世衰道微，邪說之惑人也盖久矣。向無孟子，則處士之議，豈直洪水猛獸之災？故曰：「功不在禹下。」

易
translation_en:
…to be uneasy in this way is the farmer’s concern. How could one who cares for all under Heaven concern himself with the worries of a hundred mu of farmland? When someone distributes wealth to others, the benefits he extends to the people show no partiality: this may be called generosity. Yet it remains confined within narrow bounds and does not reach widely; the gentleman considers it beneath his concern. When someone teaches others goodness, his love for the people has substance: this may be called conscientious devotion. Yet its scope is limited and it is difficult to sustain; the gentleman does not regard it as his most urgent task. Only when, like Yao, one obtains for all under Heaven a Shun who can make undertakings flourish and bring official work to completion, or, like Shun, obtains a Yu and Gao Yao who can govern in accordance with his wishes, does beneficence become so extensive that its blessings reach every person. What is this if not benevolence? Moral instruction becomes inexhaustible, and goodness extends through generation after generation. What, again, is this if not benevolence? How could one who brings benevolence to all under Heaven give priority to acts of conscientious devotion and generosity? If even these do not take priority, how much less should farming? Thus the sages’ concern for all under Heaven truly has its proper focus.

Nevertheless, once positions of high and low rank have been established, greater and lesser responsibilities differ accordingly. Even a child five feet tall knows that it would be wrong for a ruler to farm alongside the people. Yet Xu Xing upheld his petty doctrine and noisily expounded it among them. The rulers of his time were misled, while men such as Chen Xiang joined together in facing north before him and taking him as their teacher. Mencius refuted him with the great principles of righteousness, arguing back and forth over several hundred words as though confronting a powerful enemy, and only just prevailed. Thus, as the age declined and the Way grew faint, heterodox doctrines had evidently long been deluding people. Had there been no Mencius, would the arguments of private scholars have been merely a calamity like floods and savage beasts? Hence it is said: “His achievement was no less than Yu’s.”

Book of Changes

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
泰小往大来吉亨彖曰泰小往大来吉亨
則是天地交而萬物通也上下交而其
志同也內陽而外陰內健而外順內君
子而外小人君子道長小人道消也
沈元
同考試官訓導張批題本平易作者不泛則畧是
篇說理明而辭不費可謂作者
同考試官教諭袁批此作發眀泰義詳盡一結歸
本於君臣同志尤見學識他篇亦佳一薦何忝
===
考試官侍講彭批簡潔
考試官洗馬鄭批易義貴眀潔此作得之
前聖畫泰之卦後聖係泰之辭故傳復申眀之
也盖卦具通泰之義宜其占之吉亨也聖人既
畫卦而係辭吾夫子安得不申眀之於後哉昔
伏羲畫卦交坤於乾之上名之曰泰盖取通泰
之義也文王係辭以為是卦坤往居外乾来居
內又自歸妹来六往居四九来居三皆小往而
大来也夫小往居外大来居內固有吉亨之道
punctuated:
泰，小往大来，吉亨。彖曰：「泰，小往大来，吉亨，則是天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。內陽而外陰，內健而外順，內君子而外小人。君子道長，小人道消也。」
沈元
同考試官訓導張批：「題本平易，作者不泛則畧。是篇說理明而辭不費，可謂作者。」
同考試官教諭袁批：「此作發眀泰義詳盡，一結歸本於君臣同志，尤見學識。他篇亦佳，一薦何忝！」
考試官侍講彭批：「簡潔。」
考試官洗馬鄭批：「易義貴眀潔，此作得之。」
前聖畫泰之卦，後聖係泰之辭，故傳復申眀之也。盖卦具通泰之義，宜其占之吉亨也。聖人既畫卦而係辭，吾夫子安得不申眀之於後哉？昔伏羲畫卦，交坤於乾之上，名之曰泰，盖取通泰之義也。文王係辭，以為是卦坤往居外，乾来居內；又自歸妹来，六往居四，九来居三，皆小往而大来也。夫小往居外，大来居內，固有吉亨之道
translation_en:
“Tai (Peace): the small departs and the great comes. Auspicious and successful.” The Commentary on the Judgments says: “Tai: the small departs and the great comes; auspicious and successful. This means that Heaven and Earth interact and the myriad things flourish; those above and below interact and share the same purpose. Within is yang and without is yin; within is strength and without is compliance; within are gentlemen and without are petty men. The way of gentlemen advances, and the way of petty men wanes.”
Shen Yuan.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The topic is inherently straightforward, but writers tend to be either diffuse or cursory. This essay explains the principles clearly without wasting words. Its author may truly be called an accomplished writer.”
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: “This composition elucidates the meaning of Tai thoroughly. Its conclusion traces everything back to ruler and ministers sharing the same purpose, especially revealing the author’s learning and discernment. His other essays are also fine. How could recommending him be undeserved?”
Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: “Concise and clear.”
Examiner Zheng, Editorial Director, comments: “An interpretation of the Changes should above all be clear and concise. This composition achieves that.”
An earlier sage drew the hexagram Tai, and a later sage attached its statement; thus the commentary further elucidates it. Since the hexagram embodies the meaning of free intercourse and peace, its divinatory indication should naturally be auspicious and successful. Once the sages had drawn the hexagram and attached its statement, how could our Master fail to elucidate it afterward? Long ago, when Fuxi drew the hexagrams, he placed Kun above Qian so that they interacted, naming it Tai to express the meaning of free intercourse and peace. When King Wen attached the statement, he understood that in this hexagram Kun departs to occupy the outer position and Qian comes to occupy the inner position. Moreover, it derives from Guimei (The Marrying Maiden): the six departs to occupy the fourth position, and the nine comes to occupy the third. These are both instances of the small departing and the great coming. Now, when the small departs to occupy the outer position and the great comes to occupy the inner position, this inherently contains the way to auspiciousness and success…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矣占者陽剛豈不吉而且亨乎羲文聖人名卦
繫辭之意如此吾夫子傳彖又從而申明之謂
夫泰之小往大来而吉亨者則是天氣下交於
地地氣上達於天而品物流形各遂其發育之
性矣君推誠以任下臣竭誠以事上而君臣同
心共濟夫天下之事矣乾為陽為健而来居於
内坤為陰為順而往居於外乾陽為君子而在
内是君子任用於上也坤陰為小人而在外是
小人退處於下也君子在内則剛明用事而拔
===
茅連茹之吉可致其道之長為何如小人在外
則陰邪屏迹而剥廬無號之凶可必其道之消
又何如吾夫子發明名卦係辭之旨无餘蘊矣
大抵天地交而萬物通天地之泰也上下交而
其志同朝廷之泰也君子道長非天下之泰乎
以天下之泰推之朝廷之泰由朝廷之泰推而
為天下之泰然則參賛調燮致治隆平以保泰
於無窮者則本乎君臣志同以致之也大易之
旨淵乎微哉
punctuated:
矣。占者陽剛，豈不吉而且亨乎？羲文聖人名卦繫辭之意如此。吾夫子傳彖，又從而申明之，謂夫泰之小往大来而吉亨者，則是天氣下交於地，地氣上達於天，而品物流形，各遂其發育之性矣。君推誠以任下，臣竭誠以事上，而君臣同心，共濟夫天下之事矣。乾為陽、為健，而来居於内；坤為陰、為順，而往居於外。乾陽為君子而在内，是君子任用於上也；坤陰為小人而在外，是小人退處於下也。君子在内，則剛明用事，而拔茅連茹之吉可致，其道之長為何如？小人在外，則陰邪屏迹，而剥廬無號之凶可必，其道之消又何如？吾夫子發明名卦係辭之旨，无餘蘊矣。

大抵天地交而萬物通，天地之泰也；上下交而其志同，朝廷之泰也。君子道長，非天下之泰乎？以天下之泰推之朝廷之泰，由朝廷之泰推而為天下之泰。然則參賛調燮，致治隆平，以保泰於無窮者，則本乎君臣志同以致之也。大易之旨，淵乎微哉！
translation_en:
… indeed. If the diviner possesses yang firmness, how could there fail to be good fortune and success? Such was the intent of the sages Fuxi and King Wen in naming the hexagram and attaching its statement. Our Master, Confucius, further elucidated this in his Commentary on the Judgment. He explained that in Tai (Peace), the small departs and the great comes, bringing good fortune and success: Heaven’s vital energy descends to mingle with Earth, and Earth’s vital energy rises to reach Heaven. The myriad things flow into their forms, each fulfilling its inherent capacity to grow and develop. The ruler extends his sincerity in entrusting responsibilities to those below; ministers devote their utmost sincerity to serving their superior. Ruler and ministers are thus of one mind, jointly bringing the affairs of the realm to fruition. Qian is yang and strength, and comes to occupy the inner position; Kun is yin and compliance, and departs to occupy the outer position. Qian’s yang represents the noble man and is within: this means that noble men are employed in high office. Kun’s yin represents the petty man and is without: this means that petty men withdraw to lowly positions. When noble men are within, firmness and discernment govern affairs, and the good fortune of “pulling up thatch grass with its interconnected roots” can be attained. How greatly their way advances! When petty men are without, sinister and pernicious influences disappear, and the misfortune of “stripping away the dwelling” and “having none to cry out to” is assured. How completely their way wanes! Our Master’s elucidation of the intent behind the hexagram’s name and its attached statement leaves nothing unexplored.

Generally speaking, when Heaven and Earth interact and the myriad things move freely, this is the peace of Heaven and Earth. When those above and below interact and share a common purpose, this is the peace of the court. When the way of noble men advances, is this not the peace of all under Heaven? From the peace of all under Heaven one extends the reasoning to the peace of the court; from the peace of the court one extends it to bring about peace throughout all under Heaven. Thus, assisting the transforming work of Heaven and Earth, harmonizing their forces, attaining flourishing government and peace, and preserving that peace forever—all these are achieved on the foundation of a common purpose shared by ruler and ministers. How profound and subtle is the meaning of the great Book of Changes!

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
富有之謂大業日新之謂盛德生生之謂
易
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批此題人能作之而發明親切
者絕少晚得是篇詞理俱到非造詣深者不能及此宜爲
本房之冠
同考試官教諭袁批此篇本顯仁藏用立說深得
本旨誠易中之翹楚也健羨健羨
考試官侍講彭批文有發明
===
考試官洗馬鄭批理致精密其甞究心易學者乎
聖人論造化生成之功必言陰陽不已之妙盖
造化之德業生成之功也然所以生成而不已
者豈非所謂易乎宜大傳聖人詳言之也且夫
道之流行於造化也有大業焉有盛德焉果何
以見之哉自其藏用言之則斂化育於寂然之
中歸生意於至靜之内物雖萬類之不同俾各
保合其氣而無外物雖萬彙之不一俾各翕聚
其理而不遺其大而無外也如此得不謂之大
punctuated:
富有之謂大業，日新之謂盛德，生生之謂易。
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批：此題人能作之，而發明親切者絕少。晚得是篇，詞理俱到，非造詣深者不能及此，宜爲本房之冠。
同考試官教諭袁批：此篇本顯仁藏用立說，深得本旨，誠易中之翹楚也。健羨！健羨！
考試官侍講彭批：文有發明。
考試官洗馬鄭批：理致精密，其甞究心易學者乎？
聖人論造化生成之功，必言陰陽不已之妙。盖造化之德業，生成之功也。然所以生成而不已者，豈非所謂易乎？宜大傳聖人詳言之也。且夫道之流行於造化也，有大業焉，有盛德焉，果何以見之哉？自其藏用言之，則斂化育於寂然之中，歸生意於至靜之内。物雖萬類之不同，俾各保合其氣而無外；物雖萬彙之不一，俾各翕聚其理而不遺。其大而無外也如此，得不謂之大
translation_en:
“Abundant possession is called great achievement; daily renewal is called flourishing virtue; generation upon generation is called change.”
Song Li
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: Anyone can compose an answer to this topic, but very few elucidate it with close understanding. Late in the process I obtained this essay, accomplished in both expression and reasoning. Only someone of profound attainment could reach this level. It deserves first place in this examining room.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: This essay bases its argument on “manifesting benevolence and concealing its operation,” grasping the underlying meaning profoundly. It is truly outstanding among the essays on the Book of Changes. Admirable! Admirable!
Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: The essay offers illuminating insights.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian of the Heir Apparent: Its reasoning is subtle and precise. Surely its author has devoted himself to studying the Book of Changes?
When the sage discusses the work of creation in generating and completing things, he invariably speaks of the wondrous, unceasing activity of yin and yang. For the virtue and achievement of creation consist in its work of generating and completing things. Yet what enables this generation and completion to continue without cease—is it not what is called change? It is fitting that the sage should explain this in detail in the Great Commentary. Now, as the Way circulates through creation, there is great achievement, and there is flourishing virtue. How, indeed, can these be discerned? Speaking of its concealing its operation, it gathers transformation and nurture into quiescence and returns the impulse of life to the utmost stillness. Though things differ in their myriad kinds, it enables each to preserve and unite its vital energy, leaving nothing outside; though things vary in their myriad categories, it enables each to gather together its principle, omitting nothing. Its greatness is thus all-encompassing: how could it fail to be called great …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
業乎自其顯仁言之則大化運行於兩間和氣
充塞於上下與之氣以為生之質者不以古今
而有間賦之理以為性之原者不以終始而或
息其久而無窮也如此得不謂之盛德乎然造
化之所以藏用者陰之為也藏之未久而生意
顯著於外者不可遏則是陰變為陽而生生不
窮易書之姤變而為復者是已造化之所以顯
仁者陽之為也顯之未久而化工歸藏於內者
不可見則陽變為陰而生生不已易書之復變
===
而為姤者是已陰陽相生變化無窮理與書一
而已聖人論造化之生成而推之於易有以哉
大抵有天地則有此變化有變化則有此生成
推其原固莫非陰陽之所為而實有自然流行
不倚於陰陽者存乎其間不然安能亘千萬古
變化生成相為循環不已如是哉故曰陰陽不
測之謂神
書
夙夜惟寅直哉惟清
punctuated:
業乎？自其顯仁言之，則大化運行於兩間，和氣充塞於上下。與之氣以為生之質者，不以古今而有間；賦之理以為性之原者，不以終始而或息。其久而無窮也如此，得不謂之盛德乎？然造化之所以藏用者，陰之為也。藏之未久，而生意顯著於外者不可遏，則是陰變為陽，而生生不窮，《易》書之姤變而為復者是已。造化之所以顯仁者，陽之為也。顯之未久，而化工歸藏於內者不可見，則陽變為陰，而生生不已，《易》書之復變而為姤者是已。陰陽相生，變化無窮，理與書一而已。聖人論造化之生成而推之於《易》，有以哉！大抵有天地則有此變化，有變化則有此生成。推其原，固莫非陰陽之所為，而實有自然流行、不倚於陰陽者存乎其間。不然，安能亘千萬古，變化生成相為循環不已如是哉？故曰：「陰陽不測之謂神。」

書

夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。
translation_en:
…achievement? Speaking of its manifesting benevolence, the great transforming process moves between Heaven and Earth, and harmonious vital force fills the regions above and below. Its bestowal of vital force as the substance of life admits no interruption between antiquity and the present; its endowment of principle as the source of nature never ceases from beginning to end. So enduring and inexhaustible is it: can it fail to be called flourishing virtue? Yet creation’s concealing its operation is the work of yin. Before it has long remained concealed, the impulse of life becomes manifest outwardly and cannot be restrained. This is yin changing into yang, generating life without limit: it is precisely the transformation of Gou (Encounter) into Fu (Return) in the Book of Changes. Creation’s manifesting benevolence is the work of yang. Before it has long remained manifest, the workings of transformation return to concealment within and cannot be seen. Thus yang changes into yin, generating life without cease: it is precisely the transformation of Fu into Gou in the Book of Changes. Yin and yang produce one another, and their transformations are inexhaustible. The principle and the book are simply one. There is good reason why the sage, in discussing creation’s generation and completion of things, extends his account to the Changes!

In general, where there are Heaven and Earth, there are these transformations; where there are transformations, there is this generation and completion. Tracing them to their source, all are indeed the work of yin and yang. Yet within them there truly exists something that flows spontaneously and does not depend upon yin and yang. Otherwise, how could transformation, generation, and completion continue through countless ages, following one another in an unceasing cycle like this? Hence it is said: “That which is unfathomable in yin and yang is called the numinous.”

Book of Documents

“Morning and night, be reverent; be upright, be pure.”

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
張恕
同考試官訓導李批文理簡明筆力蒼古宜錄之
以式後學
同考試官教諭李批作此題者多以敬直平講而
清為之效殊非當時立言本旨此作見理明而遣辭當是
以錄之
考試官侍講彭批蓋於經文體貼不徒註脚生義
考試官洗馬鄭批得當時命官語意
聖君告典禮之官欲其端行禮之本盖必寅直
===
清而後可以行其禮也秩宗典事神之禮所以
交於神明可不知所務哉宜帝舜以是而命伯
夷也盖謂典三禮而有事於神明必端其本而
後可以交於神明是故時而夙也雖或非承祀
宗廟之時而嚴恭以度凛乎祖考之予顧盖自
早以達於昏暮翼翼其無間也時而夜也雖或
非有事乎郊社之際而祇肅以承儼乎上帝之
女臨盖自夜以接于旦朝夔夔其靡懈也于焉
必有以直乎内而不使私曲之或存不啻矢之
punctuated:
張恕

同考試官訓導李批：文理簡明，筆力蒼古，宜錄之以式後學。
同考試官教諭李批：作此題者，多以敬直平講，而清為之效，殊非當時立言本旨。此作見理明而遣辭當，是以錄之。
考試官侍講彭批：蓋於經文體貼，不徒註脚生義。
考試官洗馬鄭批：得當時命官語意。

聖君告典禮之官，欲其端行禮之本，盖必寅直清，而後可以行其禮也。秩宗典事神之禮，所以交於神明，可不知所務哉？宜帝舜以是而命伯夷也。盖謂典三禮而有事於神明，必端其本，而後可以交於神明。是故時而夙也，雖或非承祀宗廟之時，而嚴恭以度，凛乎祖考之予顧；盖自早以達於昏暮，翼翼其無間也。時而夜也，雖或非有事乎郊社之際，而祇肅以承，儼乎上帝之女臨；盖自夜以接于旦朝，夔夔其靡懈也。于焉必有以直乎内，而不使私曲之或存，不啻矢之
translation_en:
Zhang Shu 張恕

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: The reasoning and expression are concise and clear, and the writing has an archaic vigor. It should be included as a model for later students.
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: Most who write on this topic discuss reverence and uprightness on the same level, treating purity as their effect. This decidedly misses the original intent of the statement on that occasion. This essay understands the principle clearly and expresses it aptly; therefore it is included.
Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: It closely apprehends the classic’s text, rather than merely deriving interpretations from its commentary.
Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: It captures the meaning and tenor of the words used when appointing the official on that occasion.

The sage ruler instructed the official in charge of ritual, wishing him to set right the foundation for performing the rites. For only with reverence, uprightness, and purity could he perform those rites. The Director of Ancestral Sacrifices oversees the rites for serving the spirits, through which one communes with divine powers. Could he fail to understand what he must attend to? It was fitting that Emperor Shun should use these words to charge Bo Yi with his duties. The meaning is that, when overseeing the Three Rites and serving divine powers, one must first set right the foundation; only then can one commune with them.

Thus, when it is early morning, even if it is not a time for conducting sacrifices in the ancestral temple, he must regulate his conduct with solemn reverence, standing in awe as though his ancestors were watching him. From morning until dusk, his watchfulness must be unbroken. When it is night, even if it is not an occasion for sacrifices at the suburban altar or the altar of soil, he must attend to his duties with reverence and solemnity, maintaining gravity as though the Lord on High were looking down upon him. From night until the next morning, his reverent vigilance must never slacken. In this he must find the means to make himself upright within, allowing no selfish crookedness to remain, just like an arrow’s …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
棘而繩之引乃可以言乎直于焉必有以潔其
心而不使物欲之或汚不啻江漢之濯而澗沚
之湜乃可以言乎清如是則與天者游而鬼神
合德由是行其禮事其神不亦有感通之道哉
大抵禮敬而已敬則此心收斂而能直直則此
心虛明而能清故寅直清行禮之本而寅又直
清之本也若夫籩豆之事則有司存焉
伻來毖殷乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣曰明禋
拜手稽首休享
===
胡諒
同考試官訓導李 批寫出周公述成王遣使毖殷
命寧之意宛如也讀之令人心目豁然
同考試官教諭李 批場中多爲此題所窘惟是篇
辭理明暢𨗳然出衆其壁經中之巨擘歟
考試官侍講彭 批於文義訓詁皆明白
考試官洗馬鄭 批辭意通暢
大臣述賢王因敕殷之使隆錫命之禮盖謹毖
庶殷固以繫安危之慮而命寧周公則委重之
punctuated:
棘而繩之引，乃可以言乎直。于焉必有以潔其心，而不使物欲之或汚，不啻江漢之濯而澗沚之湜，乃可以言乎清。如是，則與天者游，而鬼神合德。由是行其禮、事其神，不亦有感通之道哉？大抵禮，敬而已。敬則此心收斂而能直，直則此心虛明而能清。故寅直清，行禮之本，而寅又直清之本也。若夫籩豆之事，則有司存焉。
伻來毖殷，乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣，曰明禋。拜手稽首，休享。
胡諒
同考試官訓導李批：寫出周公述成王遣使毖殷、命寧之意，宛如也。讀之令人心目豁然。
同考試官教諭李批：場中多爲此題所窘，惟是篇辭理明暢，𨗳然出衆，其壁經中之巨擘歟？
考試官侍講彭批：於文義、訓詁皆明白。
考試官洗馬鄭批：辭意通暢。
大臣述賢王因敕殷之使隆錫命之禮。盖謹毖庶殷，固以繫安危之慮，而命寧周公，則委重之
translation_en:
…straight as an arrow and drawn taut as a cord: only then can one speak of uprightness. One must then purify the heart, allowing no material desires to defile it, as though washed in the Jiang and Han rivers and made limpid as the waters of a mountain stream: only then can one speak of purity. In this way, one associates with Heaven and accords in virtue with the spirits. To perform rites and serve the spirits on this basis—is this not the way to move them and obtain a response? Rites, in essence, are simply reverence. With reverence, the heart is gathered in and can become upright; with uprightness, it is open and luminous and can become pure. Thus reverence, uprightness, and purity are the foundation for performing rites, while reverence is itself the foundation of uprightness and purity. As for the business of arranging sacrificial baskets and vessels, there are officials charged with it.
“He sent an envoy to admonish the people of Yin, and then commanded that I be comforted with two vessels of black-millet sacrificial wine, saying that it was for an illustrious sacrifice. I bowed with hands joined and touched my head to the ground, gratefully receiving the favor.”
Hu Liang.
Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This vividly conveys the Duke of Zhou’s meaning as he recounts how King Cheng sent an envoy to admonish Yin and commanded that he be comforted. Reading it opens the mind and clears the vision.”
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Many candidates in the examination hall were stymied by this topic. This essay alone is lucid and fluent in both expression and reasoning, conspicuously [?] surpassing the others. Surely it is an outstanding work among essays on the ‘Wall Classic’ [?].”
Examiner Peng, Expositor-in-waiting, comments: “Both the meaning of the text and the explanation of its words are clear.”
Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: “Its expression and meaning are coherent and fluent.”
A great minister recounts how a worthy king, on the occasion of sending an envoy to admonish Yin, magnified the ceremonial bestowal of gifts and commands. For carefully admonishing the people of Yin certainly reflected concern for the security or peril of the realm; commanding that the Duke of Zhou be comforted, meanwhile, expressed the intention of entrusting him with weighty…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
意也周公詳述其事而其君臣之際有可觀矣
昔成王甫畢事於新邑遂退即于宗周留後之
責既付於周公毖殷之事復馳於專使誠以殷
民之遐逖固雖舊矣今則密邇王室申之以文
告所以益堅其式化之念殷士之臣我亦有年
矣今則周公初政重之以戒勅所以益勵其承
叙之心然訓儆殷人固所當急而慰答周公尤
不可緩於是因毖殷之使致綏寧之命有物以
備其儀有辭以達其敬言乎其物則釀以秬黍
===
和以鬱鬯其尊以中所謂卣也其數以二所謂
朋也是儀也降灌之所須宗廟之盛禮獻之於
公豈非備非常之儀哉言乎其辭則以謂致潔
盡敬以将誠有齊明之德焉拜手稽首而休享
有嘉薦之道焉是敬也嚴於承祀之際陳於昭
假之時施之於公豈非致非常之敬哉周公述
成王之遣使錫命詞詳而不殺亦惟其儀與敬
之非常耳不然則酒醴尊罍之間豈足以煩周
公之齒頰哉又因是而有見焉周公於成王之
punctuated: 意也。周公詳述其事，而其君臣之際有可觀矣。昔成王甫畢事於新邑，遂退即于宗周。留後之責既付於周公，毖殷之事復馳於專使。誠以殷民之遐逖固雖舊矣，今則密邇王室，申之以文告，所以益堅其式化之念；殷士之臣我亦有年矣，今則周公初政，重之以戒勅，所以益勵其承叙之心。然訓儆殷人固所當急，而慰答周公尤不可緩。於是因毖殷之使，致綏寧之命，有物以備其儀，有辭以達其敬。言乎其物，則釀以秬黍，和以鬱鬯，其尊以中，所謂卣也；其數以二，所謂朋也。是儀也，降灌之所須，宗廟之盛禮，獻之於公，豈非備非常之儀哉？言乎其辭，則以謂致潔盡敬以将誠，有齊明之德焉；拜手稽首而休享，有嘉薦之道焉。是敬也，嚴於承祀之際，陳於昭假之時，施之於公，豈非致非常之敬哉？周公述成王之遣使錫命，詞詳而不殺，亦惟其儀與敬之非常耳。不然，則酒醴尊罍之間，豈足以煩周公之齒頰哉？又因是而有見焉：周公於成王之
translation_en:
…the intention of entrusting him with weighty responsibility. The Duke of Zhou recounts the affair in detail, and there is much to observe in the relations between ruler and minister.

In former times, King Cheng had just completed his business in the new city and returned to Zongzhou. Having entrusted the Duke of Zhou with responsibility for remaining behind, he also dispatched a special envoy to admonish the Yin people. Indeed, although the Yin people had long been removed to a distant place, they were now close to the royal house. Reiterating his instructions through a written proclamation would further strengthen their resolve to accept its transforming influence. The gentlemen of Yin, too, had served our dynasty as subjects for years; now that the Duke of Zhou was beginning his administration, renewed admonitions would further encourage their willingness to accept the established order. Yet, urgent though instructing and warning the Yin people certainly was, offering reassurance and recognition to the Duke of Zhou could still less be delayed. Accordingly, through the envoy sent to admonish Yin, the king conveyed a charge of reassurance, with gifts to provide the ceremonial forms and words to express his respect.

As for the gifts, the liquor was brewed from black millet and blended with aromatic herbs. Its vessel was of medium size, what is called a you; the number was two, what is called a peng, or pair. These ceremonial gifts were things required for libations to bring down the spirits, part of the grand rites of the ancestral temple. In presenting them to the duke, was the king not providing extraordinary ceremonial honors? As for the words, they spoke of achieving purity and the utmost reverence to convey sincerity, thereby displaying the virtue of purification and luminous clarity; and of bowing with hands joined and bringing the forehead to the ground in making a gracious offering, thereby observing the proper way of presenting fine offerings. This reverence was solemnly maintained when conducting sacrifices and expressed when the spirits were illustriously present. In extending it to the duke, was the king not conveying extraordinary respect?

The Duke of Zhou’s account of King Cheng’s dispatch of the envoy and bestowal of the charge is detailed and unabridged simply because these ceremonial honors and this respect were extraordinary. Otherwise, how could matters of wine, sweet liquor, and ritual vessels have warranted so much speech from the Duke of Zhou? From this, moreover, a further insight emerges: the Duke of Zhou, upon King Cheng’s …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
錫命盖不敢宿而禋于文武矣是周公之存也
且不敢以秬鬯之奉自安則其没也廟之以天
子之禮公其顧歆乎故君子之愛人孝子之事
親惟其當而已使成王之賜伯禽之受非誣則
其於周公也亦淺矣
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼既同上入執宫功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播
===
百穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌
陰四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭九月肅霜十
月滌場朋酒斯饗曰殺羔羊躋彼公堂
稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
李溥
同考試官教諭胡批〔此題傳釋明白場中作者區〕
〔區於禦寒備暑之說殊非大旨此篇深得邠民相與警戒〕
〔為農勸戒為君之意必熟於是經者宜置高選〕
同考試官學正裘批〔此作以邠民警戒勸戒立說〕
punctuated:
錫命，盖不敢宿而禋于文武矣。是周公之存也，且不敢以秬鬯之奉自安，則其没也，廟之以天子之禮，公其顧歆乎？故君子之愛人，孝子之事親，惟其當而已。使成王之賜、伯禽之受非誣，則其於周公也亦淺矣。
詩
九月築場圃，十月納禾稼。黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫，我稼既同，上入執宫功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。二之日鑿冰冲冲，三之日納于凌陰。四之日其蚤，獻羔祭韭。九月肅霜，十月滌場。朋酒斯饗，曰殺羔羊。躋彼公堂，稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆！
李溥
同考試官教諭胡批〔此題傳釋明白，場中作者區〕〔區於禦寒備暑之說，殊非大旨。此篇深得邠民相與警戒〕〔為農、勸戒為君之意，必熟於是經者，宜置高選。〕
同考試官學正裘批〔此作以邠民警戒勸戒立說〕
translation_en:
…the royal bestowal: he presumably dared not let a night pass before making a sacrificial offering to Kings Wen and Wu. Thus, even while alive, the Duke of Zhou dared not rest content in personally enjoying the gift of black-millet aromatic sacrificial wine. After his death, then, would he turn toward and accept sacrifices offered to him in his temple with the rites proper to the Son of Heaven? Therefore, in a gentleman’s love for others and a filial son’s service to his parents, what matters is simply doing what is fitting. If the account of King Cheng’s bestowal and Bo Qin’s acceptance is not false, their understanding of the Duke of Zhou was indeed shallow.
Book of Odes
In the ninth month we prepare the threshing ground where the gardens were; in the tenth month we bring in the crops: broomcorn and foxtail millet, late- and early-ripening grain, grain and hemp, beans and wheat. Ah, we farmers! Our crops are now gathered; we go up into the settlement to undertake work on the houses. By day you gather thatching grass; by night you twist rope. Hurry up onto the roofs, for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains. In the days of the second month, we hew ice with resounding blows; in the days of the third month, we store it in the icehouse. In the days of the fourth month, early in the season, we offer a lamb and sacrifice with chives. In the ninth month comes the sharp frost; in the tenth month we clear the threshing ground. With paired vessels of wine we hold a feast, saying, “Slaughter the lambs!” We ascend the lord’s hall and raise the rhinoceros-horn cup: “May you live ten thousand years without end!”
Li Pu
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor of a county Confucian school: 〔The commentary explains this topic clearly. Writers in the examination confined〕〔themselves to explanations about warding off cold and preparing for heat, which quite miss its main purport. This essay deeply grasps the meaning of the people of Bin admonishing one another〕〔in their work as farmers and exhorting and admonishing one another in their service to their lord. Its author must be thoroughly familiar with this classic and deserves a high ranking.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Qiu, Instructor of a subprefectural Confucian school: 〔This composition bases its argument on the admonitions and exhortations exchanged among the people of Bin〕…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
深合題意且筆力老健必非膚淺之學也可嘉可嘉
考試官侍講彭批篇末數語殊有餘味
考試官洗馬鄭批邠人憂勤忠愛之意溢于
言表善說詩者也
邠民爲農而相警戒有憂勤之意爲君而相勸
戒有忠愛之心夫賴以養生者在農而所以得
安於農者則君也邠民方以農事相與警戒遽
以君事相與勸戒誠知所本而風俗淳厚也歟
周公備述以教成王宜矣想夫邠人之意謂夫
===
時維九月場可治矣則種藝之圃築堅而場之
焉時維十月場已治矣則禾稼之穫自田而納
之焉黍稷重穋所納非一類也禾麻菽麥所登
非一種也於是嗟嘆以爲我農之力於田者其
稼既聚矣我室之在邑者可以上入而執其修
治之功矣彼茅所以供苫覆者晝焉而往取索
所以爲繆葺者宵焉而是綯兼晝夜之不息急
乘屋以致功蓋以嗣歲復来播穀復始而不暇
於此矣夫當農事之甫畢又念農事之將始不
punctuated:
深合題意，且筆力老健，必非膚淺之學也，可嘉，可嘉！
考試官侍講彭批：篇末數語，殊有餘味。
考試官洗馬鄭批：邠人憂勤忠愛之意，溢于言表，善說詩者也。
邠民爲農而相警戒，有憂勤之意；爲君而相勸戒，有忠愛之心。夫賴以養生者在農，而所以得安於農者則君也。邠民方以農事相與警戒，遽以君事相與勸戒，誠知所本而風俗淳厚也歟！周公備述以教成王，宜矣。想夫邠人之意，謂夫時維九月，場可治矣，則種藝之圃，築堅而場之焉；時維十月，場已治矣，則禾稼之穫，自田而納之焉。黍稷重穋，所納非一類也；禾麻菽麥，所登非一種也。於是嗟嘆以爲我農之力於田者，其稼既聚矣；我室之在邑者，可以上入而執其修治之功矣。彼茅所以供苫覆者，晝焉而往取；索所以爲繆葺者，宵焉而是綯。兼晝夜之不息，急乘屋以致功，蓋以嗣歲復来，播穀復始，而不暇於此矣。夫當農事之甫畢，又念農事之將始，不
translation_en:
…accords deeply with the meaning of the topic. Moreover, the writing is mature and vigorous: this surely cannot be the product of superficial learning. Admirable, admirable!

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor-in-waiting: The final few phrases have a particularly lingering resonance.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Editorial Director: The concern, diligence, loyalty, and affection of the people of Bin overflow beyond the words themselves. This writer interprets the Book of Poetry well.

When the people of Bin admonished one another about farming, they showed concern and diligence; when they encouraged and admonished one another in matters concerning their ruler, they showed loyalty and affection. For farming is what people depend upon to sustain their lives, while the ruler enables them to pursue farming in peace. The people of Bin had just been admonishing one another about agricultural affairs when they turned to encouraging and admonishing one another about service to their ruler. Surely they understood the foundation on which they depended, and their customs were simple and generous! It was fitting that the Duke of Zhou should recount all this to instruct King Cheng. We may imagine the people of Bin expressing their thoughts as follows:

It is the ninth month, and the threshing ground can now be prepared: they tamp firm the garden plots where crops were grown and make them into a threshing ground. It is the tenth month, and the threshing ground is ready: they bring in the harvested crops from the fields. Glutinous millet and common millet, late-ripening and early-ripening grain—the produce brought in is of many kinds. Grain, hemp, beans, and wheat—the harvest comprises more than one variety. Then they sigh and say: “We farmers have labored in the fields, and our crops have now been gathered. We may go up into our houses in the settlement and undertake their repair.” The thatching grass needed to cover the roofs they go out to gather by day; the ropes needed to bind and repair the thatch they twist by night. Working without rest both day and night, they hasten to climb onto the roofs and complete the work, because the coming year will soon arrive, grain sowing will begin again, and they will have no leisure for these tasks. Thus, just as the farming work has ended, they already think of its beginning again, without…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
待督責自相警戒其憂勤之意何如哉然猶未
也又以爲二陽之月之日爲公而伐氷冲冲焉
三陽之月之日取氷而納之凌陰焉誠以四陽
之月其日之蚤君將獻羔韭以祭司寒之神遂
啓氷而先寢廟之薦矣至於九月時已氣肅而
霜降十月則當速畢其場功於是酒則尊兩壺
以爲饗牲必兼羔羊而特殺將携以往升公之
堂舉兕觥之觫祝吾君之壽祝壽而曰萬壽則
極其數之盈也萬壽而曰無疆則申其意於不
===
已也夫汲汲於趨公之後又惓惓於享上之心
相勸以亟相戒以預其忠愛之意何如哉嗟夫
此邠俗之舊而公劉后稷之化其王業之始基
歟成王周公之際則固已彌文矣稼穡艱難之
事君民相與之真淳厚朴野之習其不得而接
於耳目者有矇瞍朝夕之誦焉於是周公之慮
盖深遠矣
豈弟君子民之父母
倪天民
punctuated:
待督責，自相警戒，其憂勤之意何如哉！然猶未也，又以爲二陽之月之日，爲公而伐氷冲冲焉；三陽之月之日，取氷而納之凌陰焉。誠以四陽之月，其日之蚤，君將獻羔韭以祭司寒之神，遂啓氷而先寢廟之薦矣。至於九月，時已氣肅而霜降；十月，則當速畢其場功。於是酒則尊兩壺以爲饗，牲必兼羔羊而特殺，將携以往升公之堂，舉兕觥之觫，祝吾君之壽。祝壽而曰萬壽，則極其數之盈也；萬壽而曰無疆，則申其意於不已也。夫汲汲於趨公之後，又惓惓於享上之心，相勸以亟，相戒以預，其忠愛之意何如哉！嗟夫！此邠俗之舊，而公劉后稷之化，其王業之始基歟！成王周公之際，則固已彌文矣。稼穡艱難之事、君民相與之真、淳厚朴野之習，其不得而接於耳目者，有矇瞍朝夕之誦焉。於是周公之慮，盖深遠矣。
豈弟君子，民之父母。
倪天民
translation_en:
…waiting for supervision or reprimand, they admonish and caution one another. How profound their concern and diligence! Yet this is not all. They further consider that, in the month of the second yang, they must cut ice for their lord, with resounding blows; in the month of the third yang, they must take the ice and store it in the icehouse. This is because, early in the month of the fourth yang, their ruler will offer a lamb and chives in sacrifice to the deity who presides over cold, then open the icehouse, giving precedence to offerings in the ancestral temple. By the ninth month, the air has turned sharp and frost descends; in the tenth month, they must swiftly finish their work on the threshing grounds. They therefore set out two vessels of wine for the feast, and for the sacrificial animals include lambs and sheep, specially slaughtered. They will carry these with them and ascend their lord’s hall, raise the rhinoceros-horn cup [?], and wish their ruler long life. In wishing him long life, they say “ten thousand years,” bringing the number to its fullest extent; in saying that these ten thousand years shall be “without limit,” they extend their wish without end. After diligently hastening to their lord’s service, they remain devoted to the thought of feasting their superior. They urge one another to act promptly and caution one another to prepare in advance. How profound their loyalty and love!
Ah! These were the old customs of Bin, the transforming influence of Gong Liu and Hou Ji. Were they not the first foundations of the royal enterprise? By the time of King Cheng and the Duke of Zhou, cultural refinement had certainly grown more elaborate. The hardships of sowing and reaping, the sincerity of the relationship between ruler and people, and their generous, simple, rustic ways—where these could no longer be encountered directly through sight and hearing, there were blind musicians to recite them morning and evening. In this, the Duke of Zhou’s concern was indeed profound and far-reaching.
“The gracious and amiable gentleman is the father and mother of the people.”
Ni Tianmin

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭胡批此本康公戒成王之詩以豈
弟望之場中作者多背本旨此篇意氣舂容辭理平實深
得進戒之意允宜錄出
同考試官學正裘批詩千卷餘作者紛無定見晚
得此篇如獲明珠於瓦礫也用錄以破羣疑
考試官侍講彭批有勸戒微婉之意
考試官洗馬鄭批得旨
大臣之戒君惟欲其德有以子乎民也夫豈弟
者子民之德也爲人君者不有是德何以爲民
===
之父母哉昔召康公之戒成王如此意謂君人
之德莫貴乎豈弟也豈而和順從容藹然春陽
之可掬弟而易直子諒坦然大道之無陂所以
強教之而陶吾民於德化者此也所以悅安之
而躋吾民於平康者此也夫然則可謂豈弟君
子矣豈弟之君子豈不爲民之父母乎夫父母
之於子有教之之道焉今也胥誨胥告雖父母
之成其子者不越是矣非民之父母而何父母
之於子有養之之道焉今也以拊以畜雖父母
punctuated:
同考試官教諭胡批：此本康公戒成王之詩，以豈弟望之。場中作者多背本旨，此篇意氣舂容，辭理平實，深得進戒之意，允宜錄出。

同考試官學正裘批：詩千卷餘，作者紛無定見。晚得此篇，如獲明珠於瓦礫也，用錄以破羣疑。

考試官侍講彭批：有勸戒微婉之意。

考試官洗馬鄭批：得旨。
