大臣之戒君，惟欲其德有以子乎民也。夫豈弟者，子民之德也。爲人君者不有是德，何以爲民之父母哉？昔召康公之戒成王如此，意謂君人之德莫貴乎豈弟也。豈而和順從容，藹然春陽之可掬；弟而易直子諒，坦然大道之無陂。所以強教之而陶吾民於德化者，此也；所以悅安之而躋吾民於平康者，此也。夫然則可謂豈弟君子矣。豈弟之君子，豈不爲民之父母乎？夫父母之於子，有教之之道焉。今也胥誨胥告，雖父母之成其子者，不越是矣，非民之父母而何？父母之於子，有養之之道焉。今也以拊以畜，雖父母
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: This was originally a poem in which Duke Kang admonished King Cheng, expressing the hope that he would be cheerful and kindly. Most candidates in the examination hall departed from its original purport. This essay is composed and expansive in spirit, its language and reasoning straightforward and sound. It deeply grasps the intent of offering admonition and fully deserves to be selected for inclusion.

Associate Examiner Qiu, School Instructor, comments: Among more than a thousand essays on the Poetry, the writers offered a bewildering variety of views without a firm understanding. Finding this essay late in the reading was like discovering a luminous pearl among broken tiles and rubble. It is included to dispel the many doubts.

Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: It conveys exhortation and admonition with subtlety and tact.

Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: It grasps the purport.

When a great minister admonishes his ruler, he desires only that the ruler’s virtue enable him to treat the people as his children. Cheerfulness and kindliness are precisely the virtues by which one treats the people as children. If a ruler lacks these virtues, how can he be the father and mother of the people? Such was the admonition that Duke Kang of Shao formerly addressed to King Cheng. His meaning was that, among the virtues of one who rules others, none is more precious than cheerfulness and kindliness. Cheerful, he is harmonious, accommodating, and composed, with a warmth like spring sunshine that one could gather in one’s hands; kindly, he is easygoing, upright, loving, and trustworthy, as level as a broad road without a slope. It is through these qualities that he earnestly instructs our people and molds them through moral transformation; it is through these qualities that he gladdens and settles them, bringing our people to peace and well-being. Such a ruler may indeed be called a cheerful and kindly gentleman. Is not such a gentleman the father and mother of the people? Parents have a way of teaching their children. Now he instructs and counsels them all; even parents bringing their children to maturity do no more than this. What is he, then, if not the father and mother of the people? Parents have a way of nourishing their children. Now he cherishes and nurtures them; even parents …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
之字其子者不過是矣非民之父母而何民之
戴之亦豈不尊之如父愛之如母哉召公之於
成王其覬幸之意深矣抑成王以幼冲之資撫
盈成之運於修德愛民之事或未之知也故召
公有卷阿之戒公劉之咏而此篇又以豈弟子
民言之此老臣忠愛之心也厥後成王果爲繼
體守成之令主而成鳧鷖旣醉之太平良有以
哉
春秋
===
晋侯入曹執曹伯畀宋人 晋侯齊師宋
師秦師及楚人戰于城濮楚師敗績
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒
子盟于踐土並僖公二十八年
徐佑
同考試官訓導沈 批 能體傳意發揚霸道不計功
之旨筆勢英偉超越衆作麟經魁選屬之子矣
考試官侍講彭 批 盡略浮釅之辭有得謹嚴之意
考試官洗馬鄭 批 文有斷制且得書法微旨佳作也
punctuated:
之字其子者不過是矣，非民之父母而何？民之戴之，亦豈不尊之如父、愛之如母哉？召公之於成王，其覬幸之意深矣。抑成王以幼冲之資，撫盈成之運，於修德愛民之事，或未之知也。故召公有《卷阿》之戒、《公劉》之咏，而此篇又以豈弟子民言之，此老臣忠愛之心也。厥後成王果爲繼體守成之令主，而成《鳧鷖》《旣醉》之太平，良有以哉！

春秋

晋侯入曹，執曹伯，畀宋人。晋侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績。公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子，盟于踐土。並僖公二十八年。

徐佑

同考試官訓導沈 批：能體傳意，發揚霸道不計功之旨，筆勢英偉，超越衆作，麟經魁選屬之子矣。

考試官侍講彭 批：盡略浮釅之辭，有得謹嚴之意。

考試官洗馬鄭 批：文有斷制，且得書法微旨，佳作也。
translation_en:
…in nurturing their children, do no more than this. What, then, could he be but the father and mother of the people? In their allegiance to him, would the people not revere him as a father and love him as a mother? Profound indeed were the hopes that the Duke of Shao placed in King Cheng. Yet King Cheng, young and inexperienced, inherited an era of full prosperity and established achievement; he may not yet have understood the work of cultivating virtue and loving the people. Thus the Duke of Shao offered the admonition of “The Winding Mound” (Juan a) and the verse of “Duke Liu” (Gong Liu), while this poem again speaks of treating the people as one’s children with kindness and ease. Such was this aged minister’s loyal and loving heart. Subsequently, King Cheng did indeed become an excellent ruler who continued the royal succession and preserved its accomplishments, bringing about the great peace depicted in “Wild Ducks and Gulls” (Fu yi) and “Already Drunk” (Ji zui). There was good reason for this!

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Marquis of Jin entered Cao, seized the Earl of Cao, and handed him over to the men of Song. The Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought the men of Chu at Chengpu; the army of Chu suffered a crushing defeat. The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and they concluded a covenant at Jiantu. All these entries are from the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.

Xu You

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Assistant Instructor: He grasps the meaning of the commentary and brings out its principle that the way of the hegemon is not to be judged by achievements. His writing has a heroic vigor that surpasses the other submissions. First place in the Classic of the Unicorn—the Spring and Autumn Annals—belongs to this candidate!

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: He dispenses entirely with superficial and overwrought language and captures the spirit of careful rigor.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: The essay shows decisive judgment and also grasps the subtle import of the Annals’ manner of recording events. An excellent work.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
惟伯主虐内致外之事不可訓故伯主攘外服
内之功不足多此可見晋文以暴譎而成伯其
功雖多而道不足尚也春秋所以備書而致意
焉夫自齊功不續宋事無成荆楚益肆其憑陵
中國盖幾於左衽有晋文者出治曹而恤宋攘
楚而安夏亦春秋之深幸也何乃謂其功雖多
而道不足尚耶道不外乎仁而暴不可以言仁
也曹未狎政莫知所承公不脩辭令以撫曹而
遽入其國遂執其君暴矣暴而不仁於道何如
===
道不離乎正而譎不可以言正也楚方圍宋簡
書可畏公不仗大義以服楚而執曹畀宋怒楚
致師譎矣譎而不正於道又何如道既不足功
多何為故城濮之戰楚勢披靡若可以為功矣
然視諸仗義而執言聲罪以致討者不有間乎
揆之於道固仲尼之徒所羞稱也踐土之盟諸
侯景從宜可以言功矣然視諸以德而服人以
善而養人者不亦遠乎揆之於道固三王之世
所不容也春秋於入曹畀宋之役不以微辭諱
punctuated: 惟伯主虐内致外之事不可訓，故伯主攘外服内之功不足多。此可見晋文以暴譎而成伯，其功雖多，而道不足尚也。《春秋》所以備書而致意焉。夫自齊功不續，宋事無成，荆楚益肆其憑陵，中國盖幾於左衽。有晋文者出，治曹而恤宋，攘楚而安夏，亦《春秋》之深幸也。何乃謂其功雖多而道不足尚耶？道不外乎仁，而暴不可以言仁也。曹未狎政，莫知所承，公不脩辭令以撫曹，而遽入其國，遂執其君，暴矣！暴而不仁，於道何如？道不離乎正，而譎不可以言正也。楚方圍宋，簡書可畏，公不仗大義以服楚，而執曹畀宋，怒楚致師，譎矣！譎而不正，於道又何如？道既不足，功多何為？故城濮之戰，楚勢披靡，若可以為功矣。然視諸仗義而執言，聲罪以致討者，不有間乎？揆之於道，固仲尼之徒所羞稱也。踐土之盟，諸侯景從，宜可以言功矣。然視諸以德而服人，以善而養人者，不亦遠乎？揆之於道，固三王之世所不容也。《春秋》於入曹畀宋之役，不以微辭諱
translation_en:
Since a hegemon’s acts of oppressing those within the central states to provoke those outside cannot serve as a model, his achievements in repelling outsiders and securing submission within deserve little praise. This shows that Duke Wen of Jin attained hegemony through violence and deceit: although his achievements were many, his way was unworthy of esteem. This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals records these matters fully and conveys its judgment through them.

After Qi’s achievements went unsustained and Song’s endeavors came to nothing, Jing-Chu grew ever more unrestrained in its aggression, and the central states nearly came to wear their robes fastened on the left, in the manner of the barbarians. Then Duke Wen of Jin emerged, chastising Cao and relieving Song, repelling Chu and bringing peace to the Xia states. This, too, was a cause for profound satisfaction in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why, then, say that although his achievements were many, his way was unworthy of esteem?

The Way cannot lie outside benevolence, and violence cannot be called benevolent. Cao was not yet accustomed to its government, and its people did not know whom to obey. Instead of framing diplomatic messages to reassure Cao, the duke abruptly entered its territory and then seized its ruler. This was violence! Being violent and lacking benevolence, how did he measure up to the Way? The Way is inseparable from rectitude, and deceit cannot be called upright. Chu was then besieging Song, and the written summons to aid it commanded respect. Instead of relying on the great principles of righteousness to bring Chu into submission, the duke seized Cao and handed it over to Song, provoking Chu’s anger and bringing its army into battle. This was deceit! Being deceitful and lacking rectitude, how, again, did he measure up to the Way? If he fell short of the Way, what use were his many achievements?

Thus, at the battle of Chengpu, Chu’s forces crumbled before him, seemingly an achievement to his credit. Yet was there not a gulf between this and acting upon righteousness with a just cause, proclaiming an adversary’s offenses and undertaking a punitive expedition? Measured against the Way, it was certainly something that the followers of Zhongni would be ashamed to praise. At the covenant of Jiantu, the regional lords followed him like shadows, which should seemingly count as an achievement. Yet was this not far removed from winning people’s submission through virtue and nurturing them through goodness? Measured against the Way, it was certainly something that would not have been tolerated in the age of the Three Kings. In its account of the campaign in which he entered Cao and handed it over to Song, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not conceal his wrongdoing through subtle wording…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而城濮踐土之文復以常辭書然則聖人明道
不計功之意可見矣抑觀文公戰城濮而盟踐
土伯業成矣由是休兵息民脩德行禮猶可以
救始事之失何踐土之盟血未乾又合諸侯以
會溫城濮之大勞甫息又率諸侯以圍許禮煩
而威黷一盛而即衰矣吁此其所以為晋文也
歟
楚公子貞伐鄭〔襄公八年〕公會晋侯宋公衛
侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
===
子齊世子光伐鄭同盟于戲〔九年〕公會
晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世子
光滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭戍鄭
虎牢楚公子貞救鄭〔十年〕公會晋侯宋
公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭同盟于亳城
北公會晋侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子
光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐
鄭會于蕭魚〔十一年〕
punctuated:
而城濮、踐土之文，復以常辭書。然則聖人明道不計功之意可見矣。抑觀文公戰城濮而盟踐土，伯業成矣。由是休兵息民，脩德行禮，猶可以救始事之失。何踐土之盟血未乾，又合諸侯以會溫；城濮之大勞甫息，又率諸侯以圍許？禮煩而威黷，一盛而即衰矣。吁！此其所以為晋文也歟？

楚公子貞伐鄭〔襄公八年〕。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭，同盟于戲〔九年〕。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，戍鄭虎牢。楚公子貞救鄭〔十年〕。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，同盟于亳城北。公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚〔十一年〕。
translation_en:
…Yet the passages concerning Chengpu and Jiantu are likewise recorded in ordinary language. Thus we can discern the sage’s intention to make the Way clear without reckoning achievements. Consider further: Duke Wen fought at Chengpu and concluded the covenant at Jiantu, thereby establishing his hegemony. Had he thereafter rested his troops and given the people respite, cultivated virtue and observed ritual, he could still have remedied the errors of his initial undertakings. Why, before the blood of the covenant at Jiantu was dry, did he again assemble the lords to meet at Wen? Why, scarcely had the great exertions at Chengpu ended, did he again lead the lords to besiege Xu? Ritual became burdensome and military might was used wantonly; scarcely had his power flourished before it declined. Alas! Is this what made him Duke Wen of Jin?

Prince Zhen of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 The duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi 杞, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi 齊, in attacking Zheng. They jointly concluded a covenant at Xi. 〔Ninth year.〕 The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju and Zhu, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They garrisoned Hulao in Zheng. Prince Zhen of Chu came to Zheng’s aid. 〔Tenth year.〕 The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They jointly concluded a covenant north of Bocheng. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. 〔Eleventh year.〕

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
呂傑
同考試官訓導沈批立論謹嚴而不遺傳註措詞
健順而自有準繩紛紛盆盎中有此古壘洗能不爲之拭目
考試官侍講彭批就中提掇善言之從違爲説
異於衆作
考試官洗馬鄭批辭嚴理正必熟於傳者
違嘉謀而致討者春秋示其譏從嘉謀而善勝
者春秋著其美此見鄭簡舎子展之言而不能
息争晋悼行知罃之策而足以復伯也何則策
===
士謀臣天生賢以立國也善言嘉猷賢承天以
賛君也天之所命而君有從違焉則國之盛衰
随見矣是故鄭之賢卿莫賢於子展當楚囊伐
鄭之日鄭伯欲従之際展也進言以决向背以
謂五會之信不可以違遼遠之師不能以久完
守而老楚仗信以待晋豈非謀之善哉使鄭簡
信而従之必無噬臍之悔矣何乃惑於子駟遂
及楚盟告絶之使方馳諸侯之師已集恐懼行
成而鄭之為鄭幾不能以國矣春秋之譏違善
punctuated:
呂傑

同考試官訓導沈批：立論謹嚴，而不遺傳註；措詞健順，而自有準繩。紛紛盆盎中，有此古壘洗，能不爲之拭目？

考試官侍講彭批：就中提掇善言之從違爲説，異於衆作。

考試官洗馬鄭批：辭嚴理正，必熟於傳者。

違嘉謀而致討者，春秋示其譏；從嘉謀而善勝者，春秋著其美。此見鄭簡舎子展之言而不能息争，晋悼行知罃之策而足以復伯也。何則？策士謀臣，天生賢以立國也；善言嘉猷，賢承天以賛君也。天之所命，而君有從違焉，則國之盛衰随見矣。是故鄭之賢卿，莫賢於子展。當楚囊伐鄭之日，鄭伯欲従之際，展也進言以决向背，以謂五會之信不可以違，遼遠之師不能以久，完守而老楚，仗信以待晋，豈非謀之善哉？使鄭簡信而従之，必無噬臍之悔矣。何乃惑於子駟，遂及楚盟？告絶之使方馳，諸侯之師已集。恐懼行成，而鄭之為鄭，幾不能以國矣。春秋之譏，違善
translation_en:
Lü Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Assistant Instructor: The argument is carefully framed and rigorous, without neglecting the commentaries and annotations. The phrasing is vigorous and flowing, yet observes its own standards. Amid a jumble of common pots and bowls, here is an ancient ritual vessel [?]: how could one fail to rub one’s eyes in admiration?

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: He singles out obedience to or rejection of good counsel as the basis of his discussion, distinguishing this essay from the others.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: The language is rigorous and the reasoning sound. He must be thoroughly familiar with the commentary.

When rulers reject good counsel and thereby invite punitive attack, the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses its censure; when they follow good counsel and achieve victory by sound means, the Spring and Autumn Annals records its praise. This is seen in Duke Jian of Zheng’s rejection of Zizhan’s advice, which left him unable to end the conflict, and Duke Dao of Jin’s implementation of Zhi Ying’s strategy, which enabled him to restore his hegemony. Why is this so? Strategists and counseling ministers are worthy men whom Heaven brings forth to establish states. Through sound advice and excellent plans, these worthy men carry out Heaven’s will in assisting their rulers. When rulers either follow or reject what Heaven has ordained, the flourishing or decline of their states becomes evident accordingly.

Thus, among the worthy ministers of Zheng, none was worthier than Zizhan. When Zinang of Chu attacked Zheng, and the Earl of Zheng was about to submit to Chu, Zizhan offered advice to settle which side Zheng should support. He argued that the pledges of five meetings must not be broken and that an army far from home could not remain long. By maintaining their defenses intact, they could wear out Chu; by standing upon their good faith, they could await Jin. Was this not excellent counsel? Had Duke Jian of Zheng trusted and followed it, he would surely have avoided the bitter regret of trying to bite his own navel. Why, then, did he let Zisi mislead him and proceed to make a covenant with Chu? The envoy announcing the severance of relations had only just set off when the armies of the feudal lords had already assembled. In fear, Zheng sought peace, and Zheng could scarcely maintain its existence as a state. The censure of the Spring and Autumn Annals is a warning against rejecting good…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
言之戒也若夫晋之賢佐莫賢於知罃當肆眚
圍鄭之時荀偃决戰之頃罃也獻策以陳利害
以謂暴骨以逞則克不可命以逸待勞則楚不
能争許盟還師以敝乎楚分軍率銳以逆其来
豈非謀之善哉使悼公忽而違之則失善勝之
道矣然而寧違荀偃卒許鄭成三駕示威楚不
戰而自屈一會推誠鄭心服而不叛從容得志
而晋之為伯盛莫越於此矣春秋之美用善言
之效也吁鄭之事無足論矣從嘉謀而成伯功
===
豈惟悼公為然齊桓創伯甞從管仲之諫以懷
鄭晋文繼伯甞從先軫之謀以克楚昔之英君
明辟以善言而興事建勳者多矣雖然發言盈
庭誰執其咎非知言之君子其孰能擇於斯
禮記
天子七廟諸侯五大夫三士一天子之豆
二十有六諸公十有六諸侯十有二上
大夫八下大夫六
盧幹
punctuated:
言之戒也。若夫晋之賢佐，莫賢於知罃。當肆眚圍鄭之時，荀偃决戰之頃，罃也獻策以陳利害，以謂暴骨以逞，則克不可命；以逸待勞，則楚不能争。許盟還師以敝乎楚，分軍率銳以逆其来，豈非謀之善哉？使悼公忽而違之，則失善勝之道矣。然而寧違荀偃，卒許鄭成。三駕示威，楚不戰而自屈；一會推誠，鄭心服而不叛。從容得志，而晋之為伯，盛莫越於此矣。《春秋》之美，用善言之效也。吁！鄭之事無足論矣。從嘉謀而成伯功，豈惟悼公為然？齊桓創伯，甞從管仲之諫以懷鄭；晋文繼伯，甞從先軫之謀以克楚。昔之英君明辟，以善言而興事建勳者多矣。雖然，發言盈庭，誰執其咎？非知言之君子，其孰能擇於斯？

禮記

天子七廟，諸侯五，大夫三，士一。天子之豆二十有六，諸公十有六，諸侯十有二，上大夫八，下大夫六。

盧幹
translation_en:
…a warning against disregarding good counsel. As for the worthy assistants of Jin, none was worthier than Zhi Ying. When an amnesty was proclaimed and Zheng was besieged, and Xun Yan resolved to fight, Ying offered a strategy, setting out the advantages and dangers. He argued that if they exposed their soldiers’ bones merely to gratify their will, victory could not be assured; but if they awaited an exhausted enemy with rested troops, Chu could not contend with them. They should agree to a covenant and withdraw their troops so as to wear Chu down, then divide their forces and lead picked troops to meet its advance. Was this not an excellent plan? Had Duke Dao disregarded and rejected it, he would have lost the way to secure victory skillfully. Instead, he chose to go against Xun Yan and ultimately granted Zheng peace. Through three campaigns he displayed his might, and Chu yielded without fighting; at a single meeting he demonstrated sincerity, and Zheng submitted wholeheartedly and did not rebel. He achieved his aims with composure, and Jin’s hegemony never flourished more greatly than this. The praise in the Spring and Autumn Annals attests to the efficacy of heeding good counsel.

Ah! Zheng’s conduct scarcely merits discussion. Was Duke Dao alone in following excellent plans and thereby achieving hegemony? Duke Huan of Qi, when establishing his hegemony, followed Guan Zhong’s admonition to win Zheng’s allegiance; Duke Wen of Jin, when succeeding to the hegemony, followed Xian Zhen’s plan to defeat Chu. Among the outstanding rulers and enlightened sovereigns of old, many undertook great affairs and established meritorious achievements through good counsel. Yet, “Words fill the court; who will bear the blame?” Without a ruler capable of discerning the worth of words, who could choose among them?

Record of Rites (Liji)

The Son of Heaven has seven ancestral temples; the feudal lords, five; the great officers, three; and the servicemen, one. The Son of Heaven has twenty-six dou offering vessels; the dukes, sixteen; the feudal lords, twelve; the senior great officers, eight; and the junior great officers, six.

Lu Gan

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭蕭批此題論廟豆之數見禮有以
多爲貴作者盖知之詞理俱到不泛不畧如此篇者則亦不
多得也
考試官侍講彭批器數儀節之間禮家所謹此
能悉之
考試官洗馬鄭批敷析詳明
随其分而制廟豆之數此禮之以多爲貴也盖
禮莫大於分也先王制廟豆之數得不各随其
尊卑而爲之等殺也哉記禮器者謂先王之制
===
禮有以多爲貴者以廟制言之廟所以祀先也
而天子諸侯大夫士之廟有差等焉是故天子
則三昭三穆與太祖之廟而七也諸侯則二昭
二穆與太祖之廟而五也大夫則一昭一穆與
太祖之廟而三焉下士則無昭無穆而祖禰共
一廟焉所以然者由尊而卑爲之差等耳其獨
隆於天子者非特以誠深孝篤而然盖不如是
無以致尊祖之義盡親親之仁也禮之見於廟
制者如此以豆數言之豆所以薦羞也而天子
punctuated:
同考試官教諭蕭批：此題論廟豆之數，見禮有以多爲貴。作者盖知之，詞理俱到，不泛不畧，如此篇者則亦不多得也。
考試官侍講彭批：器數儀節之間，禮家所謹，此能悉之。
考試官洗馬鄭批：敷析詳明。
随其分而制廟豆之數，此禮之以多爲貴也。盖禮莫大於分也，先王制廟豆之數，得不各随其尊卑而爲之等殺也哉？記禮器者謂先王之制禮，有以多爲貴者。以廟制言之，廟所以祀先也，而天子、諸侯、大夫、士之廟有差等焉。是故天子則三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七也；諸侯則二昭二穆，與太祖之廟而五也；大夫則一昭一穆，與太祖之廟而三焉；下士則無昭無穆，而祖禰共一廟焉。所以然者，由尊而卑，爲之差等耳。其獨隆於天子者，非特以誠深孝篤而然，盖不如是，無以致尊祖之義，盡親親之仁也。禮之見於廟制者如此。以豆數言之，豆所以薦羞也，而天子
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: This topic discusses the numbers of ancestral temples and dou offering vessels, showing that in ritual there are instances where greater numbers are prized. The author evidently understands this. His expression and reasoning are both fully developed, neither vague nor cursory. Essays such as this are seldom encountered.
Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: The numbers of ritual vessels and the details of ceremonial observance are matters that ritual specialists treat with care. This essay comprehensively explains them.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: The exposition and analysis are detailed and clear.
To prescribe the numbers of ancestral temples and dou offering vessels according to each person's station exemplifies the ritual principle of prizing greater numbers. For nothing in ritual is more important than distinctions of station. When the former kings prescribed the numbers of temples and offering vessels, how could they have failed to establish graduated distinctions according to each person's higher or lower rank? The author of “Ritual Vessels” (Li qi) states that, in the former kings' institution of ritual, there were instances where greater numbers were prized. To speak first of the temple system: temples serve to offer sacrifices to ancestors, and the temples of the Son of Heaven, the feudal lords, the great officers, and the servicemen differ in number according to rank. Thus, the Son of Heaven has three zhao temples and three mu temples, which, together with the temple of the founding ancestor, make seven. The feudal lords have two zhao and two mu temples, which, together with the temple of the founding ancestor, make five. The great officers have one zhao and one mu temple, which, together with the temple of the founding ancestor, make three. The lower-ranking servicemen have neither zhao nor mu temples; their grandfather and father share a single temple. The reason for this is simply to establish graduated distinctions from the highest rank down to the lowest. That the Son of Heaven alone enjoys the fullest provision is not merely because of his profound sincerity and devoted filial piety. Rather, without this provision, he could not fulfill the righteous duty of honoring his ancestors or fully realize the benevolence of affection for his kin. Such is ritual as manifested in the temple system. To speak of the numbers of dou vessels: these vessels serve to present offerings of food, and the Son of Heaven…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
公侯大夫之豆亦有隆殺焉是故天子朔食之
豆二十有六則朝踐八饋食八加豆八羞豆二
也諸公相朝堂上之豆十有六則朝事八而無
加豆饋食八而無羞豆也諸侯相朝堂上之豆
則朝事六饋食六凡十有二焉主國食使臣之
豆則上大夫八下大夫六焉所以然者亦惟自
尊而卑為之隆殺耳其獨尊於天子者非特以
備味多品而然盖不如是無以極九州之美備
四時之和也禮之見於豆數者又如此吁以分
===
之尊卑為數之多寡先王制禮之意不其至歟
大抵禮所以辨上下而定民志也故先王緣情
以制宜隨宜以為貴或多或寡各當其位而不
相紊各稱其情而不相悖不然則尊卑無序貴
賤無等而上下不相安其何以致天下之治哉
故曰安上治民莫善於禮
子民如父母有憯怛之愛有忠利之教親
而尊安而敬威而愛富而有禮惠而能
散
punctuated:
公侯大夫之豆亦有隆殺焉。是故天子朔食之豆二十有六，則朝踐八、饋食八、加豆八、羞豆二也。諸公相朝，堂上之豆十有六，則朝事八而無加豆，饋食八而無羞豆也。諸侯相朝，堂上之豆則朝事六、饋食六，凡十有二焉。主國食使臣之豆，則上大夫八、下大夫六焉。所以然者，亦惟自尊而卑為之隆殺耳。其獨尊於天子者，非特以備味多品而然，盖不如是，無以極九州之美、備四時之和也。禮之見於豆數者又如此。吁！以分之尊卑為數之多寡，先王制禮之意不其至歟？大抵禮所以辨上下而定民志也。故先王緣情以制宜，隨宜以為貴，或多或寡，各當其位而不相紊，各稱其情而不相悖。不然，則尊卑無序，貴賤無等，而上下不相安，其何以致天下之治哉？故曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮。」

子民如父母，有憯怛之愛，有忠利之教，親而尊，安而敬，威而愛，富而有禮，惠而能散。
translation_en:
…dukes, marquises, and grand masters likewise have graded numbers of dou offering vessels. Thus, at the Son of Heaven’s meal on the first day of the month, there are twenty-six dou: eight for the morning presentation, eight for the food offering, eight additional vessels, and two vessels of delicacies. When dukes pay court visits to one another, there are sixteen dou in the hall: eight for the morning service, without additional vessels, and eight for the food offering, without vessels of delicacies. When the other feudal lords pay court visits to one another, the dou in the hall comprise six for the morning service and six for the food offering, twelve in all. When the host state entertains an envoy, there are eight dou for a senior grand master and six for a junior grand master. The reason for this, too, is simply to establish descending gradations from the exalted to the lowly. The uniquely exalted provision for the Son of Heaven is not merely intended to furnish a full range of flavors and a multitude of dishes. Without it, there would be no means of bringing together the finest produce of the Nine Provinces and providing the harmonious flavors of all four seasons. Such, again, is the manifestation of ritual propriety in the number of dou vessels.

Ah! To determine greater or smaller numbers according to higher or lower station—was not the intention of the former kings in establishing ritual most consummate? In general, ritual serves to distinguish superiors from inferiors and to settle the people’s minds. Thus the former kings established what was fitting on the basis of human feelings and esteemed what accorded with that fitness. Whether the number was greater or smaller, each provision suited its station without confusion and matched the feelings involved without contradiction. Otherwise, the exalted and lowly would lack proper order, the noble and humble would lack distinctions, and superiors and inferiors would be uneasy with one another. How could order throughout the realm then be achieved? Hence the saying: “For securing those above and governing the people, nothing surpasses ritual.”

Treat the people as one’s children, as a father and mother would: have deeply compassionate love and instruction devoted to their benefit. Be affectionate yet dignified, at ease yet respectful, awe-inspiring yet loving, wealthy yet observant of ritual, and benevolent and able to distribute one’s resources.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
方榮
同考試官教諭蕭批表記此題傳註明白作者臆
說紛紛令人厭觀此卷體認真切發明教養之道通貫
無遺非熟於禮者不能本房之冠舍子其誰
考試官侍講彭批文意通貫
考試官洗馬鄭批辭暢而理亦足可取
聖人論聖君之子民盡教養之道而無偏也盖
教養兼盡而無偏子民之道也此聖君所以能
盡乎仁也歟昔吾夫子論君道之難於盡仁而
===
及此謂夫虞舜之君天下也心乎斯民猶父母
之於子而教養之兼盡焉以言其養則慘怛之
心發於至誠真猶母之愛其子也如拯民於洪
水之災洽民于好生之德非責報於人非要譽
於衆其養之盡其道也何如以言其教則忠利
之道本乎實心真猶父之教其子也如命官以
教人倫制器以利民用有教人以善之實有通
變宜民之功其教之盡其道也又何如惟其愛
也則有以致其親而和之於內豈不猶母之親
punctuated:
方榮。
同考試官教諭蕭批：「表記此題，傳註明白，作者臆說紛紛，令人厭觀。此卷體認真切，發明教養之道，通貫無遺，非熟於禮者不能。本房之冠，舍子其誰？」
考試官侍講彭批：「文意通貫。」
考試官洗馬鄭批：「辭暢而理亦足，可取。」
聖人論聖君之子民，盡教養之道而無偏也。盖教養兼盡而無偏，子民之道也。此聖君所以能盡乎仁也歟！昔吾夫子論君道之難於盡仁，而及此，謂夫虞舜之君天下也，心乎斯民，猶父母之於子，而教養之兼盡焉。以言其養，則慘怛之心發於至誠，真猶母之愛其子也。如拯民於洪水之災，洽民于好生之德，非責報於人，非要譽於衆，其養之盡其道也何如！以言其教，則忠利之道本乎實心，真猶父之教其子也。如命官以教人倫，制器以利民用，有教人以善之實，有通變宜民之功，其教之盡其道也又何如！惟其愛也，則有以致其親，而和之於內，豈不猶母之親
translation_en:
Fang Rong.

Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “For this topic from ‘The Record of Exemplary Conduct’ (Biao ji), the commentaries are clear, yet writers produce a profusion of conjectural explanations that make tiresome reading. This script grasps the meaning accurately and profoundly and elucidates the way of teaching and nurturing with complete coherence, leaving nothing out. Only someone thoroughly versed in ritual could achieve this. Who but you could rank first in this examining room?”

Examiner Peng, Expositor-in-waiting, comments: “The ideas in the essay are coherent throughout.”

Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: “The language flows smoothly, and the reasoning is also sufficient. Worth accepting.”

In discussing how a sage ruler treats the people as his children, the Sage shows that he fulfills the way of teaching and nurturing without partiality. To fulfill both teaching and nurturing without favoring either is indeed the way to treat the people as one’s children. Is this not how the sage ruler fully realizes benevolence? In former times, our Master, discussing the difficulty of fully realizing benevolence in rulership, came to this point. He meant that when Yu Shun ruled All-under-Heaven, his concern for the people was like that of parents for their children, and he fulfilled both teaching and nurturing.

As for his nurturing, his compassionate heart arose from the utmost sincerity, truly like a mother’s love for her child. Thus he rescued the people from the calamity of the great flood and suffused them with the virtue of cherishing life. He neither demanded repayment from others nor sought praise from the multitude. How completely he fulfilled the way of nurturing!

As for his teaching, his way of devotedly benefiting others was rooted in a sincere heart, truly like a father’s instruction of his child. Thus he appointed officials to teach human relationships and fashioned implements for the people’s use. There was the substance of teaching people goodness and the achievement of adapting to change to meet their needs. How completely, again, he fulfilled the way of teaching!

Precisely through his love, he could bring about their affection and harmonize them inwardly. Was this not like a mother’s affection…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
乎惟其教也則有以致其尊而率之於外豈不
猶父之尊乎親而有所尊則和靖以安而莊敬
之心于焉而存尊而有所親則德威惟威而慈
愛之念于焉而著安而敬則富而能節於物而
驕奢之患無有焉威而愛則惠而能周於物而
偏黨之私無有焉吁尊親兼盡教養無偏此有
虞聖人所以能用中於民而盡君道之仁也歟
抑考表記此章言君道之難於盡仁惟舜可以
為德之至然此言愛敬之事特舜之粗迹耳果
===
極致乎下文言君子化之皆為全德特舜之德
廣耳果聖人之道化止於君子而已哉讀者詳
之
第貳場
論
聖人太極之全體
楊本清
同考試官訓導沈批論場欲觀士子性理實學
作者類為浮泛之辭無所發明惟是作議論精明文章醇
punctuated:
乎？惟其教也，則有以致其尊而率之於外，豈不猶父之尊乎？親而有所尊，則和靖以安，而莊敬之心于焉而存；尊而有所親，則德威惟威，而慈愛之念于焉而著。安而敬，則富而能節於物，而驕奢之患無有焉；威而愛，則惠而能周於物，而偏黨之私無有焉。吁！尊親兼盡，教養無偏，此有虞聖人所以能用中於民而盡君道之仁也歟！抑考《表記》，此章言君道之難於盡仁，惟舜可以為德之至。然此言愛敬之事，特舜之粗迹耳，果極致乎？下文言君子化之，皆為全德，特舜之德廣耳，果聖人之道化止於君子而已哉？讀者詳之。

第貳場

論

聖人太極之全體

楊本清

同考試官訓導沈批：論場欲觀士子性理實學，作者類為浮泛之辭，無所發明。惟是作議論精明，文章醇
translation_en:
…as with the affection felt for a mother? Through his instruction, he inspires reverence and guides them in their outward conduct: is this not like the reverence felt for a father? When affection is accompanied by reverence, harmony and tranquillity bring peace, while a solemn and respectful disposition remains. When reverence is accompanied by affection, the awe inspired by virtue is true awe, while loving concern becomes manifest. With peace and respect, people can be wealthy yet restrained in their use of things, free of the evils of arrogance and extravagance. With awe and love, beneficence can extend to all, free of the selfishness of partiality and faction. Ah! Bringing both reverence and affection to fulfilment, and neglecting neither instruction nor nurture: was this not how the sage of Youyu could apply the mean in governing the people and fully realize the benevolence proper to a ruler?

Yet consider the “Record of Exemplary Conduct” (Biaoji). This chapter speaks of the difficulty a ruler faces in fully realizing benevolence, and holds that only Shun may be deemed to have attained the utmost virtue. But the acts of love and respect described here are merely the outward traces of Shun’s conduct. Do they really represent its highest attainment? The following passage says that gentlemen were transformed by him and all attained complete virtue; this merely indicates how widely Shun’s virtue extended. Could the transforming influence of the sage’s Way really have reached only gentlemen? Readers should examine this carefully.

Second Session

Discourse

“The Sage Embodies the Supreme Ultimate in Its Entirety”

Yang Benqing

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, an Assistant Instructor: The discourse session is intended to reveal candidates’ substantial learning concerning human nature and principle. Writers generally offer superficial, vague language that illuminates nothing. This composition alone presents incisive and lucid arguments, and its prose is refined…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
古盖嘗潜心濂溪考亭之學者歟
考試官侍講彭批作論者鶩於誇多闘靡之習
簡切如此者亦未必不佳也
考試官洗馬鄭批理學精深非可臆說此作見
理明白措辭醇正其積學之士乎宜在優選
論曰太極者何陰陽之道也陰陽者何動靜之
迹也聖人者何人之至而天地之參也聖人所
以參天地而成位乎中者全動靜之德一太極
之本然而已盖自上天之載而言之則所謂造
===
化之樞紐品彙之根柢者此太極也自其在人
而言之則中正仁義所謂天之命人之性動靜
之德者聖人固無毫髮之不盡而亦豈能有毫
髮之加哉是之謂太極之全體盖嘗觀於穹壤
之間矣何者而非太極之所形何者而非太極
之所妙形者其氣之著也妙者其理之所以然
也真精之合而萬物化生靈秀所鍾而在人獨
異故曰中曰正凡橫目之民無不具曰仁曰義
凡黔首之輩靡不全然中正仁義雖曰稟賦未
punctuated:
古，盖嘗潜心濂溪、考亭之學者歟？
考試官侍講彭批：作論者鶩於誇多闘靡之習，簡切如此者，亦未必不佳也。
考試官洗馬鄭批：理學精深，非可臆說。此作見理明白，措辭醇正，其積學之士乎？宜在優選。
論曰：太極者何？陰陽之道也。陰陽者何？動靜之迹也。聖人者何？人之至而天地之參也。聖人所以參天地而成位乎中者，全動靜之德，一太極之本然而已。盖自上天之載而言之，則所謂造化之樞紐、品彙之根柢者，此太極也。自其在人而言之，則中正仁義，所謂天之命、人之性、動靜之德者，聖人固無毫髮之不盡，而亦豈能有毫髮之加哉？是之謂太極之全體。盖嘗觀於穹壤之間矣，何者而非太極之所形？何者而非太極之所妙？形者，其氣之著也；妙者，其理之所以然也。真精之合而萬物化生，靈秀所鍾而在人獨異。故曰中、曰正，凡橫目之民無不具；曰仁、曰義，凡黔首之輩靡不全。然中正仁義，雖曰稟賦未
translation_en:
…classical in style. Perhaps he has devoted himself to the teachings of Lianxi and Kaoting [Zhou Dunyi and Zhu Xi]?
Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: Writers of discourses pursue the habit of displaying extensive learning and competing in ornate language. A work as concise and pertinent as this may well also be judged excellent.
Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: The learning of principle is profound and cannot be discussed through mere conjecture. This work shows a clear understanding of principle and employs pure and correct language. Is its author not a scholar of accumulated learning? It deserves a place among the best selections.
The discourse says: What is the Supreme Ultimate? It is the Way of yin and yang. What are yin and yang? They are the manifestations of activity and stillness. What is the sage? He is the utmost perfection of humanity and forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. What enables the sage to form this triad and establish his place between them is simply that he fully realizes the virtues of activity and stillness and is one with the original nature of the Supreme Ultimate. Speaking in terms of the workings of Heaven above, what is called the pivot of creation and transformation and the root of all categories of beings is this Supreme Ultimate. Speaking in terms of its presence in human beings, it is centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness—what are called Heaven’s mandate, human nature, and the virtues of activity and stillness. The sage assuredly leaves not the slightest part of these unrealized; yet how could he add even the slightest thing to them? This is what is meant by the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate.
I have contemplated what lies between Heaven and Earth. What is there that does not give form to the Supreme Ultimate? What is there in which its wondrous operation is not present? Its taking form is the manifestation of its material force; its wondrous operation is the principle that makes it so. Through the union of the true and the vital essences, the myriad things are generated through transformation; the concentration of spiritual and refined qualities makes human beings uniquely different. Thus, as for centrality and correctness, all people possess them; as for benevolence and righteousness, all common people have them in full. Yet although it may be said that, in the endowment of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness, there has never …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
嘗不同也而不能不奪於情偽之相感利害之
相攻中或失於偏倚正或失於邪回仁或至於
殘忍義或至於無耻支離决裂而違太極遠矣
况可謂太極之全體乎雖曰性分未有不兼也
然清濁之相揉純駁之相雜或正也而未必得
於中或仁也而未必諧於義虧欠間隔而於太
極之本然有不完矣又可謂太極之全體乎惟
聖人得夫秀而秀者其行之也中其處之也正
不假脩為而從容乎中道其發之也仁其裁之
===
也義不待勉強而自然其無疵故太極動而生
陽則誠之通也繼之者善也元亨之德也萬物
之所資以始也而聖人之動而為仁為中者以
之太極靜而生陰則誠之復也成之者性也利
貞之德也萬物之所以各正性命也而聖人之
靜而為義為正者以之萬物體統一太極是太
極無一物而不包而聖人渾然一理之具於心
者非太極之全體乎一物各具一太極是太極
無一物之不在而聖人泛應曲當之見於用者
punctuated: 嘗不同也，而不能不奪於情偽之相感、利害之相攻。中或失於偏倚，正或失於邪回，仁或至於殘忍，義或至於無耻，支離决裂而違太極遠矣，况可謂太極之全體乎？雖曰性分未有不兼也，然清濁之相揉、純駁之相雜，或正也而未必得於中，或仁也而未必諧於義，虧欠間隔而於太極之本然有不完矣，又可謂太極之全體乎？惟聖人得夫秀而秀者，其行之也中，其處之也正，不假脩為而從容乎中道；其發之也仁，其裁之也義，不待勉強而自然其無疵。故太極動而生陽，則誠之通也，繼之者善也，元亨之德也，萬物之所資以始也，而聖人之動而為仁為中者以之。太極靜而生陰，則誠之復也，成之者性也，利貞之德也，萬物之所以各正性命也，而聖人之靜而為義為正者以之。萬物體統一太極，是太極無一物而不包，而聖人渾然一理之具於心者，非太極之全體乎？一物各具一太極，是太極無一物之不在，而聖人泛應曲當之見於用者
translation_en:
…have never differed, yet they cannot help being overwhelmed by the interplay of genuine and false feelings and the clash of advantage and harm. Centrality may lapse into partiality, correctness into perversity, benevolence into cruelty, and righteousness into shamelessness. Fragmented and torn apart, they depart far from the Supreme Ultimate; how, then, could they be called its complete embodiment? Although one may say that all these virtues are included in everyone’s inherent nature, the clear and turbid intermingle, and the pure and mixed become entangled. One may be correct without necessarily attaining centrality, or benevolent without necessarily according with righteousness. With deficiencies and divisions, one falls short of the original completeness of the Supreme Ultimate. How, again, could this be called its complete embodiment?
Only the sage receives the finest of the finest endowment. In acting he achieves centrality; in remaining at rest he achieves correctness. Without relying on deliberate cultivation, he moves at ease along the mean. In giving expression he is benevolent; in making determinations he is righteous. Without awaiting strenuous effort, he is naturally free from flaws. Thus, when the Supreme Ultimate moves and generates yang, this is the flowing forth of sincerity; what continues it is goodness. These are the virtues of origination and flourishing, upon which the myriad things depend for their beginning. Through this, the sage’s activity constitutes benevolence and centrality. When the Supreme Ultimate becomes still and generates yin, this is the return of sincerity; what completes it is nature. These are the virtues of benefit and constancy, through which each of the myriad things attains its proper nature and allotted destiny. Through this, the sage’s stillness constitutes righteousness and correctness.
The myriad things, taken together as a whole, are one Supreme Ultimate: thus there is nothing that the Supreme Ultimate does not embrace. Is not the single, undivided principle fully present in the sage’s heart the complete embodiment of the Supreme Ultimate? Each individual thing possesses a Supreme Ultimate in its entirety: thus there is nothing in which the Supreme Ultimate is not present. And the sage’s responsiveness to all things, fitting each particular circumstance, as manifested in his functioning…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
又非太極之全體乎中也仁也而太極之用以
行正也義也而太極之體以立由是而有以一
天下之動由是而有以立斯人之極所以與天
地合其德日月合其明四時合其序鬼神合其
吉凶首出庶物而為人之至也歟是知陰陽成
象而天道立矣天一太極也剛柔成質而地道
立矣地一太極也仁義成德而人道立矣聖人
一太極也天地聖人雖三才之不同其實一太
極而已噫聖人合動靜之德故為太極之全體
===
其未至於聖人者夫何如曰脩之而已脩之何
如曰持敬寡欲而已寡之又寡以至於無則靜
虛動直而聖可學矣雖然此非愚之言也考亭
之論也濂溪周子之意也
表
擬
詔加崇闕里釋奠禮樂衍聖公謝表
蕭瓛
同考試官教諭胡 批 表得體
punctuated:
又非太極之全體乎？中也，仁也，而太極之用以行；正也，義也，而太極之體以立。由是而有以一天下之動，由是而有以立斯人之極，所以與天地合其德，日月合其明，四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶，首出庶物而為人之至也歟！是知陰陽成象而天道立矣，天一太極也；剛柔成質而地道立矣，地一太極也；仁義成德而人道立矣，聖人一太極也。天地聖人，雖三才之不同，其實一太極而已。噫！聖人合動靜之德，故為太極之全體。其未至於聖人者，夫何如？曰：脩之而已。脩之何如？曰：持敬寡欲而已。寡之又寡，以至於無，則靜虛動直，而聖可學矣。雖然，此非愚之言也，考亭之論也，濂溪周子之意也。
表
擬詔加崇闕里釋奠禮樂衍聖公謝表
蕭瓛
同考試官教諭胡 批：表得體。
translation_en:
…is this not also the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety? Through centrality and benevolence, the functioning of the Supreme Ultimate proceeds; through correctness and righteousness, its substance is established. Thus there is a means to unify all activity under Heaven, and thus there is a means to establish the ultimate standard for humankind. Hence the sage accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth, in brightness with the sun and moon, in order with the four seasons, and in auspiciousness and inauspiciousness with spirits. Does he not stand foremost among the myriad beings and constitute the utmost perfection of humanity?
From this we know that yin and yang form images, and the Way of Heaven is established: Heaven is one Supreme Ultimate. The hard and the soft form material substance, and the Way of Earth is established: Earth is one Supreme Ultimate. Benevolence and righteousness constitute virtue, and the human Way is established: the sage is one Supreme Ultimate. Although Heaven, Earth, and the sage differ as the Three Powers, in reality they are simply one Supreme Ultimate. Ah! The sage unites the virtues of activity and stillness and therefore embodies the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.
What, then, should those who have not yet attained sagehood do? The answer is: cultivate themselves, and that is all. How should they cultivate themselves? The answer is: maintain reverent attentiveness and lessen their desires, and that is all. Lessen them again and again until none remain; then one will be empty in stillness and upright in activity, and sagehood can be learned. Yet these are not my humble words: this is the teaching of Kaoting [Zhu Xi], and the intent of Master Zhou of Lianxi [Zhou Dunyi].
Memorial
A simulated memorial of thanks from the Duke for Perpetuating the Sage, upon an imperial decree enhancing the rites and music of the offering ceremony at Queli.
By Xiao Huan 蕭瓛.
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: The memorial conforms to the appropriate form.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正裘批駢儷可觀
考試官侍講彭批作儷語而有渾成意表如是可已
考試官洗馬鄭批典則可嘉
臣某言伏蒙
聖恩遣官祭告闕里加崇釋奠禮樂者伏以
端己無爲丕闡右文之至治自
天有命肅昭崇德之盛儀洙泗增輝雲仍動色
臣惶懼惶懼頓首頓首竊惟闕里有太牢
之祠肇於前漢辟雍用六羽之獻昉自盛
===
唐自是以還每致其意厥名曁物與次俱
升然近代於章服已崇而釋奠之禮樂猶
殺隆文異數蓋有待於
聖明重道尊師示莫加於今昔建白雖由於臣
下施行一斷於
宸衷損益稱情從違協志豆籩登薦上同
郊社之規羽籥在陳非復王侯之制聲容斯備
氣象一新玆蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
punctuated:
同考試官學正裘批：駢儷可觀。
考試官侍講彭批：作儷語而有渾成意，表如是可已。
考試官洗馬鄭批：典則可嘉。
臣某言：伏蒙聖恩，遣官祭告闕里，加崇釋奠禮樂者。伏以端己無爲，丕闡右文之至治；自天有命，肅昭崇德之盛儀。洙泗增輝，雲仍動色。臣惶懼惶懼，頓首頓首。竊惟闕里有太牢之祠，肇於前漢；辟雍用六羽之獻，昉自盛唐。自是以還，每致其意，厥名曁物，與次俱升。然近代於章服已崇，而釋奠之禮樂猶殺。隆文異數，蓋有待於聖明；重道尊師，示莫加於今昔。建白雖由於臣下，施行一斷於宸衷。損益稱情，從違協志。豆籩登薦，上同郊社之規；羽籥在陳，非復王侯之制。聲容斯備，氣象一新。玆蓋伏遇皇帝陛下
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Qiu, Instructor, comments: “The parallel phrasing is impressive.”
Examiner Peng, Expositor, comments: “The paired phrases have a natural unity of meaning. A memorial composed in this manner is entirely satisfactory.”
Examiner Zheng, Librarian, comments: “Its classical propriety deserves praise.”
Your servant, so-and-so, states: I have humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious favor in dispatching an official to offer sacrifice and announce at Queli the enhancement of the rites and music of the offering ceremony to Confucius. I humbly reflect: by maintaining personal rectitude and governing without action, you greatly manifest the consummate rule that honors culture; through a command issued from Heaven, you solemnly display the magnificent ceremonies that exalt virtue. The Zhu and Si rivers gain new luster; the descendants are visibly moved. Your servant is fearful, fearful, and bows his head to the ground, bows his head to the ground.
I respectfully consider that the offering of an ox, sheep, and pig at Queli began under the Former Han, while the presentation of dances in six ranks with feather plumes at the Imperial University began in the flourishing Tang. From then onward, successive rulers devoted attention to these observances, and their designations and material provisions rose with successive gradations [?]. Yet in recent times, although ceremonial dress has already been elevated in dignity, the rites and music of the offering ceremony have remained on a reduced scale. Such splendid observances and exceptional distinctions evidently awaited Your sagely enlightenment. In honoring the Way and venerating the teacher, you have set an example unsurpassed in past or present. Although the proposal originated with your servants below, its implementation was decided entirely in Your imperial heart. Additions and reductions accord with proper feeling; acceptance and rejection accord with your intent. The offering vessels and bamboo baskets are presented according to standards as exalted as those of the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the sacrifices at the altars of Soil and Grain. Feather plumes and flutes are arrayed in a manner no longer confined to the ceremonial regulations for princes and lords. Music and ceremonial display are thus complete, and the entire scene is renewed. This is because we have humbly encountered Your Majesty the Emperor…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
秉心淵塞
凝命穆清
敬德以先
用儒而治
潛心經幄得刪述之精微
垂意人文妙昭回之賁飾惟茲曠典遂出
明時
玉音渙發於九重
天使遠馳於六轡升堂薦告洋洋乎如聞金
===
石之聲夾道瞻趨欣欣然宛有堵墻之集
制實通於天下匪直魯宫士胥慶於寰中
矧惟孔氏臣某紹續前封因緣末系行其
禮奏其樂庸虛深愧於象賢月之恒日之
升感激徒能於華
祝臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
punctuated: 秉心淵塞，凝命穆清，敬德以先，用儒而治。潛心經幄，得刪述之精微；垂意人文，妙昭回之賁飾。惟茲曠典，遂出明時。玉音渙發於九重，天使遠馳於六轡。升堂薦告，洋洋乎如聞金石之聲；夾道瞻趨，欣欣然宛有堵墻之集。制實通於天下，匪直魯宫；士胥慶於寰中，矧惟孔氏！臣某紹續前封，因緣末系，行其禮，奏其樂，庸虛深愧於象賢；月之恒，日之升，感激徒能於華祝。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱
translation_en:
…Your Majesty holds a mind both profound and sincere, and secures the Mandate in solemn purity. You take reverence for virtue as your foremost concern and govern by employing Confucian scholars. Devoting yourself to study in the imperial lecture chamber, you grasp the subtle essence of Confucius’s editing and exposition; attending to cultural refinement, you adorn it wondrously with your far-reaching radiance. Thus this exceptional ceremony has emerged in your enlightened age. Your august pronouncement issues forth from the ninefold palace; your imperial envoy speeds afar with the six reins in hand. Ascending the hall to present offerings and announce the decree, we seem to hear everywhere the sounds of bells and chime stones. Lining the roads to watch the procession, people gather joyfully, packed like a wall. The decree extends throughout the realm, not merely to the temple in Lu; scholars everywhere rejoice together—how much more, then, the Kong lineage!

Your servant, so-and-so, has succeeded to the former enfeoffment by virtue of belonging to a distant branch of the lineage. In performing these rites and having this music played, I am deeply ashamed that my mediocrity and inadequacy fall short of emulating my worthy ancestor. May you endure like the waxing moon and the rising sun: in my gratitude, I can only offer the blessings of Hua. Your servant, looking up to Heaven and revering the sage sovereign, is overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
謝以
聞
第參塲
策
第一問
高輝
同考試官訓導李批筆勢翩翩如天馬行空躡浮
雲而上征非復可施銜勒矣敬羨敬羨
同考試官教諭李批議論英發才氣偉然仰頌
===
聖祖之製覈論漢唐諸君反復頓挫隱然有一唱三嘆之音髙薦何忝
考試官侍講彭批疎密輕重皆有意謂非苟然者
考試官洗馬鄭批五策皆可觀此篇尤善揄揚
文亦滂沛策塲之優者歟
性於天者不必其成於人務於大者無所
事於小聞大道之要則區區之文藝有不
足言而得於天質之美者亦豈規規於綴
緝者之所能及哉盖嘗觀於先哲之論矣
夫留意詞藻之末弊精文義之間此拘儒
punctuated:
謝以聞。
第參塲，策，第一問。
高輝。
同考試官訓導李批：筆勢翩翩，如天馬行空，躡浮雲而上征，非復可施銜勒矣。敬羨，敬羨！
同考試官教諭李批：議論英發，才氣偉然。仰頌聖祖之製，覈論漢唐諸君，反復頓挫，隱然有一唱三嘆之音，髙薦何忝！
考試官侍講彭批：疎密輕重，皆有意謂，非苟然者。
考試官洗馬鄭批：五策皆可觀，此篇尤善揄揚，文亦滂沛，策塲之優者歟！
性於天者，不必其成於人；務於大者，無所事於小。聞大道之要，則區區之文藝有不足言，而得於天質之美者，亦豈規規於綴緝者之所能及哉？盖嘗觀於先哲之論矣。夫留意詞藻之末，弊精文義之間，此拘儒
translation_en:
…to express thanks and bring this to Your Majesty’s attention.

Third Session: Policy Essays, Question One.
Gao Hui.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, an Assistant Instructor: “The strokes of his brush soar gracefully, like a celestial horse coursing through the sky, treading the floating clouds and ascending beyond the reach of bit and bridle. My respectful admiration! My respectful admiration!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, an Instructor: “His arguments are brilliant, his literary talent magnificent. He reverently praises the august founding emperor’s institutions and critically discusses the rulers of Han and Tang. Through his repeated turns and measured cadences, one senses the resonance of a single voice answered by three sighs of appreciation. What shame could there be in recommending him highly?”

Comment by Examiner Peng, an Expositor-in-waiting: “Density and sparseness, lightness and weight—all are deliberate and meaningful; none is haphazard.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, a Librarian: “All five policy essays merit attention. This piece is particularly accomplished in its praise, and its prose flows abundantly. Surely it ranks among the finest in the policy-essay session!”

What is endowed by Heaven need not depend upon human effort for its completion; one who devotes himself to great matters has no need to occupy himself with small ones. Once one has learned the essentials of the Great Way, the petty arts of literary composition scarcely deserve mention. And how could those narrowly preoccupied with piecing words together attain the excellence of one whose natural endowment comes from Heaven? I have considered the discussions of earlier sages. To fix one’s attention on the trifles of ornate diction and exhaust one’s energies amid literary meanings—this is what pedantic scholars …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
曲士之所攻非致治保邦之所急則謂帝
王之學與常人不同者是也然大學之道
修身為本天子庶人其理無二則謂帝王
之學與常人不異者亦是也漢唐以来盖
無足與於斯者高帝以明達之資豁大之
度奔走英豪宰制羣力舉措施為規摹宏
逺出詞吐論氣格開張使其本於身者有
先王講學之功談詩書者非陸賈叔孫生
之陋則大風之作且將有阜財解慍之念
===
而新語之奏豈足以少符其起居造誡之
心哉若夫孝武之好文學魏武之本諸生
唐太宗之才敏夙成玄宗之文譽自負皆
嘗致力於斯事而今昔所共推者至論其
得於天資之高則其視不事詩書者反有
間焉是以橫汾之作後世嘗譏其氣象之
委靡宫體之傳當時已病其純正之不足
曹氏之述作尤多開元之篇製具在品目
高下曾莫遁情使其有見於明良喜起之
punctuated: 曲士之所攻，非致治保邦之所急，則謂帝王之學與常人不同者是也。然大學之道，修身為本，天子庶人，其理無二，則謂帝王之學與常人不異者亦是也。漢唐以来，盖無足與於斯者。高帝以明達之資、豁大之度，奔走英豪，宰制羣力，舉措施為，規摹宏逺；出詞吐論，氣格開張。使其本於身者有先王講學之功，談詩書者非陸賈、叔孫生之陋，則大風之作且將有阜財解慍之念，而新語之奏，豈足以少符其起居造誡之心哉？若夫孝武之好文學，魏武之本諸生，唐太宗之才敏夙成，玄宗之文譽自負，皆嘗致力於斯事，而今昔所共推者。至論其得於天資之高，則其視不事詩書者反有間焉。是以橫汾之作，後世嘗譏其氣象之委靡；宫體之傳，當時已病其純正之不足。曹氏之述作尤多，開元之篇製具在，品目高下，曾莫遁情。使其有見於明良喜起之
translation_en:
…what narrow-minded scholars devote themselves to, rather than what is urgent for achieving good government and safeguarding the state. Thus it is correct to say that the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of ordinary people. Yet the Way of the Great Learning takes self-cultivation as its foundation: from the Son of Heaven to the common people, the principle is the same. Thus it is also correct to say that the learning of emperors and kings does not differ from that of ordinary people. From the Han and Tang onward, scarcely anyone has been worthy of inclusion in this regard. Emperor Gao of Han, endowed with clear understanding and expansive generosity, set heroes in motion and directed their collective strength. His actions and undertakings were grand and far-reaching in conception; his utterances and arguments displayed an expansive spirit and manner. Had his personal cultivation benefited from the former kings’ diligent study, and had those who discussed the Odes and Documents with him not been men of such limited learning as Lu Jia and Master Shusun, then his Song of the Great Wind would also have expressed a wish to enrich the people and relieve their grievances. How, then, could the presentation of the New Discourses have sufficed even slightly to meet his desire for admonitions concerning his daily conduct [?]?
As for Emperor Xiaowu of Han’s fondness for literary learning, Emperor Wu of Wei’s origins among students of the classics, Emperor Taizong of Tang’s precocious talent and quick intelligence, and Emperor Xuanzong’s pride in his literary reputation: all devoted effort to these pursuits and have been praised alike in past and present. Yet when one considers the excellence of their natural endowments, they actually fall short in comparison with the ruler who did not occupy himself with the Odes and Documents. Thus later generations criticized the dispirited tone of the composition on crossing the Fen River, while the palace-style poems that circulated were already faulted in their own day for insufficient purity and correctness. The writings of the Cao family are particularly numerous, and the compositions of the Kaiyuan era remain available in full. When ranked as higher or lower, their true qualities have nowhere to hide. Had they perceived the lofty spirit of the song in which an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers delight in rousing one another to action…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
高致而相與爲允懐典學之實功且将進
而彷彿於六義六體之製豈特頡頏於終
馬褚虞燕許之間哉
天生
聖祖光啓
大明心學得於自然化筆妙於神授敷言之訓
衣被臣民昭回之光藻飾萬物愚嘗詮伏
草茅而竊窺其一二若君臣同游之一語
置之典謨訓誥之列泯乎其無以别也未
===
有外綱常而可以爲君之一言雖千百世
之後聖確乎其不可易也至於訓迪治官
昭陳政體旁盡物情下悉民志補先儒之
所未備正前世之所謬訛鑿鑿如五穀之
療飢布帛之衞寒不可一日而無也又嘗
聞之
先朝之舊臣故老矣以爲
聖心所屬翰墨時御略不駐思而頃刻數百言
意足辭止不復點竄是豈竭精弊神爭妍
punctuated:
高致，而相與爲允懐典學之實功，且将進而彷彿於六義六體之製，豈特頡頏於終馬褚虞燕許之間哉？
天生聖祖，光啓大明，心學得於自然，化筆妙於神授。敷言之訓，衣被臣民；昭回之光，藻飾萬物。愚嘗詮伏草茅，而竊窺其一二。若「君臣同游」之一語，置之典謨訓誥之列，泯乎其無以别也。「未有外綱常而可以爲君」之一言，雖千百世之後聖，確乎其不可易也。至於訓迪治官，昭陳政體，旁盡物情，下悉民志，補先儒之所未備，正前世之所謬訛，鑿鑿如五穀之療飢、布帛之衞寒，不可一日而無也。又嘗聞之先朝之舊臣故老矣，以爲聖心所屬，翰墨時御，略不駐思，而頃刻數百言，意足辭止，不復點竄。是豈竭精弊神、爭妍
translation_en:
…lofty aspiration, and together undertaken the substantive work of sincerely cherishing constant learning, they might further have approached the compositions exemplifying the six principles of poetry and the six literary forms. Would they merely have vied with Zhong [?], Ma, Chu, Yu, Yan, and Xu?
Heaven brought forth our sage founder, who gloriously inaugurated the Great Ming. His learning of the mind came naturally; the wondrous skill of his transforming brush was divinely bestowed. The teachings he set forth clothed his ministers and people; his radiant light adorned all things. I, in my humble obscurity [?], have privately glimpsed one or two examples. Such a phrase as “ruler and ministers roaming together,” if placed among the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements, would blend in without any discernible difference. His statement, “No one can stand outside the cardinal bonds and constant virtues and yet be a ruler,” is so firmly established that even a sage a thousand or a hundred generations hence could not alter it. As for his instructing officials in government, clearly explaining the principles of governance, comprehensively encompassing the circumstances of things, and fully understanding the aspirations of the common people, he supplied what earlier Confucian scholars had left incomplete and corrected the errors of previous ages. These teachings are as sound and indispensable as grain for relieving hunger and cloth for warding off cold: one cannot do without them for a single day. I have also heard from veteran ministers and elders of the former reign that, whenever his sagely mind turned to a subject and he took up brush and ink, he scarcely paused to think before producing several hundred words in an instant. When his meaning was fully expressed, his words stopped; he made no further corrections. Could those who exhaust their energies and wear out their spirits, competing in literary beauty…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
取工較一日之長者可望其萬一哉愚敢
曰
高皇帝之於文盖性之天者也
第二問
方榮
同考試官教諭蕭批理學一策有先儒成說學
者多不之講此篇發明詳盡末復言工夫次第知入德
之門必嘗用心於此者
考試官侍講彭批記憶儒先之論略無所遺
===
考試官洗馬鄭批敷對詳明足見學力
汗牛充棟天下之圖書富矣而闡明夫義
理者惟二三策而已耳際天蟠地天下之
義理廣矣而究極其精微者在方寸間而
已耳盖天下之學莫粹於性理天下之理
不外乎一心故欲究先儒之學當求諸書
欲求先儒之書當究諸心得於心則先儒
之理學可論矣太極西銘探極造化之秘
推明仁孝之理得千載之不傳發前聖之
punctuated:
取工，較一日之長者，可望其萬一哉？愚敢曰：高皇帝之於文，盖性之天者也。

第二問
方榮

同考試官教諭蕭批：理學一策，有先儒成說，學者多不之講。此篇發明詳盡，末復言工夫次第，知入德之門，必嘗用心於此者。

考試官侍講彭批：記憶儒先之論，略無所遺。

考試官洗馬鄭批：敷對詳明，足見學力。

汗牛充棟，天下之圖書富矣，而闡明夫義理者，惟二三策而已耳。際天蟠地，天下之義理廣矣，而究極其精微者，在方寸間而已耳。盖天下之學莫粹於性理，天下之理不外乎一心。故欲究先儒之學，當求諸書；欲求先儒之書，當究諸心。得於心，則先儒之理學可論矣。太極、西銘，探極造化之秘，推明仁孝之理，得千載之不傳，發前聖之
translation_en:
…seeking technical polish and competing for a momentary superiority—could such writers hope to attain even one ten-thousandth of his achievement? I venture to say: Emperor Gao’s literary ability was surely endowed by Heaven in his very nature.

Second Policy Question
Fang Rong

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: On this policy question concerning the learning of principle, earlier Confucian scholars have established explanations, but students often fail to study them. This essay expounds the subject fully and thoroughly. At its close, it also discusses the successive stages of practical effort, showing knowledge of the gateway to virtue. Its author must have devoted serious attention to this subject.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: He recalls the arguments of earlier Confucian scholars, omitting virtually nothing.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Librarian: His response is detailed and lucid, amply demonstrating his scholarly attainment.

Enough to make oxen sweat under their loads and fill buildings to the rafters—the books of the world are abundant indeed. Yet those that elucidate moral principles number only two or three volumes. Extending to the bounds of Heaven and encompassing the earth—the moral principles of the world are vast indeed. Yet that which fathoms their utmost subtlety lies solely within the tiny compass of the heart. For no learning in the world is purer than the study of human nature and principle, and no principle in the world lies outside the single heart. Thus, to investigate the learning of earlier Confucian scholars, one must seek it in their books; to seek what is in their books, one must investigate it in one’s heart. Once it is grasped in the heart, one can discuss their learning of principle. The Supreme Ultimate (Taiji) and the Western Inscription (Ximing) probe the deepest mysteries of creation and transformation and elucidate the principles of benevolence and filial piety. They recover what had gone untransmitted for a thousand years and bring to light what the earlier sages…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
未發誠理學之宗也愚嘗因程朱之言究
二書之旨矣請陳其槩太極圖說首言陰
陽變化之原繼以人物禀受之序惟人也
得其秀而最靈純粹至善之性也是所謂
太極也形生神發其陽動陰靜之為乎五
性感動其陽變陰合而生五行之性乎曰
善惡生萬事出其成男成女萬物化生之
象乎終之以易者豈不以易之為書廣大
悉備而圖有以盡之歟首尾相因有緒而
===
不遺脉絡貫通有條而不紊朱子之言可
謂深得其旨矣彼謂傳於种放之徒近於
老氏之說者何足以知之西銘一篇始言
乾為父坤為母所謂理一也然乾坤者天
地之父母而父母者一身之父母非所謂
分殊乎民為同胞物為吾與自天下之父
母言之所謂理一也然謂之民則非真以
為吾之同胞謂之物則非真以為吾之同
類自一身之父母言之非所謂分殊乎至
punctuated: 未發，誠理學之宗也。愚嘗因程朱之言，究二書之旨矣。請陳其槩。《太極圖說》首言陰陽變化之原，繼以人物禀受之序。「惟人也，得其秀而最靈」，純粹至善之性也，是所謂太極也。「形生神發」，其陽動陰靜之為乎？「五性感動」，其陽變陰合而生五行之性乎？曰「善惡生，萬事出」，其成男成女、萬物化生之象乎？終之以《易》者，豈不以《易》之為書，廣大悉備，而圖有以盡之歟？首尾相因，有緒而不遺；脉絡貫通，有條而不紊。朱子之言，可謂深得其旨矣。彼謂傳於种放之徒、近於老氏之說者，何足以知之？《西銘》一篇，始言乾為父、坤為母，所謂理一也。然乾坤者，天地之父母，而父母者，一身之父母，非所謂分殊乎？「民為同胞，物為吾與」，自天下之父母言之，所謂理一也。然謂之民，則非真以為吾之同胞；謂之物，則非真以為吾之同類。自一身之父母言之，非所謂分殊乎？至
translation_en:
…what the earlier sages had not yet expressed: these are truly foundational works of the learning of principle. I have sought to investigate the purport of these two works through the words of the Cheng masters and Zhu Xi. Allow me to outline it.

The Explanation of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tushuo) first discusses the source of the transformations of yin and yang, then the sequence in which human beings and other things receive their endowments. “Human beings alone receive their finest essence and are the most spiritually perceptive”: this is the pure and supremely good nature, what is called the Supreme Ultimate. “Physical form is born, and spirit becomes active”: is this not the working of yang in motion and yin at rest? “The five aspects of the nature are stirred into activity”: is this not the nature arising when yang transforms and yin unites to generate the Five Phases? It says, “Good and evil arise, and the myriad affairs emerge”: is this not the image of the formation of male and female and the transformative generation of the myriad things? Does it not conclude with the Book of Changes because that book is vast and all-encompassing, and the diagram can encompass it fully? Beginning and end follow from each other, forming an ordered sequence with nothing omitted; its underlying connections run throughout, systematically and without confusion. Master Zhu’s words may indeed be said to grasp its purport profoundly. How could those who claim that it was transmitted through the likes of Chong Fang, and that it resembles the teachings of Laozi, be capable of understanding it?

The Western Inscription (Xi ming) begins by saying that Qian is father and Kun is mother: this is what is meant by “the unity of principle.” Yet Qian and Kun are the father and mother of heaven and earth, whereas one’s parents are the father and mother of one’s own person. Is this not what is meant by “the differentiation of particular relationships”? “The people are my siblings, and other things are my companions”: speaking from the standpoint of the parents of all under heaven, this is what is meant by the unity of principle. Yet calling them “the people” does not mean that they are literally my siblings, and calling them “things” does not mean that they are literally of my own kind. Speaking from the standpoint of the parents of one’s own person, is this not what is meant by the differentiation of particular relationships? As for…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
若大舜之厎豫曾子之全歸則因事親之
誠以明事天之道皆理一而分殊也所謂
名虛理實者亦謂是耳程子之論可謂一
言蔽之矣彼謂語體而遺用平施而無稱
物者又何足以語此夫自孔孟不作理學
無傳縱橫於秦黃老於漢清談於晋辭章
於唐天下不知所謂理學者盖非一日也
至宋周張二夫子者出闡性命之旨開理
學之源而嘉惠後學至矣學者讀二書而
===
有得焉則自戒謹恐懼以脩性分之本然
存心養性以盡畏天之當然由是而造夫
仁義中正之地樂天踐形之域何有豈徒
誦說之而已哉執事幸有以教之
第叁問
倪天民
同考試官教諭胡 批此策正欲觀士子該博之學而
善答者甚不多見是篇考據精詳論議切當真策手也視
彼敷演問目者風斯下矣
punctuated:
若大舜之厎豫、曾子之全歸，則因事親之誠以明事天之道，皆理一而分殊也。所謂名虛理實者，亦謂是耳。程子之論，可謂一言蔽之矣。彼謂語體而遺用、平施而無稱物者，又何足以語此？夫自孔孟不作，理學無傳，縱橫於秦，黃老於漢，清談於晋，辭章於唐，天下不知所謂理學者，盖非一日也。至宋，周張二夫子者出，闡性命之旨，開理學之源，而嘉惠後學至矣。學者讀二書而有得焉，則自戒謹恐懼以脩性分之本然，存心養性以盡畏天之當然。由是而造夫仁義中正之地、樂天踐形之域，何有？豈徒誦說之而已哉？執事幸有以教之。

第叁問

倪天民

同考試官教諭胡批：此策正欲觀士子該博之學，而善答者甚不多見。是篇考據精詳，論議切當，真策手也。視彼敷演問目者，風斯下矣。
translation_en:
…As for the great Shun’s bringing his parents to contentment and Zengzi’s returning his body intact at death, these illustrate the Way of serving Heaven through sincerity in serving one’s parents. In both cases, principle is one, while its particular manifestations differ. This, too, is what is meant by saying that the designations are figurative but the principle is real. Master Cheng’s judgment may be said to sum it up in a single statement. How could those who claim that it discusses substance while neglecting function, or extends concern uniformly without weighing the distinctions among things, be qualified to discuss this?

Since Confucius and Mengzi ceased to arise among us, the Learning of Principle had no transmission. Diplomatic strategizing prevailed under the Qin, the teachings of Huangdi and Laozi under the Han, pure conversation under the Jin, and literary composition under the Tang. The world’s ignorance of what is called the Learning of Principle had thus lasted no short time. In the Song, the two masters Zhou and Zhang appeared, elucidating the meaning of human nature and Heaven’s mandate and opening the source of the Learning of Principle. Their beneficence toward later students was truly profound. If students read these two works and gain an understanding of them, they will, through vigilance and apprehension, cultivate what is originally inherent in their nature, and, by preserving the mind and nourishing their nature, fulfill their proper duty of revering Heaven. Proceeding thus, what difficulty would there be in reaching the ground of benevolence, righteousness, centrality, and correctness, and the realm of delighting in Heaven and fulfilling one’s bodily endowment? Surely this is not merely a matter of reciting and expounding the texts! I hope that you, sir, will favor me with your instruction.

Third Question

Ni Tianmin

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: This policy question was expressly intended to reveal the breadth of the candidates’ learning, yet very few answered it well. This essay is meticulous and thorough in its examination of evidence, and its arguments are apt and sound. Its author is truly an accomplished writer of policy essays. Those who merely elaborate on the wording of the question fall below him by comparison.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正裘批此策條答不遺考論有據且
詞氣豐贍蔚然可觀蓋優於策學者寘之高等公論
攸歸
考試官侍講彭批比辭析事皆有條理
考試官洗馬鄭批論古人成敗歷歷如見各當其
情殆非謏學
不兼天下之智不足以用天下之言不用
天下之言不足以濟天下之事蓋天下之
事無窮而一人之見有限必用天下之言
===
斯能盡天下之智而天下之事無不濟矣
古之人君臨天下之大定天下之業孰不
樂聞忠讜之論為國家助哉顧用之何如
耳然非在我者有以兼天下之智又孰能
知而用之執事發策舉古人之用言下詢
愚生何足以知此然即其取舍之由考其
成敗之迹不難知也夫六國之印遽銷於
子房一借箸之間高帝之悟速矣向使酈
生之說行則漢事不幾於去乎馬邑之誘
punctuated:
同考試官學正裘批：此策條答不遺，考論有據，且詞氣豐贍，蔚然可觀，蓋優於策學者。寘之高等，公論攸歸。
考試官侍講彭批：比辭析事，皆有條理。
考試官洗馬鄭批：論古人成敗，歷歷如見，各當其情，殆非謏學。
不兼天下之智，不足以用天下之言；不用天下之言，不足以濟天下之事。蓋天下之事無窮，而一人之見有限，必用天下之言，斯能盡天下之智，而天下之事無不濟矣。古之人君，臨天下之大，定天下之業，孰不樂聞忠讜之論，為國家助哉？顧用之何如耳。然非在我者有以兼天下之智，又孰能知而用之？執事發策，舉古人之用言下詢，愚生何足以知此？然即其取舍之由，考其成敗之迹，不難知也。夫六國之印，遽銷於子房一借箸之間，高帝之悟速矣！向使酈生之說行，則漢事不幾於去乎？馬邑之誘
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Qiu, School Director, comments: This policy essay answers every point without omission, grounding its investigations and arguments in evidence. Its language is ample and rich, making an impressive display. The writer surely excels in policy essays. Placing it in a high grade accords with the consensus of impartial judgment.
Examiner Peng, Hanlin Expositor-in-waiting, comments: Both the arrangement of language and the analysis of affairs are orderly.
Examiner Zheng, Librarian of the Heir Apparent, comments: The successes and failures of men of antiquity are discussed so vividly that they seem present before our eyes, each faithfully represented in its circumstances. This is surely no shallow learning.
Without drawing together the wisdom of all under Heaven, one cannot make use of the counsel of all under Heaven; without using that counsel, one cannot accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven. For the world's affairs are inexhaustible, while one person's understanding is limited. Only by using the counsel of all under Heaven can one fully draw upon their wisdom, so that no affair in the world remains unaccomplished. Among the rulers of antiquity who presided over the vast realm and established its great undertakings, who did not delight in hearing loyal and forthright counsel to aid the state? The question lies simply in how they used it. Yet unless a ruler himself possesses the capacity to encompass the wisdom of all under Heaven, how can he recognize and employ such counsel? In setting this policy question, you have cited the ancients' use of counsel and graciously sought my views. How could an ignorant student such as I be qualified to understand this? Yet by examining why they accepted or rejected counsel and investigating the traces of their successes and failures, it is not difficult to understand.
The seals for the Six States were promptly melted down in the brief interval when Zifang borrowed chopsticks to explain his argument: how swiftly Emperor Gao came to understand! Had Master Li's proposal been implemented, would not the Han cause have come close to being lost? The lure at Mayi …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
卒成於王恢屢廷辨之餘武帝之惑深矣
向使安國之計用則邊塵其至於屢驚乎
孫權之走操周瑜之策也若懾於長江共
之之語則何以成鼎足之勢晉武之平吴
羊祜之謀也若奪於秦涼爲憂之論則何
以成混一之功苻堅南冦苟惟陽平之聽
則五將之奔可免矣何說於躬行天罰之
面諛而自速其亡邪宋文北侵苟惟慶之
之用則元嘉之政不衰矣何動於席卷趙
===
魏之浮談而自蹙其國邪勸伐高麗李勣
之逢君可罪也師出無功適足爲太宗之
累使能受遂良之直言而不變寧有是哉
主盟吐蕃張延賞之誤國可責也刼盟見
辱亦足爲德宗之玷使先知栁渾之料敵
而不疑豈至是哉帥兵淮西裴度欲勵諸
將也一鼓而元濟成擒設其事沮於逢吉
則淮蔡之人終不知有生民之樂矣請幸
澶淵冦準欲破敵膽也一出而契丹奪氣
punctuated: 卒成於王恢屢廷辨之餘，武帝之惑深矣！向使安國之計用，則邊塵其至於屢驚乎？孫權之走操，周瑜之策也；若懾於「長江共之」之語，則何以成鼎足之勢？晉武之平吴，羊祜之謀也；若奪於「秦涼爲憂」之論，則何以成混一之功？苻堅南冦，苟惟陽平之聽，則五將之奔可免矣，何說於「躬行天罰」之面諛，而自速其亡邪？宋文北侵，苟惟慶之之用，則元嘉之政不衰矣，何動於「席卷趙魏」之浮談，而自蹙其國邪？勸伐高麗，李勣之逢君可罪也；師出無功，適足爲太宗之累。使能受遂良之直言而不變，寧有是哉？主盟吐蕃，張延賞之誤國可責也；刼盟見辱，亦足爲德宗之玷。使先知栁渾之料敵而不疑，豈至是哉？帥兵淮西，裴度欲勵諸將也；一鼓而元濟成擒。設其事沮於逢吉，則淮蔡之人終不知有生民之樂矣！請幸澶淵，冦準欲破敵膽也；一出而契丹奪氣。
translation_en:
…was finally carried through after Wang Hui’s repeated arguments at court: deep indeed was Emperor Wu’s delusion! Had Han Anguo’s plan been adopted, would the frontier have suffered repeated alarms of war? Sun Quan’s putting Cao Cao to flight was owed to Zhou Yu’s strategy. Had he been intimidated by the claim that “the Yangzi is shared by both sides,” how could he have established a position as one of three powers, like the legs of a tripod? Emperor Wu of Jin’s pacification of Wu was owed to Yang Hu’s planning. Had he been swayed by the argument that “Qin and Liang are cause for concern,” how could he have achieved unification?

When Fu Jian invaded the south, had he listened only to the Duke of Yangping, the flight of the five generals could have been avoided. Why did he delight in the to-his-face flattery that he would “personally carry out Heaven’s punishment,” thereby hastening his own destruction? When Emperor Wen of Song invaded the north, had he employed Shen Qingzhi’s counsel alone, the government of the Yuanjia reign would not have declined. Why was he moved by the empty talk of “sweeping through Zhao and Wei,” thereby bringing distress upon his own state?

In urging the attack on Gaoli, Li Ji deserves condemnation for pandering to his sovereign. The army marched out without achieving anything, serving only to burden Emperor Taizong’s reputation. Had the emperor accepted Chu Suiliang’s frank counsel and remained steadfast, could this have happened? In advocating a covenant with Tubo, Zhang Yanshang deserves blame for misleading the state. The treacherous attack at the covenant meeting and the resulting humiliation likewise stained Emperor Dezong’s reputation. Had he recognized beforehand the soundness of Liu Hun’s assessment of the enemy and entertained no doubts, could matters have come to this?

In taking command of the troops in Huaixi, Pei Du sought to spur on the generals. With one beat of the battle drums, Wu Yuanji was captured. Had Li Fengji thwarted this undertaking, the people of Huai and Cai would never have known the joys of a peaceful livelihood! In requesting that the emperor proceed to Chanyuan, Kou Zhun sought to break the enemy’s courage. With the emperor’s advance, the Khitan lost heart…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
設其議移於欽若則大梁之危將不待靖
康而然矣嗚呼一言可以興邦一言可以
喪邦其安危之機成敗之分一係於言如
此為天下國家者可不以知言為務哉雖
然有權之平然後能知物之輕重有度之
精然後能知物之長短有吾心之權度然
後能知言之是非故曰人在堂上方能辨
堂下人曲直正謂是也欲知天下之言又
當以窮天下之理為本執事以為何如
===
第四問
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批此卷五策俱能條答治教
一篇於立法用人處蓋有見乎其大者非徒區區於條
肄之末至於寫一時之弊宛然可見非諳涉之素而才
氣之充者殆不及此
同考試官教諭袁批有鋪敘委曲之雅辭有含蓄
不盡之餘意燕趙古稱多感慨之士信然
考試官侍講彭批中間議論有引其九而不竟
punctuated:
設其議移於欽若，則大梁之危將不待靖康而然矣。嗚呼！一言可以興邦，一言可以喪邦，其安危之機、成敗之分，一係於言如此，為天下國家者可不以知言為務哉？雖然，有權之平，然後能知物之輕重；有度之精，然後能知物之長短；有吾心之權度，然後能知言之是非。故曰：「人在堂上，方能辨堂下人曲直。」正謂是也。欲知天下之言，又當以窮天下之理為本。執事以為何如？

第四問
宋禮

同考試官訓導張批：此卷五策俱能條答。治教一篇，於立法用人處，蓋有見乎其大者，非徒區區於條肄之末。至於寫一時之弊，宛然可見，非諳涉之素而才氣之充者，殆不及此。

同考試官教諭袁批：有鋪敘委曲之雅辭，有含蓄不盡之餘意。燕趙古稱多感慨之士，信然。

考試官侍講彭批：中間議論，有引其九而不竟
translation_en:
… Had his proposal been deflected by Qinruo, the peril that befell Daliang would not have waited until the Jingkang era to occur. Alas! A single utterance can make a state flourish; a single utterance can bring a state to ruin. The turning point between security and peril, the distinction between success and failure, depends so entirely upon words. Can those who govern the realm fail to make discerning words their concern? Nevertheless, only with a balanced weighing scale can one determine how heavy or light things are; only with an accurate measure can one determine their length. Only with the scales and measures of our own minds can we discern right and wrong in words. Thus it is said: “Only when one stands above in the hall can one distinguish who is right and who is wrong among those below.” This is precisely what is meant. To discern the words of all under Heaven, one must moreover take the thorough investigation of the principles of all under Heaven as the foundation. What do you, honored sir, think?

Fourth Question
Song Li

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: All five policy essays in this script answer the questions point by point. The essay on governance and education shows an understanding of the essentials in its treatment of establishing laws and employing men, rather than merely dwelling on the minutiae of regulations and practice [?]. As for its portrayal of the abuses of the present day, these are made vividly apparent. Someone without long familiarity and ample literary talent could scarcely attain this level.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: There is elegant language that sets matters out fully and in all their intricacy, and there is further meaning held in reserve, not exhausted by the words. Since ancient times, Yan and Zhao have been said to produce many men of impassioned spirit. Truly this is so.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: Within the argument, there are places where he cites its nine [?] but does not finish …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
其目者豈風簷寸晷之間不能盡其說耶雖然可以
意得之矣
考試官洗馬鄭批論議切直卓有所見其識時
務者哉他日設施未必無可觀也
以馭吏之法為疎密而疎密之用常不繫
於法以用人之塗為輕重而輕重之勢常
必變其初盖天下無一法之無其弊而亦
無一塗之不足以得人雖周官六典之制
亦未必其盡宜於今而假令出於鄉舉里
===
選之目者亦豈必皆舉其職哉此愚所以
反覆於執事之問而有感焉夫為州縣者
有吏員也有監生也有進士也而議者以
為莫賢於進士任學校者或自鄉貢除或
自明經薦或由監學選而議者以為莫弊
於薦舉夫進士之科
朝廷所留意士夫所傾心其選授之初上下
嘗屬目焉今進士之選盛行矣而執事所
謂漸輕之勢已有見於今者愚固不敢謂
punctuated:
其目者，豈風簷寸晷之間不能盡其說耶？雖然，可以意得之矣。
考試官洗馬鄭批：論議切直，卓有所見，其識時務者哉！他日設施，未必無可觀也。
以馭吏之法為疎密，而疎密之用常不繫於法；以用人之塗為輕重，而輕重之勢常必變其初。盖天下無一法之無其弊，而亦無一塗之不足以得人。雖周官六典之制，亦未必其盡宜於今；而假令出於鄉舉里選之目者，亦豈必皆舉其職哉？此愚所以反覆於執事之問而有感焉。夫為州縣者，有吏員也，有監生也，有進士也，而議者以為莫賢於進士。任學校者，或自鄉貢除，或自明經薦，或由監學選，而議者以為莫弊於薦舉。夫進士之科，朝廷所留意，士夫所傾心，其選授之初，上下嘗屬目焉。今進士之選盛行矣，而執事所謂漸輕之勢，已有見於今者，愚固不敢謂
translation_en:
…their particulars. Could it be that, beneath the wind-swept eaves and in the brief time available, he could not fully explain his argument? [?] Even so, his meaning can be grasped.
Examiner Zheng, Librarian of the Heir Apparent, comments: His arguments are pertinent and forthright, and display outstanding insight. Surely he understands the affairs of the time! What he puts into practice in the future may well be worth observing.
Methods of controlling functionaries are deemed lax or strict, yet their laxity or strictness in practice often does not depend on the regulations themselves. Routes into official service are deemed prestigious or insignificant, yet their relative standing invariably changes from what it was at the outset. No method in the world is without its abuses, and no route is incapable of yielding capable men. Even the system of the six codes in the Offices of Zhou would not necessarily be entirely suitable today; and even those recruited through local recommendation and selection would not necessarily all discharge their duties adequately. This is why I have pondered your question repeatedly and been moved to reflect upon it.
Those who administer prefectures and counties include clerks, students of the Imperial University, and metropolitan graduates (jinshi); yet commentators hold that none are worthier than the metropolitan graduates. Those appointed to schools may receive appointments as provincial tribute candidates, be recommended for mastery of the Classics, or be selected from the Imperial University; yet commentators hold that no route is more beset by abuses than recommendation.
As for the metropolitan graduate examination, the court gives it close attention, and scholars and officials set their hearts upon it. When its graduates first undergo selection and appointment, those above and below alike watch closely. Today, the selection of metropolitan graduates is widely practised; yet the tendency toward diminishing prestige of which you speak can already be seen. I certainly would not dare to say …

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
無也薦舉之人夤緣以求知僥倖以苟得
其末流之壞士類嘗扼腕焉今薦舉之門
已杜矣而執事所謂不職之弊未有以賢
於彼者愚亦不敢謂無也至於責治於州
縣者其法不密於近時乎鋤芸櫛治無間
於歳年升華躋要改觀於轉盼可謂急於
幽明之黜陟矣加意於學校者其法不因
仍於昔日乎責成之效惟在於貢舉考功
之課不及以吏事可謂專於師儒之責任
===
矣雖然知鮮印之不旋踵也則京兆之五
日必有以償其未愜之心而拱辰之一網
尚幸其或吞舟之漏知召檄之不終朝也
則操轡策於上者必闊略於惠文之治而
屏聲氣於下者常鳥息於吞鯢之威夫豈
勸懲之本意哉若夫人材之産也有謂為
孝秀之淵有謂為夷荒之壤故或倚席不
講而功籍已盈或課授不輟而殿負自若
至其學問之察也外而風憲有比年之試
punctuated:
無也。薦舉之人，夤緣以求知，僥倖以苟得，其末流之壞，士類嘗扼腕焉。今薦舉之門已杜矣，而執事所謂不職之弊，未有以賢於彼者，愚亦不敢謂無也。至於責治於州縣者，其法不密於近時乎？鋤芸櫛治，無間於歳年；升華躋要，改觀於轉盼，可謂急於幽明之黜陟矣。加意於學校者，其法不因仍於昔日乎？責成之效，惟在於貢舉；考功之課，不及以吏事，可謂專於師儒之責任矣。
雖然，知鮮印之不旋踵也，則京兆之五日，必有以償其未愜之心，而拱辰之一網，尚幸其或吞舟之漏。知召檄之不終朝也，則操轡策於上者，必闊略於惠文之治，而屏聲氣於下者，常鳥息於吞鯢之威。夫豈勸懲之本意哉？
若夫人材之産也，有謂為孝秀之淵，有謂為夷荒之壤，故或倚席不講而功籍已盈，或課授不輟而殿負自若。至其學問之察也，外而風憲有比年之試。
translation_en:
…that there are none. Those seeking office through recommendation cultivated connections to gain recognition and relied on luck to obtain appointments by any means. Scholars have long wrung their hands over the abuses into which this practice ultimately degenerated. Now the avenue of recommendation has been closed; yet the failings in the discharge of office of which you speak are no better than those under that system. I, too, would not venture to deny that such failings exist. As for requiring good administration from prefectures and counties, have the regulations ever been more stringent than in recent times? Officials are weeded out and combed through without waiting for years to pass; promotion to prestigious and important posts transforms their prospects in the blink of an eye. One may indeed say that demotion of the unworthy and advancement of the worthy are pursued urgently. As for the special attention given to schools, do the regulations not continue the practices of former days? The results demanded lie solely in presenting candidates for the examinations; evaluations of merit do not extend to administrative business. One may indeed say that their responsibilities are concentrated on their role as scholarly teachers.
Nevertheless, knowing that the matter of their seals will follow immediately [?], they will surely use their “five days as Metropolitan Governor” to satisfy their unfulfilled desires, still hoping that Gongchen’s single cast of the net will leave a gap through which even a boat-swallowing fish can escape. Knowing that a summons may arrive before the morning is over, those above who hold the reins and whip inevitably become lax in enforcing the law, while those below, suppressing their voices and holding their breath, cower like birds before the might of a devouring whale [?]. Can this possibly be the original intention of encouragement and punishment?
As for the production of talented men, some places are called deep pools of filial and outstanding scholars, while others are called uncivilized wastelands. Thus some teachers leave their teaching mats propped aside and give no lectures, yet their records of merit are already full; others teach without respite, yet remain burdened with poor assessments. As for examining their learning, outside the capital the censorial authorities conduct annual tests…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
内而銓曹較一日之長故浮華之小技立
見而真實之隱德難知文藝之一節可師
而範模之大本無係又豈建立之初心哉
凡此者有識之所同病而執事之所以不
能忘言也歟愚竊以為馭吏之法備矣而
執法以馭吏者有其要用人之塗嚴矣而
探本以作人者有所先知要之所在則知
救弊補偏雖不可無法而所以得失之相
乗利病之相半者非法之罪也知本之所
===
先則知辨材論德雖不能以不異而所以
輕重殊勢後先殊效者非所由以進之塗
之罪也方今
聖天子明道致法運之於上二三大臣揆道守
法賛之於下鳴琴製錦之賢棟梁榱桷之
頌固當見之一得獻愚多見其贅爾
第五問
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批場中多爲夷狄一策所窘簡
punctuated:
内而銓曹較一日之長，故浮華之小技立見，而真實之隱德難知；文藝之一節可師，而範模之大本無係，又豈建立之初心哉？凡此者，有識之所同病，而執事之所以不能忘言也歟？愚竊以為，馭吏之法備矣，而執法以馭吏者有其要；用人之塗嚴矣，而探本以作人者有所先。知要之所在，則知救弊補偏，雖不可無法，而所以得失之相乗、利病之相半者，非法之罪也。知本之所先，則知辨材論德，雖不能以不異，而所以輕重殊勢、後先殊效者，非所由以進之塗之罪也。方今聖天子明道致法，運之於上；二三大臣揆道守法，賛之於下。鳴琴製錦之賢、棟梁榱桷之頌，固當見之。一得獻愚，多見其贅爾。
第五問
宋禮
同考試官訓導張批：場中多爲夷狄一策所窘，簡
translation_en:
…while within the central government, the personnel authorities compare accomplishments displayed on a single day. Thus superficial cleverness is immediately apparent, while genuine but unassuming virtue is difficult to discern. Literary accomplishment, merely one aspect, can serve as a standard, while the fundamental basis of exemplary conduct has no bearing. How could this have been the original intention in establishing these arrangements?
These are failings that all discerning people deplore, and surely they explain why you, sir, cannot refrain from addressing the matter. In my humble opinion, the laws for controlling officials are comprehensive, but those who enforce them must grasp what is essential. The avenues for employing men are rigorously regulated, but those who seek the foundations of cultivating talent must recognize what comes first. Once we understand where the essentials lie, we understand that, although laws are indispensable for remedying abuses and correcting imbalances, the fact that gains and losses overtake one another, and benefits and harms occur in equal measure, is not the fault of the laws. Once we understand what must come first at the foundation, we understand that, although assessments of ability and virtue cannot avoid distinctions, the disparities in the weight accorded to men and the different results achieved sooner or later are not the fault of the avenues through which they advance.
Today the sagely Son of Heaven elucidates the Way and brings the laws into effect, directing their operation above; his high ministers measure their actions against the Way and uphold the laws, assisting him below. We should surely witness worthy administrators who govern by playing the zither and weaving brocade, and hear praise of men who serve as the pillars, beams, and rafters of the state. In offering this single humble insight, I fear I have mostly said what is superfluous.
Fifth Question
Song Li
