title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
有答者亦不能悉此篇直以漢事論辨亹亹不已波瀾
疊出筆力老健讀之能不令人起敬
同考試官教諭袁批策場羣作類皆疎略於夷
狄一問尤不知所謂纏繞紛拏無以自解此篇直寫其胸
中所欲言而事意完足無復闕遺至其歸宿亦寓深
意非淺學謭聞之士必矣
考試官侍講彭批反覆漢事甚熟而文亦粲然
考試官洗馬鄭批詞氣沛然不為問目所制能
文之士也場中諸子無出其右者矣
===
畜夷狄猶禽獸然畫之於山澤不可也闢
撤垣毀而無以備之不可也畏其噬搏而
飲食之以冀其免已雖五尺之童知其不
可矣是故至則驅之馴則豢之而已漢之
事匈奴曠世歷年詘信異變彊弱相反然
大率嚴尤之所謂下策也高帝脫平城之
困約結和親文帝通關市之使增厚賂遺
然而寇盜不衰嫚倨彌甚虜騎至於同中
烽火通於甘泉是以文帝躬擐甲之勞肄
punctuated:
有答者，亦不能悉。此篇直以漢事論辨，亹亹不已，波瀾疊出，筆力老健，讀之能不令人起敬？

同考試官教諭袁批：策場羣作，類皆疎略，於夷狄一問，尤不知所謂，纏繞紛拏，無以自解。此篇直寫其胸中所欲言，而事意完足，無復闕遺。至其歸宿，亦寓深意，非淺學謭聞之士必矣。

考試官侍講彭批：反覆漢事甚熟，而文亦粲然。

考試官洗馬鄭批：詞氣沛然，不為問目所制，能文之士也。場中諸子，無出其右者矣。

畜夷狄，猶禽獸然。畫之於山澤，不可也；闢撤垣毀，而無以備之，不可也；畏其噬搏，而飲食之，以冀其免已，雖五尺之童，知其不可矣。是故至則驅之，馴則豢之而已。漢之事匈奴，曠世歷年，詘信異變，彊弱相反，然大率嚴尤之所謂下策也。高帝脫平城之困，約結和親；文帝通關市之使，增厚賂遺。然而寇盜不衰，嫚倨彌甚，虜騎至於同中，烽火通於甘泉。是以文帝躬擐甲之勞，肄
translation_en:
…Those who did answer could not cover it fully. This essay proceeds directly through discussion and argument based on Han affairs, developing its case tirelessly, with wave upon wave of fresh turns. Its writing is mature and vigorous: how could reading it fail to inspire respect?

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: The essays in the policy examination were generally cursory. On the question concerning the barbarians in particular, the candidates scarcely knew what they were saying, becoming entangled in confused arguments from which they could not extricate themselves. This essay directly expresses what its author wishes to say; its facts and ideas are complete, with nothing omitted. Its conclusion also contains profound meaning. Certainly its author is no man of shallow learning and scant knowledge.

Comment by Examiner Peng, Expositor: His sustained examination of Han affairs shows considerable familiarity with them, and his prose is also brilliant.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Library Aide: His language and force of expression flow abundantly, unconstrained by the wording of the question. He is an accomplished writer. None of the other candidates surpasses him.

Managing the barbarians is like keeping birds and beasts. It will not do to confine them within designated mountains and marshes; nor will it do to tear down the enclosing walls [?] and have no means of guarding against them. To fear their biting and striking, and therefore feed them in hopes that they will spare oneself—even a child five feet tall knows that this will not do. Thus, when they come, drive them off; when they are tame, nourish them: that is all. The Han dynasty’s dealings with the Xiongnu extended across generations and years. Submission and assertion varied, and relative strength and weakness were reversed; yet, on the whole, its approach was what Yan You called the inferior strategy. Emperor Gao, after escaping the siege at Pingcheng, concluded a treaty of peace through marriage. Emperor Wen sent envoys to open frontier markets and increased the generous gifts bestowed upon them. Yet their raids did not abate, and their arrogance grew ever worse. Enemy cavalry reached Tongzhong [?], and beacon alarms extended to Ganquan. Consequently, Emperor Wen personally endured the toil of donning armor and practiced…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
上林之射當食思賢拊髀興喟是豈和好
之足恃哉武帝選將練兵深入窮追使衛
青霍去病之徒先後出入搴旗大漠之北
登臨瀚海之陰然而中國罷耗士馬物故
報復相當桀驁自若亦豈威武之足恃哉
孝宣承先世奮擊之威值匈奴百年之運
為權時施宜之計然後羈縻外属三世賓
庭盖高文武昭之前其盛強愁然以相抗
宣元成哀之後其削弱萎然而自屈與漢
===
盛衰略相終始至論漢興以来君臣之間
謀議所持計策所出則當時之得失而後
世之明效也雖其成敗亦有出於偶然而
圖為或不叶於道義然大略有可見矣劉
敬知冒頓非可以仁義說而欲結以婚姻
之好賈誼憤首足之倒懸而欲餌以金絮
采繒之奉前後相違卑陋無取若夫乘邊
之士至數十萬人固已羅絡山川而包嚢險
翳其為防可謂周矣然疲於東西之奔命無
punctuated:
上林之射，當食思賢，拊髀興喟，是豈和好之足恃哉？武帝選將練兵，深入窮追，使衛青、霍去病之徒先後出入，搴旗大漠之北，登臨瀚海之陰。然而中國罷耗，士馬物故，報復相當，桀驁自若，亦豈威武之足恃哉？孝宣承先世奮擊之威，值匈奴百年之運，為權時施宜之計，然後羈縻外属，三世賓庭。盖高、文、武、昭之前，其盛強愁然以相抗；宣、元、成、哀之後，其削弱萎然而自屈，與漢盛衰略相終始。
至論漢興以来，君臣之間謀議所持、計策所出，則當時之得失，而後世之明效也。雖其成敗亦有出於偶然，而圖為或不叶於道義，然大略有可見矣。劉敬知冒頓非可以仁義說，而欲結以婚姻之好；賈誼憤首足之倒懸，而欲餌以金絮采繒之奉。前後相違，卑陋無取。若夫乘邊之士至數十萬人，固已羅絡山川，而包嚢險翳，其為防可謂周矣。然疲於東西之奔命，無
translation_en:
…archery in Shanglin Park; at his meals he thought of worthy men, slapped his thigh, and sighed. How could peaceful friendship possibly be relied upon? Emperor Wu selected generals and trained troops, penetrating deep into enemy territory and pursuing them to the utmost. He sent men such as Wei Qing and Huo Qubing on successive campaigns to seize banners north of the great desert and advance to the northern reaches of the Hanhai. Yet the Central States were exhausted and depleted, soldiers and horses perished, and retaliation met retaliation in equal measure, while the enemy remained as defiant as ever. How, then, could military might be relied upon either? Emperor Xiaoxuan inherited the prestige of his predecessors’ vigorous attacks and encountered a turning point in the Xiongnu’s century-long fortunes. He devised measures suited to the moment and its circumstances; only then were they held in loose external allegiance, attending the imperial court as guests for three generations. In the earlier period, under Emperors Gao, Wen, Wu, and Zhao, their strength was at its height, and they stood against the Han [?]; in the later period, under Emperors Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, and Ai, their power declined, and they weakened and submitted of their own accord. Their rise and decline broadly coincided in timing with those of the Han.
As for the positions maintained in deliberation between rulers and ministers, and the strategies they devised from the founding of the Han onward, these constituted successes and failures at the time and furnished clear evidence of their effects for later generations. Although success or failure sometimes arose by chance, and their designs and actions did not always accord with the Way and righteousness, their general outlines remain discernible. Liu Jing knew that Modu could not be persuaded through benevolence and righteousness, yet wished to bind him through a marriage alliance. Jia Yi was indignant at the inversion of head and feet, yet wished to entice the Xiongnu with offerings of gold, silk floss, and colored silks. Their proposals contradicted their premises; they were base and shallow, with nothing to commend them. As for the troops guarding the frontier, numbering several hundred thousand, they already formed a network across mountains and rivers and encompassed rugged and concealed terrain. Their defensive arrangements could indeed be called comprehensive. Yet they were exhausted by rushing east and west to answer emergencies, without…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
救吏民之侵掠安在其為防也西域之通至
三十餘國謂將斷其右臂而離其外交其為
謀可謂得矣然首鼠陰持於兩屬反覆常
伺於強弱安在其為謀也至於望之建敵
國不臣之議而荀悅有僭度失序之譏誠
以彼之自居自後倔彊於域中固不必彊而臣
之而来享来王使命之加遺亦不當抗而
尊之也故以愚論斷之衛青霍去病之舉
猶獸而欲盡之於山澤者也劉敬賈誼之
===
策畏其噬搏而飲食之者也其謂選武略
之臣修障隧之具厲長戟勁弩之械則知
撤關毀垣之不可而欲備之者也得陵廣
之材勇不若用充國之善勝賞甘陳之竒
節不若推魏尚之善守此又欲備之者之
所宜知也善乎班孟堅之言之也以為與
結約則耗費而見欺就征伐則勞師而招
寇是以外而不內疎而不戚其来也懲而
禦之其去也備而守之其靡服也隨宜而
punctuated: 救吏民之侵掠，安在其為防也？西域之通至三十餘國，謂將斷其右臂而離其外交，其為謀可謂得矣。然首鼠陰持於兩屬，反覆常伺於強弱，安在其為謀也？至於望之建敵國不臣之議，而荀悅有僭度失序之譏，誠以彼之自居自後，倔彊於域中，固不必彊而臣之；而来享来王，使命之加遺，亦不當抗而尊之也。故以愚論斷之，衛青、霍去病之舉，猶獸而欲盡之於山澤者也；劉敬、賈誼之策，畏其噬搏而飲食之者也。其謂選武略之臣，修障隧之具，厲長戟勁弩之械，則知撤關毀垣之不可而欲備之者也。得陵、廣之材勇，不若用充國之善勝；賞甘、陳之竒節，不若推魏尚之善守。此又欲備之者之所宜知也。善乎班孟堅之言之也！以為與結約則耗費而見欺，就征伐則勞師而招寇。是以外而不內，疎而不戚。其来也，懲而禦之；其去也，備而守之；其靡服也，隨宜而
translation_en:
…protect officials and commoners from raids and plunder: wherein lay its effectiveness as a defense? Relations were opened with more than thirty states in the Western Regions, ostensibly to sever the enemy’s right arm and break its foreign ties. This might be called a sound strategy. Yet those states wavered, secretly maintaining allegiance to both sides, repeatedly shifting their position as they watched which side was stronger or weaker. Wherein lay its effectiveness as a strategy? As for Xiao Wangzhi’s proposal to treat them as a peer state rather than as subjects, Xun Yue criticized it as overstepping proper bounds and disrupting the prescribed order. Indeed, since they kept to themselves and held back [?], remaining defiant within their own territory, there was certainly no need to force them into subjection. Yet when they came to present offerings and acknowledge the sovereign, and envoys were dispatched with gifts, neither should they have been elevated and honored as equals.

Thus, in my humble judgment, the campaigns of Wei Qing and Huo Qubing were like treating them as beasts and seeking to exterminate them in the mountains and marshes. The plans of Liu Jing and Jia Yi were those of men who, fearing the beasts’ bites and attacks, gave them food and drink. Those who advocated selecting ministers skilled in military strategy, putting frontier fortifications and beacon installations in order, and readying long halberds and powerful crossbows understood that dismantling the passes and demolishing the walls was unacceptable, and sought to prepare against them. Securing the talent and courage of Li Ling and Li Guang was less valuable than employing Zhao Chongguo’s skill in achieving victory; rewarding the exceptional integrity of Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang was less valuable than promoting Wei Shang’s skill in defense. This, too, is something those seeking to prepare against them ought to understand.

How well Ban Mengjian expressed it! He held that making treaties with them exhausted resources and invited deception, while undertaking punitive campaigns wearied the army and provoked incursions. Therefore, they were to be kept outside rather than brought within, held at a distance rather than treated as kin. When they came, they were to be punished and repelled; when they withdrew, preparations were to be made and defenses maintained; when they submitted, they were to be dealt with as circumstances required, and…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
接之使在我有可恃之勢而在彼無得乗
之機亦庶乎其有見焉雖然書曰無怠無
荒四夷来王又曰惇德允元蠻夷率服漢
之諸臣豈足以與此
punctuated: 接之，使在我有可恃之勢，而在彼無得乗之機，亦庶乎其有見焉。雖然，《書》曰：「無怠無荒，四夷来王。」又曰：「惇德允元，蠻夷率服。」漢之諸臣，豈足以與此？
translation_en: …receive them, so that we possess a position on which we can rely, while they have no opportunity to exploit. This, too, may be considered an insightful view. Nevertheless, the Book of Documents says: “Be neither negligent nor idle, and the peoples of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.” It also says: “Honor the virtuous and trust the good, and the Man and Yi peoples will all submit.” How could the ministers of the Han dynasty possibly measure up to this?

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
順天府鄉試錄後序
上命臣環臣教來考順天鄉試既
畢事臣教謹敘論其意於錄
後夫取人之不廢言也舊矣
書曰敷奏以言又曰詢事考
言文則言之成章而著者也
自漢以來充賦有司而登其
===
說於王庭者可考見已至于
今莫之有改蓋言之不可廢
也如此然以唐虞明良之盛
猶致意於靜庸之際而後世
之品藻文藝差次事功亦每
岐而論之則又以見言之難
恃已
punctuated:
順天府鄉試錄後序

上命臣環、臣教來考順天鄉試。既畢事，臣教謹敘論其意於錄後。夫取人之不廢言也，舊矣。《書》曰：「敷奏以言。」又曰：「詢事考言。」文則言之成章而著者也。自漢以來，充賦有司而登其說於王庭者，可考見已。至于今，莫之有改，蓋言之不可廢也如此。然以唐虞明良之盛，猶致意於靜庸之際，而後世之品藻文藝、差次事功，亦每岐而論之，則又以見言之難恃已。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

His Majesty commanded your servants Huan and Jiao to come and serve as Examiners for the Shuntian Provincial Examination. Now that our duties are completed, I, your servant Jiao, respectfully set forth and discuss the purpose of this undertaking at the end of the record. The practice of taking account of a person's words when selecting men for office is ancient. The Book of Documents says, “Have them present their statements in words.” It also says, “Inquire into their deeds and examine their words.” Written compositions are words arranged into coherent form and set down in writing. Since the Han, instances of men being presented as candidates by the responsible authorities and submitting their statements at the royal court can be traced in the records. Down to the present, this practice has remained unchanged: such is the indispensability of words. Yet even amid the flourishing rule of enlightened sovereigns and worthy ministers under Tang and Yu, attention was still paid to the discrepancy between fine words and contrary conduct. In later ages, too, appraising literary accomplishment and ranking achievements in affairs were often discussed separately. This further shows how difficult it is to rely upon words.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
陛下在位今十有三年益明習
國家事方勵精求人以振庶功
小大之臣奔走恐懼仰承
威命而臣猥以文字充乏適當
任使大懼無以稱塞
明詔蓋鄉舉取士公卿輔相且
將階級焉事至重也其敢不
===
共況天府之士畿內之秀四
方游學之英宜有卓異以備
異時登簡顧臣之淺昧何足
以知之雖然畢力於文辭論
議之間而精察舉之任此臣
事力所及也若夫恢宏碩大
之器剛方敦厚之質疏通敏
punctuated: 陛下在位今十有三年，益明習國家事，方勵精求人，以振庶功。小大之臣奔走恐懼，仰承威命，而臣猥以文字充乏，適當任使，大懼無以稱塞明詔。蓋鄉舉取士，公卿輔相且將階級焉，事至重也，其敢不共？況天府之士，畿內之秀，四方游學之英，宜有卓異，以備異時登簡。顧臣之淺昧，何足以知之？雖然，畢力於文辭論議之間，而精察舉之任，此臣事力所及也。若夫恢宏碩大之器，剛方敦厚之質，疏通敏
translation_en: Your Majesty has now occupied the throne for thirteen years and has become ever more thoroughly versed in the affairs of state. You are exerting yourself to seek worthy men and advance the many undertakings of government. Your servants, great and small, hasten about their duties in reverent apprehension, receiving Your Majesty’s august commands. Yet I, your unworthy servant, have been called upon to fill a vacancy on the strength of my literary abilities. Entrusted with this assignment, I greatly fear that I lack the means to fulfill your enlightened edict. For the selection of men through the Provincial Examination provides the steps by which future dukes, ministers, and chief councilors will rise. This is a matter of the utmost gravity: how could I dare be anything but reverent? Moreover, among the scholars of the metropolitan prefecture—the outstanding men of the capital region and the gifted students who have traveled here from every quarter—there should be men of exceptional distinction, ready for selection and advancement in years to come. But with my shallow understanding, how could I adequately recognize them? Nevertheless, to devote all my efforts to examining their literary expression and argument, and to exercise discrimination in the responsibility of assessing and recommending them: this lies within the reach of my duties and abilities. As for men of broad and ample capacity, of upright and steadfast, sincere and generous character, of penetrating understanding and keen…

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
text:
達之才由是有得焉此則臣
之志也
翰林院侍講彭教謹序
punctuated:
達之才，由是有得焉，此則臣之志也。
翰林院侍講彭教謹序。
translation_en:
…talents of penetrating understanding: that such men may be found through this process is your servant’s aspiration.
Peng Jiao, Expositor of the Hanlin Academy, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
成化十三年順天府鄉試錄
